We're looking for a driven, high-energy Inside Sales Rep/Appointment Setter to join our team. Your primary mission is to generate qualified appointments from inbound leads, call-ins, aged leads, rehash opportunities, and proactive follow-up activity. This is a phone-first role built for someone who loves the chase, can handle objections without flinching, and knows how to turn a conversation into a committed appointment. You'll work closely with our outside sales team, feeding them high-quality, fully qualified demos, and your success is measured — and rewarded — by the results you drive.

We serve all three U.S. time zones, so schedules include options such as Monday–Friday, Tuesday–Saturday, or Wednesday–Sunday (40 hours/week, non-exempt), and weekend availability is mandatory. You'll need a quiet, distraction-free home workspace and will provide your own computer to start (as a growing company, we're not able to promise reimbursement on a set timeline, though it's something we hope to offer down the road).

This is a remote position open only to applicants located within the State of Colorado

What You'll Do

  • Work inbound leads, call-ins, aged leads, and rehash campaigns every day
  • Convert web form submissions, phone inquiries, and follow-up opportunities into qualified, confirmed appointments
  • Execute fast speed-to-lead — responding to new leads immediately and consistently
  • Handle objections with confidence and bring conversations back on track
  • Maintain clean CRM records and disciplined follow-up on every open opportunity
  • Hit daily activity expectations: dials, appointments set, talk time, and sit-rate goals
  • Collaborate with the sales team to ensure smooth handoffs and high show rates
  • Participate in ongoing coaching, call review, and process improvement

What You Bring

Required:

  • 1+ year of phone sales, appointment setting, lead generation, or call center experience preferred

  • Strong objection handling — you know how to redirect without going off-script
  • Money motivation — you want your income tied to what you produce

Preferred:

  • Experience with inbound leads, aged leads, and rehash campaigns
  • Proven track record hitting activity and conversion targets

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Fast ramp — training wheels come off by the end of week two

  • Real upside — hit your numbers and you'll feel it in your paycheck
  • Direct feedback — we coach, we don't micromanage, but we do hold the bar high

jobs.description:
Datavant is the data collaboration platform trusted for healthcare. Guided by our mission to make the world’s health data secure, accessible and actionable, we provide critical data solutions for organizations across the healthcare ecosystem - including providers, health plans, researchers, and life sciences companies. From fulfilling a single patient’s request for their medical records to powering the AI revolution in healthcare, Datavanters are building the future of how data is connected and used to improve health.

By joining Datavant today, you’re stepping onto a driven and highly collaborative team that is passionate about creating transformative change in healthcare.

What We’re Looking For

The Training Specialist owns the training that prepares our customer service associates and leaders to succeed. In this role, you will identify where teams need to build skills, decide what training will close those gaps, design and deliver that training, and determine when associates are ready to support customers on their own.

You will work closely with Customer Service leaders, Quality, Process Improvement, Workforce Management, Product, and other partners to keep training current as products and processes change. You will also measure whether training is working by tracking its impact on readiness, quality, productivity, and customer experience. This role calls for strong facilitation skills, sound independent judgment, reliable follow-through, and the ability to make complicated information easy to understand.

What You Will Do

Training Needs Analysis and Program Planning

  • Analyze quality results, customer feedback, performance data, process changes, and leader input to identify skill and knowledge gaps across customer service teams.
  • Decide which training solutions are needed to close identified gaps, such as new courses, refreshers, job aids, or targeted coaching, and recommend priorities to Customer Service leadership.
  • Advise leaders and cross-functional partners on training strategy and timing for product releases, system changes, and process updates.
  • Set learning objectives and success measures for each training program.

Curriculum Design and Development

  • Design new hire and ongoing training programs, including deciding on content, sequence, delivery method (classroom, virtual, or blended), practice activities, and assessment approach.
  • Turn operating procedures, system changes, and business requirements into clear learning objectives and practical, hands-on training activities.
  • Create and maintain facilitator guides, learner materials, job aids, practice exercises, and assessments that meet company standards.
  • Partner with subject matter experts and process owners to confirm content accuracy before release and decide when materials should be revised or retired.

Facilitation and Coaching

  • Lead instructor-led and virtual new hire training for customer service associates on products, systems, policies, and customer workflows.
  • Delivering ongoing skill development, product release, process change, and refresher training for frontline associates and people leaders.
  • Adjust delivery in real time based on learner needs, pace, and understanding.
  • Provide structured coaching during training and the transition to live customer work, partnering with supervisors to create development plans for employees who need extra support.
  • Stay current on the systems and workflows being taught through calibration sessions, process reviews, and regular hands-on practice.

Readiness Assessment and Program Evaluation

  • Evaluate learner knowledge and skills through observation, practice scenarios, knowledge checks, and readiness assessments.
  • Determine whether each learner meets readiness standards and recommend to leaders whether the associate should move into production, receive extended training, or receive additional support.
  • Analyze training results and feedback from learners and stakeholders to judge program effectiveness, and recommend changes to content, delivery, and follow-up reinforcement.

Program Administration

Coordinate training schedules, rosters, system access, training environments, and materials with Workforce Management and leaders.

  • Maintain accurate training records and reports in the learning management system and other approved tools.
  • Protect confidential, proprietary, and health information by following all privacy, security, and records handling requirements.
  • Support other training, knowledge management, and operational readiness priorities as assigned.

What You Need to Succeed

Minimum Qualifications

  • 4+ years of training experience.
  • Experience designing and delivering instructor-led and virtual training.
  • Strong facilitation, coaching, and communication skills.
  • Experience developing training materials, job aids, and assessments.
  • Ability to analyze performance gaps and evaluate learner readiness.
  • Strong organizational and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Customer service or contact-center training experience.
  • Healthcare or other regulated-industry experience.
  • Experience with LMS and virtual learning platforms.
  • Experience supporting product, system, or process changes.
  • Experience facilitating and managing training programs for geographically distributed or remote teams.
  • L&D instructional design or related experience.

jobs.description:
The Manager, Customer Care is the accountable operational leader for California Closets’ centralized Customer Care function. This hands-on role leads the internal Central Support team and owns the operational relationship with the First Contact Call Center vendor, TLS. The Manager is responsible for day-to-day service performance, departmental KPIs, quality, lead-management operations, customer escalations, market support, operational risk, and continuous improvement.

The role maintains a strong working knowledge of contact-center workforce management principles to evaluate TLS forecasts, staffing and capacity recommendations, identify performance risks, and hold the vendor accountable for corrective action.

The Manager also serves as the business and operational owner for Customer Care Salesforce campaigns and lead-routing requirements. The role defines and validates operational requirements, coordinates setup and testing with appropriate technical partners, monitors routing performance, and remains accountable for business impact, escalation, communication and validation when issues occur.

Success requires equal strength in people leadership and operational management. This individual is expected to operate with minimal day-to-day direction, use data to identify root causes and recommendations, and drive issues through resolution even when execution requires support from TLS, Salesforce/Technology resources, Service Delivery or other business partners.

Pay - $95K or more depending on experience

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Independently lead the day-to-day operation of the Central Support team, establishing priorities and ensuring business goals, service expectations and customer experience standards are met.
  • Directly manage Customer Liaisons, Specialists and Team Leads responsible for consultation scheduling, technical support and back-office administration across supported communication channels.
  • Own departmental performance and KPIs, including lead-management metrics, complaint and feedback handling, quality, team NPS and applicable contact-center service metrics; identify root causes and establish measurable corrective actions when results fall below expectations.
  • Serve as the primary operational point of contact for markets supported by Customer Care. Prepare performance reporting, analyze trends, conduct regular business reviews and translate findings into clear recommendations, owners and follow-up actions.
  • Lead hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, payroll administration, schedules and rosters for the internal Central Support team; build a culture of accountability, customer focus and continuous improvement.
  • Manage the Quality Assurance program and provide guidance to the Quality Assurance Team Lead. Audit and monitor customer interactions, identify trends and ensure coaching and corrective actions are completed for internal and external teams.
  • Lead customer escalations with sound judgment, customer focus and solution-oriented decision making.
  • Partner with Service Delivery to develop and maintain departmental SOPs, training and operational documentation, and ensure consistent execution across Central Support and applicable vendor teams.
  • Communicate recurring issues, trends, risks and key learnings to leadership and internal partners, including Marketing, Product, Service Delivery and Technology, and drive follow-through on agreed actions.
  • Perform other duties aligned to the scope and accountability of the role.

Vendor Performance

  • Own the day-to-day operational relationship with TLS, including service performance, quality, lead-management expectations, issue escalation, action-plan follow-through and adherence to agreed operating standards.
  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of workforce-management principles, including forecasting, capacity planning, staffing, scheduling and intraday management, sufficient to evaluate vendor recommendations and performance.
  • Review and challenge TLS forecasts, staffing and capacity plans; understand forecast-versus-actual performance and escalate material staffing or service-level risks.
  • Hold TLS accountable for investigating performance gaps, presenting recovery plans and demonstrating sustained improvement. Ensure operational issues remain actively managed through resolution rather than relying solely on ticket creation or vendor escalation.
  • Use vendor performance, quality and operational data to identify trends and recommend changes to processes, training, staffing assumptions or service-delivery practices.

Salesforce Campaign & Lead Routing Operations

  • Own the business and operational requirements for Customer Care lead management and customer service campaigns, queues and lead-routing processes.
  • Guide and coordinate campaign setup, routing changes, testing, launch readiness and post-launch validation with appropriate Salesforce/Technology partners and TLS.
  • Maintain current documentation of campaign purpose, routing logic, operational dependencies, ownership and escalation paths.
  • Monitor lead-routing and campaign performance for exceptions, failures or unintended outcomes that may affect customer response, lead handling or market performance.
  • When campaign or routing issues occur, assess business impact, coordinate containment or interim procedures, engage the appropriate technical owner, communicate status to stakeholders, and validate operational recovery before closure.
  • Provide operational input into Salesforce enhancements and process changes that affect Customer Care, lead management, routing or call-center workflows.

Operational Risk & Incident Management

  • Identify and escalate material operational risks based on customer, lead, service, revenue or brand impact, developing and following established escalation protocols.
  • Own business-side incident coordination through containment, technical or vendor escalation, operational workaround, validation and closure.
  • Communicate issue scope, business impact, current status, ownership, interim actions and next steps to affected stakeholders and leadership.
  • Lead or participate in post-incident reviews for material or recurring issues and ensure preventive actions, documentation, controls, testing or training are implemented.
  • 7+ years of progressive customer care or contact-center experience, including demonstrated responsibility for contact-center operations and people leadership.
  • Demonstrated experience managing outsourced contact-center or BPO relationships and holding partners accountable for service, quality and operational performance.
  • Strong understanding of contact-center workforce-management principles and ability to evaluate forecasts, staffing plans, capacity recommendations and service-level performance; direct ownership of vendor agent scheduling is not required.
  • Experience working with Salesforce or a comparable CRM in a lead-management, campaign, queue or routing environment. Ability to define business requirements, validate operational outcomes and partner effectively with technical resources.
  • Thorough understanding of contact-center KPIs and performance drivers, with the ability to interpret operational data, identify root causes and turn findings into executable, measurable plans.
  • Experience leading operational incidents or cross-functional escalations and maintaining accountability through resolution.
  • Strong process-management and continuous-improvement capabilities, including development and maintenance of SOPs and operating controls.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication with the ability to clearly communicate performance, risks, recommendations and decisions to team members, vendors, markets and leadership.
  • Proven people leadership capability, including hiring, coaching, performance management and development of team members and leads.
  • Strong working knowledge of contact-center and CRM technologies and the ability to distinguish operational issues from technical issues and engage the appropriate owner.

Key Success Characteristics

  • Operational ownership: takes accountability for business outcomes and drives issues through resolution, even when another team or vendor performs the technical work.
  • Analytical judgment: uses data to diagnose performance, challenge assumptions and make clear recommendations.
  • Proactive communication: identifies and communicates material risks early, with impact, ownership and an action plan.
  • Vendor leadership: establishes clear expectations and follows through on corrective actions and sustained performance.
  • Process discipline: ensures campaign, routing, escalation and service processes are documented, tested and consistently executed.
  • Customer focus: balances operational efficiency with the quality of the customer and market experience.

jobs.description:
About Music Will

Music Will runs the largest nonprofit music education program in the U.S. public school system. We transform lives by transforming music education.

Using genres including rock, pop, Latin, and hip hop, our program empowers teachers to build music programs as diverse as the kids they serve. As a result, students see themselves reflected in their classes, which strengthens their connection to their school, their peers, and their community. Music Will also donates necessary instruments and curriculum, meeting a key need of many school music programs.

Since 2002, Music Will has served more than 1,800,000 students in more than 6,000 schools in over 1,000 cities and communities across 50 states with highly inclusive and culturally responsive music education. Today, over 1 million kids currently participate in Music Will programs, and we’ve set an ambitious goal to serve 11 million students annually by 2030. Learn more here: .

Summary of the Opportunity

Reporting directly to the Chief Finance & Operating Officer (CFOO), the Controller is the organization's senior hands-on accounting leader, responsible for the integrity, accuracy, and timeliness of Music Will's financial reporting and accounting operations.

The Controller will own the monthly close, maintain strong accounting processes and internal controls, oversee cash-flow reporting and forecasting, support budgeting and rolling forecasts, and manage the annual audit and related financial reporting requirements. The role will ensure compliance with GAAP and nonprofit accounting standards, including restricted revenue, grants, and revenue recognition.

This role will also serve as a practical business partner to department leaders, translating financial information into clear, useful insights while supervising and developing the team member responsible primarily for accounts payable and accounts receivable.

Responsibilities

  • Own and manage the monthly close process, ensuring accurate and timely recording, reconciliation and reporting of financial transactions, including cash activity, pledges, journal entries, accruals, restricted funds, and grants.
  • Ensure accounting practices and financial statements comply with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and applicable nonprofit accounting standards, including revenue recognition, restricted contributions, grants, and functional expense reporting, while maintaining accurate financial documentation, established accounting policies, and a strong internal control environment.
  • Maintain the integrity of the general ledger, chart of accounts, and subsidiary ledgers while administering and continuously improving Sage Intacct and related accounting processes, systems, and controls.
  • Develop and maintain cash-flow reporting and a rolling 13-week cash-flow forecast to support liquidity and cash-management decisions.
  • Lead monthly financial forecasting and update full-year revenue and expense projections in partnership with the CFOO and department leaders, including collaboration with the Development team on fundraising projections, grants, and restricted revenue.
  • Partner with department managers to review monthly budget-to-actual performance, understand variances, and update projections.
  • Lead the annual organizational budget process, including developing templates and assumptions, consolidating departmental budgets, and preparing financial reports for review.
  • Ensure accurate and timely preparation of monthly financial statements and reports, including maintaining supporting financial documentation and preparing workpapers for the annual external audit and Form 990 preparation.

Skills, Experiences, and Qualifications

At Music Will, we strive to mitigate inherent biases that influence hiring practices by focusing on a holistic view of potential candidates and understanding that no single candidate will offer every desired skill and characteristic.

jobs.excerpt: beehiiv is where the world's best newsletters, podcasts, and digital products are built, grown, and distributed.
jobs.description:
beehiiv is where the world's best newsletters, podcasts, and digital products are built, grown, and distributed. The platform combines email, podcast hosting, websites, community, and digital products — connected to a single audience and a single set of tools to publish, grow, and monetize. As we approach $50M in annualized revenue and continue to grow almost 100% YoY, our rapidly growing product suite and strong brand position set us up for the next stage of hypergrowth.

We’re hiring an Integrated Marketing Manager to own how beehiiv shows up at the moments that matter. Alongside our Creative Director, you’ll help set the strategy for our campaigns, launches, and events: what we’re saying, to whom, and why now. Then, you’ll own the plan that ships it: the brief, the channel mix, the timeline, the partners, the budget, the measurement, and the live moment itself. Some weeks that’s a billboard and a feed takeover; others it’s an event on the ground, a creator activation, or a product launch running across paid, lifecycle, social, and press at once.

This is a generalist role with spikes in brand campaigns, events, and experiential. You’ll own your programs end to end, and you’re expected to bring ideas, not just plans: a point of view on what a campaign or event should be, before the brief gets written.

Ideally, you'll have:

  • 4-6+ years of experience in integrated or brand marketing, preferably in consumer SaaS, with proven success leading complex projects to fruition
  • A concept-led approach and an opinionated point of view
  • A bias towards action and operating with ambition, creating processes that help cross-functional teams do the same
  • A strong understanding of and passion for go-to-market planning, messaging, and storytelling for brand-driven campaigns
  • The ability to lead through influence: people on the projects you lead become the best versions of themselves by working with you, across product, creative, and data teams
  • Strong organizational and analytical skills, with the ability to balance multiple work streams and deadlines at once
  • Experience owning on-site execution for high-stakes projects, from scouting locations and managing vendors to running the show.

What you'll be responsible for:

In year one, expect roughly 70% integrated campaigns and launches, 20% events and experiential, and 10% building the playbooks and partner bench that make every campaign faster and more impactful.

Run integrated campaigns end to end

  • Turn a creative brief into a working campaign plan: objective, audience, channel mix, timeline, budget, owners, and the KPI we’ll judge it on.
  • Manage the work across internal team members, agencies, and freelancers; keep deliverables, reviews, and deadlines moving without someone chasing you.
  • Own the channel plan for each campaign (paid, social, lifecycle, partnerships, OOH, PR) so it lands as one idea, not six disconnected executions.

Manage events and experiential

  • Work with the broader Growth & Comms teams to produce beehiiv’s presence at the moments that matter: our own events, creator and media gatherings, industry conferences, pop-ups, and activations.
  • Coordinate the whole thing: venue, production partners, speakers and talent, guest list, on-site execution, and the content capture that extends the moment online.
  • Build the recurring calendar of tentpole moments beehiiv can own each year, and make each one measurably better than the last.

Measure and report

  • Define measurement for every program up front with Growth and Analytics: reach, engagement, signups, pipeline, and what we learned.
  • Run daily and weekly check-ins while a campaign is live, recommend budget and channel shifts, and lead the post-mortem.
  • Document playbooks for launches, events, and campaign types so the second run takes half the effort of the first.

What success looks like

A year in, you’ve taken over the live campaign and events calendar.

  • You’ve successfully shipped several integrated campaigns from start to finish.
  • Some of your original ideas have made it from concept to execution.
  • Leadership no longer has to ask who’s handling the logistics — they know you’ve got it covered.

Why this role might be for you

  • You love momentum. You’d rather ship, learn, and iterate than polish something for months. Here, a good idea on Monday can be live by Friday, and you’ll see your impact in real time.
  • You want your creative work to drive business results. You get energy from tying great storytelling to growth. You’ll own work that shows up in reach, pipeline, and revenue, and you’ll be able to point to exactly what it moved.
  • You’re a builder who likes to stay hands-on. You’ll set the bar, pick the right freelancers and agencies, and grow the team as the results justify it.
  • You treat data as a creative partner. You like testing your instincts, learning from the numbers, and coming back with something sharper. Strong ideas get stronger here because we pressure-test them.

Why this role might not be for you

  • You prefer long timelines. Some campaigns go from idea to live in days, not months.
  • You can’t execute without a clear brief. You’ll take great ideas that aren’t fully formed and use your experience and judgment to fill in the gaps and bring them to life.
  • You don't want your ideas tested. Sometimes the data will overrule a great concept.

Why beehiiv?

Our values aren't a poster on the wall. They're the bar. It’s how we operate, publicly and privately, and what we should return to when making decisions. That’s how we keep our team's momentum. That’s how we hire and keep A players.

beehiiv’s core values

  1. There's no room for B players ⭐: the best makes everyone better.
  2. Maniacal sense of urgency ⚡: speed is our superpower.
  3. Say what you think with positive intent 💬: disagree openly and give hard feedback directly, with the intent to help someone improve.
  4. User-obsessed 🐝: every decision starts with one question: how does this add value for the user?
  5. Ego comes second, winning comes first 🏆: we're here to create the best outcome; the team comes before the individual.

We'll take care of you:

  • Competitive salary
  • Stock options
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) employer match
  • Unlimited PTO (mandatory 10 days per year minimum)
  • Annual in-person team offsite
  • Unlimited book budget
  • Monthly Wellness Days (every third Friday of the month)
Salary: USD 130,000 - 150,000

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are hiring a Global Director of Transfer Pricing to our Tax & Treasury team!

Reporting to the SVP of Tax & Treasury, the Global Director of Transfer Pricing will lead the company’s worldwide transfer pricing strategy, governance, compliance, and controversy agenda. This executive will serve as the principal advisor to senior tax, finance, treasury, legal, and business leaders on the design and operation of arm’s-length policies for intercompany transactions. The role will align transfer pricing outcomes with the company’s operating model and value chain; oversee documentation and reporting; strengthen audit readiness and dispute resolution; and translate regulatory developments into practical, scalable business solutions. The Director will coordinate regional and country teams, manage external advisors, and build data-enabled processes and controls that support consistent execution across the enterprise.

YOUR IMPACT

  • Own and continuously improve the global transfer pricing framework for services, intellectual property, cost-sharing or contribution arrangements, business restructurings, and intercompany financing.
  • Partner with business, finance, supply chain, R&D, legal, controllership, and treasury leaders to ensure policies reflect functions, assets, risks, economic substance, and the evolving global operating model.
  • Lead economic and financial analyses, including functional analyses, benchmarking studies, valuation of intangibles, profit-split assessments, and support for financial transactions.
  • Direct the global documentation and reporting program, including the Master File, Local Files, country-by-country reporting, local forms, and contemporaneous support, with clear ownership, calendars, quality standards, and escalation protocols.
  • Establish operational transfer pricing processes for forecasts, target margins, quarterly monitoring, true-ups, journal entries, management reporting, and reconciliation to tax returns and statutory accounts.
  • Develop and maintain a global control framework, including policy governance, intercompany agreements, data lineage, documentation retention, risk assessment, and data-driven key performance indicators.
  • Lead transfer pricing controversy and audit defense worldwide; coordinate responses to tax authorities and manage advance pricing agreements, mutual agreement procedures, competent-authority matters, and settlement strategy where appropriate.
  • Collaborate with the Sr. Director of International Tax Planning on mergers, acquisitions, integrations, divestitures, legal-entity changes, value-chain transformations, and new business models, including implementation requirements and post-transaction monitoring.
  • Monitor OECD, U.S., and local-country developments and assess their impact on transfer pricing, tax accounting, and related global tax initiatives, incorporating AI-driven monitoring and data-driven scenario modeling for Pillar Two and country-by-country analytics.
  • Partner with Treasury to establish and support arm’s-length pricing for intercompany loans, guarantees, cash pools, and other financial transactions.
  • Support tax accounting by assessing transfer pricing exposures, documenting uncertain tax positions, and providing clear inputs for reserves, disclosures, and management reporting.
  • Build trusted relationships with regional finance and tax teams; deliver practical training to stakeholders; and communicate complex issues clearly to executive leadership.
  • Drive innovation in financial modeling and transfer pricing risk management by leveraging AI, automation, and advanced analytics to ensure forecasts, target margins, and compliance processes are accurate, predictive, and scalable globally.
  • Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life wellness.

WHO YOU ARE

  • An experienced tax leader with an advanced degree in economics, accounting, finance, tax, or a related discipline (JD, LLM, CPA, or equivalent professional credential preferred).
  • A seasoned professional with at least 12+ years of progressively responsible transfer pricing experience, including significant leadership in a complex multinational enterprise, major advisory firm, or a combination of both.
  • Expert in transfer pricing with deep command of OECD principles and U.S. and local-country rules, including documentation, economic analysis, IP, services, financial transactions, restructurings, and dispute resolution.
  • A strategic problem solver with demonstrated success designing and operationalizing global policies across multiple jurisdictions, legal entities, business models, and enterprise systems.
  • A battle-tested advocate with proven experience leading audits and controversy matters and working effectively with tax authorities, competent authorities, external counsel, and economic advisors.
  • A strong communicator with excellent executive presence, able to convert complex technical analysis into clear decisions, business implications, and actionable recommendations.
  • A highly effective matrix leader with strong stakeholder management, change leadership, program management, and team-development capabilities across cultures and time zones.
  • A hands-on, daily user of AI tools such as Gemini, Claude or ChatGPT, with concrete examples of work you have automated or redesigned with them.
  • Experience building your own AI workflows or agents, for example, with Claude Code or Codex, to automate recurring work such as monitoring tax law changes across countries, or intercompany calculations or documentation is a strong plus.

Reporting to the SVP of Tax & Treasury, the Sr. Director of Global Tax Reporting & Compliance will lead the company’s worldwide income tax accounting, external reporting, compliance governance, and tax operations. This leader will own the integrity of the global tax provision and related disclosures; establish a scalable, well-controlled compliance model; and modernize the function through standardized processes, trusted data, automation, and responsible use of emerging technology. The Sr. Director will advise senior Finance and business leaders on the reporting, cash-tax, and risk implications of transactions, growth initiatives, and regulatory change, and will build and develop a high-performing global team.

YOUR IMPACT

  • Own the quarterly and annual worldwide income tax provision under ASC 740, including current and deferred tax, effective tax rate analysis, valuation allowances, uncertain tax positions, return-to-provision adjustments, and tax-related disclosures, ensuring external financial statements, regulatory filings, management reporting, and local statutory accounts are accurate, timely, and audit-ready.
  • Lead effective tax rate, taxable income, cash-tax, and balance-sheet forecasting in partnership with FP&A, Controllership, and Treasury.

  • Oversee corporate income tax and related reporting obligations, including extensions, estimates, information returns, country-by-country reporting, and relevant indirect-tax processes.
  • Lead readiness for OECD BEPS and Pillar Two requirements, including governance over GloBE data, calculations, safe-harbour assessments, tax accounting impacts, and filing obligations where applicable.
  • Maintain consistency among tax returns, legal-entity books, transfer pricing policies, intercompany activity, and the consolidated tax provision.
  • Oversee tax audits, notices, and information requests in partnership with specialist teams and external advisors, ensuring positions are documented and defensible.
  • Own the tax control framework, including SOX controls, process documentation, evidence standards, and issue remediation, using a risk-based approach with clear escalation protocols and materiality thresholds.
  • Advise senior Finance leadership and external auditors on the tax impacts of acquisitions, dispositions, integrations, restructurings, financing, new markets, and changes in law.
  • Drive the tax technology roadmap with an emphasis on AI-driven automation and predictive analytics, integrating ERP, consolidation, provision, and compliance systems; standardize, simplify, and automate end-to-end tax processes to shorten close cycles, optimize data quality, and reduce manual effort.
  • Lead the responsible AI governance framework and deployment of advanced AI/ML capabilities across Tax & Treasury, incorporating AI tools for predictive tax forecasting, automated scenario planning, and enhanced risk management with rigorous validation, data security, and human oversight.
  • Monitor tax and financial-reporting developments and translate them into timely decisions, implementation plans, controls, and stakeholder communications.
  • Build, develop, and retain a globally connected team with clear roles, succession plans, and measurable performance expectations; partner with Controllership, FP&A, Treasury, Legal, Internal Audit, IT, and regional finance and business leaders to embed tax considerations in decisions.
  • Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life wellness.

jobs.description:
Position Title: Senior Manager, Youth Grants & Educator Engagement

Status: Full Time

FLSA: Exempt

Location: Flexible

JOB SUMMARY & KEY PRIORITIES

The Youth Leadership Team equips and mobilizes youth and young adults to strengthen their leadership, advocate for mental health, and create change in their schools and communities through accessible, high-quality, equity-centered leadership programs and opportunities. The team works directly with youth and young adults, schools and Youth Champions (adult stakeholders, such as educators, counselors, and caregivers) to foster youth-led initiatives that drive school-based mental health change.

The Senior Manager, Youth Grants & Educator Engagement oversees two initiatives within the Youth Leadership portfolio: the Active Minds Youth Mental Health Innovation Fund, a national microgrant program for youth-designed mental health projects, and Youth Champions, Active Minds’ engagement strategy for adult stakeholders. This role manages microgrants, mentorship, technical assistance, and scaling support for youth grantees, while centering BIPOC and LGBTQ+ youth. The Senior Manager also manages professional development, coaching, and training that equip adult allies to sustain youth mental health leadership in schools and communities.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Youth Leadership, this role manages program operations, cultivates school and community partnerships, tracks impact metrics, and stewards grant resources to advance youth mobilization. The Senior Manager directly supervises the Manager, Middle School Engagement.

ABOUT ACTIVE MINDS

Active Minds is the largest nonprofit in the United States mobilizing youth and young adults to transform mental health norms across society. For more than 20 years, we have equipped the next generation of peer mental health advocates through a variety of programs, including the Active Minds Chapter Network, A.S.K., and Send Silence Packing. Our advocacy, initiatives, and campaigns foster lasting change in how youth view and discuss mental health, encouraging them to use their voices to influence broader conversations and inform mental health supports within their communities. Together, we are building a diverse movement of champions committed to improving mental health for all.

KEY RESULTS

Oversee Functional/Tactical Goals

  • Manage the annual planning, launch, and distribution cycle of the Active Minds Youth Mental Health Innovation Fund, awarding microgrants to youth-designed mental health projects.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain clear eligibility, selection, and equity criteria for the Innovation Fund that actively center BIPOC and LGBTQ+ youth and historically under-resourced communities.
  • Facilitate virtual and in-person Youth Champion workshops and Connection sessions, equipping adult stakeholders with the language, resources, and tools needed to champion youth-led mental health advocacy.
  • Track and report the number of youth and young adults mobilized through Innovation Fund and Youth Champion programming, contributing to the Program Department’s annual goals.
  • Maintain organized tracking of project milestones, partner interactions, grant awards, and participant data in Salesforce and ClickUp.

Cross Functional Program Collaboration

  • In collaboration with other teams within the Programs Department, partner with schools and districts to position peer-led mental health strategies as actionable solutions within school wellness priorities and Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) frameworks.
  • Collaborate with the Chapters and Community Programs teams to support Chapter Advisors as local technical assistance providers and frontline champions for high school youth mobilization, in line with Active Minds’ integrated high school engagement approach.
  • Serve as a collaborative thought partner across the Youth Leadership team to ensure seamless handoffs and consistent youth advocacy pathways.
  • In partnership with team leadership and the Development Team, cultivate and maintain relationships with K-12 school districts, education associations, charter networks, and funding partners, and contribute to grant proposals, concept notes, and stewardship reports highlighting the Youth Innovation Fund and Youth Champion results.
  • In collaboration with Marketing & Communications, guide the development of outreach campaigns, newsletters, web content, and spotlight stories that showcase youth grantees and Youth Champion accomplishments.
  • In collaboration with the Measurement Team, collect standardized data on participation, completion, participant experience (maintaining a new promoter score of 80% or higher), and intended leadership outcomes across the Innovation Fund and Youth Champion programming. Establish baselines and improvement targets, and document data-informed program improvements annually. Establish annual participation baselines and demographic tracking across applicant and grantee pools to ensure continuous equity-centered representation.

Budget Management

  • Manage Innovation Fund disbursements and program budgets, maintaining accurate records, fiscal compliance, and timely stipend and grant payments.
  • In partnership with the Senior Director, Youth Leadership, contribute to annual budget planning for the Innovation Fund and Youth Champion programming.

Program Development

  • Build and manage mentorship, coaching, and technical assistance for Innovation Fund grantees, connecting them with subject matter experts to support project implementation, sustainability, and scale.
  • Manage the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of professional development, coaching, and training for Youth Champions, including educators, school administrators, counselors, and caregivers.
  • Grow networks of Youth Champions and parent/caregiver allies, building ongoing engagement pathways that reinforce youth mental health leadership locally.
  • Position the Innovation Fund within Youth Leadership’s mental health champions continuum, connecting grantees to related leadership opportunities (e.g., Mental Health Advocacy Academy, Mental Health Advocacy Institute, High School Advisory Board, Chapters) so they can deepen their leadership over time.
  • Engage BIPOC and LGBTQ+ youth, including High School Advisory Board members and past grantees, in shaping Innovation Fund design, selection, and resources, and document how their input leads to program improvements each year.

Proactive Innovation

  • Collaborate closely with Active Minds’ Measurement Team to establish, monitor, and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) evaluating the impact of Youth Champions on youth mobilization and school climate, sharing results and learnings to inform future program strategy.
  • Partner with Innovation Fund grantees as co-creators, documenting project outcomes, case studies, and scalable practices to inform Active Minds’ programmatic strategy and external thought leadership.

Team Supervision

  • Supervise, coach, and develop the Manager, Middle School Engagement and any assigned interns, establishing clear performance expectations, deliverable timelines, and meaningful professional development pathways.
  • Oversee middle school engagement goals and deliverables, including growing the number of new sites implementing the Middle and High School Mental Health Curriculum year over year.
  • Share tools, training, and practices with colleagues outside the direct team to strengthen adult support for youth leadership across the department.

Organization-Wide Competencies

  • Actively advance Active Minds’ racial equity and social justice goals, ensuring programming reflects inclusive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based practices.
  • Represent Active Minds externally at conferences, symposia, and working groups as a subject matter expert in youth-led innovation and adult stakeholder engagement.
  • Support cross-functional organizational initiatives and strategic planning deliverables as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 6+ years of demonstrated professional experience working within K-12 schools and/or higher education settings or youth serving organizations (school-based or campus-based environments), with deep familiarity with school culture, administration, and student programming.
  • Proven track record of cultivating and sustaining positive relationships with adult and parent/caregiver stakeholders, including teachers, school counselors, building and district administrators, parent-teacher associations, and community partners.
  • Demonstrated expertise in youth development, student mentorship, and leadership coaching, with a strong background in guiding youth-led projects, advocacy campaigns, or social entrepreneurship initiatives.
  • Demonstrated experience in program design and project management, including managing multi-phase initiatives, establishing timelines, coordinating cross-functional deliverables, and tracking budgets.
  • Experience designing and facilitating adult learning or interactive youth programming, with the ability to lead engaging workshops and trainings in both virtual and in-person environments.
  • Demonstrated commitment to racial equity and social justice, with direct experience designing culturally responsive programming and centering the lived experiences of BIPOC and LGBTQ+ youth and adult communities.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, with proven experience translating programmatic data into compelling narratives, presentations, and stakeholder reports.
  • Willingness and ability to travel periodically for conferences, summits, site visits, and team retreats, along with occasional scheduled evening programming to accommodate student and educator schedules.
  • Proficiency with collaborative technology, including Google Workspace, project management software (e.g., ClickUp, Asana), and CRM systems (e.g., Salesforce).

OUR CULTURE

Active Minds is a place where every employee matters. We value diverse perspectives, radical authenticity, and a community-driven approach. We dream big, offering flexibility to staff while we work to achieve our mission. As such, we are proud to offer competitive salaries and benefits and an environment that is friendly to remote working and life/work balance.

Active Minds is an equal opportunity employer that works to advance racial equity and social justice in an increasingly multicultural and globally connected world. We value diverse experiences, including educational background, intersectional identities, and lived experiences. We make a particular effort to recruit people of color, LGBTQ individuals, people with disabilities, and people with other marginalized identities. Active Minds encourages all to apply for our open positions as we depend on a diverse staff to carry out our mission.

COMPENSATION

This position offers an initial salary range of $80,850–$91,700 along with robust benefits. The starting pay for this position is equal to others at the same level throughout the organization. The role sits within Active Minds Level 4 salary band, and as such, has the potential to grow to $113,400 over time. FLSA Status: Exempt.

Active Minds has an industry-leading and competitive benefits package that includes Health, Vision, and Dental Insurance, Paid Vacation and Sick Leave, Paid Holidays, Company Wide Mental Health Days, 401(k) Matching, HSA and FSA Options, Life Insurance, Short Term and Long Term Disability, Fully Paid Parental Leave, Wellness Reimbursement Program, and Professional Development Stipends.

Active Minds recruits, hires, trains, compensates, and promotes our staff regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, sexual orientation, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law.

ACTIVE MINDS RECRUITING PROTOCOLS

  • Active Minds will never ask an applicant to send – and Active Minds will never send an applicant - a check or any payment or item of value (such as a gift card) in connection with the interview process or job onboarding process.
  • Active Minds will never ask for personal information about an applicant (such as their Social Security number or banking information) until the job onboarding process.
  • All legitimate Active Minds job offers are extended verbally by the HR/People & Culture Team.
  • If you are expecting an email from Active Minds, please always verify that the sending domain in the email is activeminds.org and NOT any variation of it.

For further information on how to protect yourself from employment scams, please review these“Consumer Advice” guidelines.

While this position is remote, it may include occasional work at a Wabtec office/site or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager.

Relocation assistance may be provided if eligibility requirements are met.

CENSUS is an internationally acclaimed Cybersecurity services provider. We support the needs of multiple industries, providing IT and OT security assessment services to public and private organizations around the world, including international financial institutions and Fortune 500 companies. Powered by cutting-edge research, scientific analysis, and real-world engineering, we deliver unparalleled security assessment services for software, devices, infrastructure, and organizations. Learn more about CENSUS at census-labs.com.

About the Role

CENSUS is looking for a Vulnerability Researcher specializing in modern web browsers and browser exploitation.

The role focuses on identifying, analyzing, and demonstrating security vulnerabilities in complex browser components such as rendering engines, JavaScript engines, IPC systems, sandboxing mechanisms, and platform integrations.

Responsibilities

  • Research security vulnerabilities in modern browsers such as Firefox, Chromium-based and WebKit-based browsers.
  • Perform source-code auditing of large C/C++ codebases to identify memory-safety, logic, sandbox, and privilege-boundary vulnerabilities.
  • Investigate JavaScript engine internals such as V8, SpiderMonkey, or JavaScriptCore.
  • Analyze browser sandbox boundaries and investigate sandbox escape vulnerabilities.
  • Reverse engineer browser binaries and security-relevant operating-system components.
  • Debug crashes and memory-corruption issues using tools such as WinDbg, GDB, LLDB, AddressSanitizer, and related tooling.
  • Develop fuzzers, harnesses, and automation for vulnerability discovery.
  • Study exploit mitigations such as ASLR, DEP/NX, Control Flow Guard, CET, CFI, MTE/MIE, pointer authentication, and sandboxing.
  • Develop proof-of-concept exploits to validate vulnerabilities and understand their practical impact.
  • Produce clear technical reports describing vulnerability root cause, exploitability and affected components.

Required Skills

  • Strong knowledge of C/C++ and x64/aarch64 assembly.
  • Excellent understanding of memory management, pointers, object lifetime, and concurrency.
  • Strong knowledge of operating-system internals, particulary Android and iOS.
  • Experience with reverse engineering tools such as IDA Pro, Ghidra, Binary Ninja, or similar.
  • Familiarity with browser architecture and multi-process sandbox designs.
  • Experience analyzing large codebases.
  • Knowledge of common memory-corruption vulnerability classes and exploitation techniques.
  • Familiarity with debugging and sanitization tools such as ASan, UBSan, WinDbg, GDB, or LLDB.
  • Ability to independently investigate complex technical problems and document findings clearly.

Preferred Skills

Experience researching Chrome, Firefox, Safari.

Experience developing browser exploits or participating in vulnerability disclosure / bug-bounty programs.

Experience with coverage-guided fuzzing tools such as libFuzzer, AFL++, or custom fuzzing frameworks.

Familiarity with modern exploit-development techniques including heap manipulation, arbitrary read/write primitives, information leaks, and control-flow manipulation.

Knowledge of compiler-generated mitigations and browser hardening mechanisms.

  • Thought leadership in data science or analytics, internally and externally

The opportunity is growing fast. AI is driving growth in GitLab's consumption business, creating new ways for data to drive growth. As AI takes over routine reporting, the team focuses on the hard problems: experimentation, causal inference, production models, and recommendations leaders act on.

Role Title: Principal Engineer / Professor — Technical Expert

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

Opportunity Snapshot

Pay:$80- $185/hour

Commitment: Flexible — fits alongside your current role

Location: Fully remote

You’ll need: Master’s or PhD in an engineering or physical science field, plus principal-level industry experience or a faculty appointment

Your tasks: Build challenging technical problems from your own domain and define what makes an answer correct

micro1 is engaging principal-level engineers, scientists, and faculty to design the technical problems that measure what AI systems can actually do. Your domain expertise is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.

We’re building this across four areas: aerospace, semiconductors, manufacturing and industrial engineering, and materials science. If your work sits in one of those — or across two of them — this is for you.

The work draws on what you already know: the problems where the textbook answer isn’t enough, where the right approach depends on reading the constraints correctly, where a plausible-looking solution is quietly wrong.

What you’ll do

  1. Design difficult technical problems from your own area, with realistic constraints and supporting data.
  2. Provide the correct solution and walk through the reasoning that gets there.
  3. Define objective criteria for correctness, so another expert reviewing the work would reach the same verdict.
  4. Review problems built by other contributors for technical accuracy and soundness of method.
  5. Flag problems that turn out to be ambiguous or ungradable rather than submitting them.

What we’re looking for

  1. Master’s or PhD in engineering, physics, materials, or a closely related field.
  2. Principal, staff, or fellow-level experience at a major engineering organization, a national lab, or a faculty appointment at a leading university.
  3. Deep technical depth in at least one area, with hands-on ownership of the work.
  4. Able to explain why an answer is correct clearly enough that another expert could verify it.
  5. Publications, patents, or a record of technical leadership is a strong plus.

How the selection process works

  1. Apply and complete the screening questions
  2. Complete the AI interview for this role
  3. Profile review
  4. Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

jobs.description:
About Improvado

Improvado is an AI-powered marketing data platform built for mid-market and enterprise teams. We help companies automate complex marketing data workflows, unify data at scale, and surface insights through BI and AI. Brands like Genentech, T-Mobile, Activision, and H&R Block rely on us to simplify analytics and improve marketing performance.

We’re a fast-growing Series A startup backed by $34M in funding and driven by a team that moves fast, stays curious, and cares about high-quality execution.

About the role

Improvado is a marketing data platform for enterprise brands and agencies. You will own how our revenue runs and how it is measured. That covers Salesforce and the GTM tools, the path from signed contract to paid invoice, the revenue data model, and the reports leadership decides from. You work closely with the analytics team: you don’t have to build the data models yourself, but you must read them, spot what is wrong and say what to change. You work through AI agents daily, doing the work of a bigger team.

What you will do

Salesforce and GTM stack

  • Own Salesforce configuration, release process and user access, plus the integrations around it (Gong, Clay, Lemlist, enrichment, e-signature, lead routing).
  • Keep CRM data clean with guardrails that block mistakes. Manage licences and vendor renewals.
  • Maintain the Salesforce manual and RevOps SOPs, and train new hires.

Contract to cash

  • Own ARR and bookings logic (new, upsell, downsell, churn, renewals) and keep agreement, opportunity, and invoice consistent.
  • Run the closed-deals and billing check with Finance. Fix errors at the source and add a control so they don’t repeat.
  • Audit invoices, track and chase unpaid ones, and prepare quarterly commission and quota reports.

Revenue analytics and data model

  • Own the quarterly sales analytics pack, the CRO report, the forecast and pipeline coverage (including CS renewal inputs).
  • Track funnel conversion, explain why deals move, stall or slip, and keep attribution correct with Marketing.
  • Query ClickHouse daily, trace any number to its source, and write specs for model changes. Give each metric one documented definition and add data quality checks.
  • Build leadership dashboards, retire unused ones, and end every analysis with a recommendation, a number and an owner.

AI and automation

  • Use coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) for queries, scripts and Salesforce automation, and always verify their output.
  • Automate manual work (invoice and payment checks, CRM hygiene, deal-risk alerts, call analysis) and measure hours saved and errors avoided.

Ownership

  • Be the single RevOps contact for Sales, CS, Marketing, Finance and Product. Turn each request into a task with an owner, date and success metric.

Requirements

  • 4-6+ years in RevOps, Sales Ops or GTM systems in B2B SaaS, with hands-on admin of a live Salesforce org.
  • Strong SQL and comfort in a modeled warehouse (layers, lineage, one definition per metric). dbt is a plus.
  • Deep knowledge of the B2B SaaS revenue cycle: funnel, pipeline, forecast, ARR, churn, renewals.
  • Experience running the money side: contracts, invoicing, collections, kept in sync with the CRM.
  • Proof you build with AI agents: something you shipped that others use.
  • Fluent English and clear written updates without being asked.

Nice to have

  • Salesforce Administrator or Advanced Administrator certification.
  • ClickHouse or another columnar warehouse, and any BI tool.
  • Salesforce development (Apex, triggers, API).
  • Gong, Clay, Lemlist, or workflow automation tools.
  • Billing, CPQ, or accounting systems.
  • HubSpot to Salesforce migration.
  • Attribution or CS health score data.
  • Martech or analytics company background.

What We Offer

  • Remote-first environment
  • Strong product/market fit: marketing data product for US-based enterprises
  • 20 working days of PTO per year
  • US holidays and additional days off
  • Professional development reimbursement

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.

As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.

About the role

At Moniepoint, as an Analytics Manager, you will use data to make better decisions, faster for the business. You will own metrics, measurement, experimentation and the analysis/data roadmap for a business area. You’ll use data to quantify business KPIs and conduct analyses to uncover unknowns, helping the business unit achieve its goals for acquisition, conversion, activation, retention, and revenue. As a leader of the business unit, the role sits at the intersection of product management, data engineering, and growth.

What you’ll do

  • Strategic Leadership: Build a disciplined, exceptional analytical team. Develop and execute a comprehensive data and analytics roadmap and strategy
  • Team Building & Management: Hire, develop, and retain a high-performing team of analytics professionals
  • Data Insights & Analytics - including forecast building, business analysis and model development and productionisation. Drive the generation of actionable insights from data to support various business functions, including product, operations, marketing and engineering. What is our actual CAC per channel? Which customer segments are more/less engaged? What are our customers’ share of wallet - how can we use this? What is the typical behaviour of a Moniepoint consumer? What products cause the biggest incremental engagement?
  • Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner with growth, product, and engineering managers to ensure we collect the right data for meaningful business insights. Bring data leadership and rigour to our approach to product development. Build a strategic understanding of the business and structure complex projects to bring them to life.

Business: Growth

  • Create and maintain the yearly forecast and budget for your products.
  • Define the product's growth plan and lead execution across the entire funnel from acquisition through to monetisation and retention
  • Own and optimise specific business metrics or commercial goals, covering the entire funnel from new user acquisition through conversion, activation, retention, and expansion
  • Perform detailed product analysis covering the product management funnel with all its aspects, implementing changes into the buying funnel to improve conversion
  • Design and execute A/B testing programs to optimise sales and conversion rates/adoption at each funnel stage
  • Lead testing and optimisation efforts for the conversion funnel across offline and online channels, prioritising tests that drive the biggest business impact
  • Improve the product's design and deploy experiments to improve lifetime value (LTV) and decrease churn

Technical: Data & Analytics

  • Use deep, flexible, and comprehensive analytics covering the entire funnel from marketing acquisition to product usage
  • Analyse user behaviour to improve the sales funnel and increase conversions, using advanced analytics to assess campaign performance and refine strategies
  • Define and track growth metrics including customer acquisition cost (CAC), activation rate, retention rate, payback time, and revenue per customer
  • Conduct cohort analysis and journey mapping to identify bottlenecks and optimisation opportunities

What you need to succeed

  • +5 years in Analytics and Analytics Management.
  • 2+ years in a management role managing teams and driving strategic initiatives
  • Proven track record in a consumer-FMCG environment, preferably in a CPG or fintech environment
  • Deep experience scaling product businesses, with demonstrated ownership of significant revenue targets

Technical Skills

  • Strong analytical skills with ability to drive metrics and benchmarks, plus experience with growth experiments, A/B testing, and funnel optimisation
  • Deep SQL knowledge.
  • Proficiency in product analytics tools (Mixpanel, Grafana, Tableau, Looker, etc)

Leadership & Soft Skills

  • Strong communication skills to interact with teams, stakeholders, and users through verbal presentations, written reports, and visual media
  • Proven ability to build, mentor, and scale high-performing product teams
  • Expertise in data analytics tools and digital marketing platforms with the ability to manage and mentor teams of marketers, analysts, and designers

Key Performance Indicators

  • Customer retention and churn rates
  • Expansion revenue (upsell/cross-sell)
  • Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) / Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) ratio
  • Product adoption metrics

What sets you apart

  • Advanced degree in Business or STEM
  • Experience in Growth Analytics, Product analytics, Credit risk analytics
  • Background in both mass-marketing and product-led growth models
  • Experience managing P&L or budget responsibility

What you’ll get

jobs.excerpt: About TintTint enables SaaS platforms and marketplaces to unlock growth and improve profitability through embedded insurance.
jobs.description:
About Tint

Tint enables SaaS platforms and marketplaces to unlock growth and improve profitability through embedded insurance. We offer plug-and-play and white-labeled integrations, equipping brands we partner with a sophisticated mix of technology infrastructure, services, and deep industry expertise. Embedded insurance can transform insurance from a product bought separately to a feature of brands consumers love and we are on a mission to make that happen.

Happy Tint customers include Turo, Deel, uShip, Guesty, Montway, Neighbor, and CitizenShipper, among others.

We've raised $30M and are backed by world-class investors such as Y Combinator, QED, Deciens, Nyca, Plug and Play, WIN, Soma Capital, and Pioneer Fund.

About the role

Tint is seeking a Head of Drone & UAV Insurance to lead the strategy, development, and growth of embedded insurance solutions for the commercial drone market. This includes inspection and survey operators, drone delivery, agriculture, aerial imaging, drone-as-a-service platforms, and rental and equipment marketplaces.

This leader will design and scale insurance programs for one of the fastest-evolving risk categories in the market. Working closely with aviation carriers, MGAs, brokers, drone platforms, and our internal product and operations teams, you will build programs that fit how modern drone businesses operate, from per-flight and on-demand coverage to annual fleet policies.

The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in aviation or drone insurance and a track record of designing and launching programs with carriers and distribution partners. This role is highly strategic and requires both domain expertise and the ability to build a new market from the ground up.

What you will do

  • Lead Drone/UAV Insurance Strategy: Define and execute Tint’s strategy across the drone vertical, identifying market opportunities and building scalable embedded insurance solutions for operators, platforms, and marketplaces.
  • Design and Launch Insurance Programs: Lead the design and launch of drone insurance programs, including:
    • Program structure across hull, liability, payload, and non-owned coverage
    • Underwriting guidelines and eligibility criteria (pilot certification, operation type, airspace)
    • Pricing and risk segmentation, including usage-based and per-flight models
    • Policy forms, filings, and regulatory compliance
  • Build Carrier and Capacity Partnerships: Develop and manage relationships with aviation carriers, MGAs, reinsurers, and brokers to secure sustainable capacity and competitive program structures.
  • Grow Tint’s Presence in the Drone Ecosystem: Build relationships with drone operators, software platforms, OEMs, and marketplaces to grow Tint’s customer base and uncover new embedded insurance opportunities.
  • Monitor Program Performance: Track underwriting results, claims trends, and operational metrics to improve profitability, risk management, and customer value.
  • Serve as Industry Subject Matter Expert: Act as Tint’s internal and external expert on drone risk, tracking FAA rules (including Part 107, Remote ID, and BVLOS developments), emerging exposures such as privacy and cyber, and new coverage models.
  • Represent Tint in the Market: Engage with carriers, brokers, drone companies, and industry groups to position Tint as a leader in drone insurance.

You should apply if you have...

  • 5+ years in aviation, drone/UAV, or specialty insurance, with meaningful exposure to commercial drone operations
  • Experience designing or launching insurance programs, including underwriting structures, filings, and carrier partnerships
  • A strong understanding of drone risk characteristics across operation types, equipment, and regulatory environments
  • Experience working with carriers, MGAs, brokers, and reinsurers to structure programs
  • The ability to work cross-functionally with product, engineering, operations, and sales teams
  • Strong analytical and strategic thinking, with the ability to turn market opportunities into scalable solutions
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills
  • Experience in fast-paced environments such as startups, MGAs, or program administrators

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with embedded insurance, program business, or digital insurance platforms
  • Familiarity with flight log data, telematics, or usage-based insurance models
  • An FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate
  • CPCU, CIC, or similar professional certifications

What We Value Most in a Candidate

  • Culture is Key. As a remote company, we take culture very seriously. We are looking for self-motivated candidates who can stay motivated and focused. But don't worry, we're still social! We work collaboratively even though we are remote and travel to team and company retreats throughout the year, which builds the personal relationships that allow us multiply our power working remotely. That also means we hold ourselves to a high standard in how we treat each other (with respect, professionalism, and genuine care) to maintain an environment where colleagues feel safe and valued - that's something we don't compromise on.
  • Focused on Results. We are a fast-moving small team with big goals. We need team players that feel a sense of urgency to drive meaningful results for the business. We have clear company goals and a pathway to significant growth - and this role is integral to that journey.
  • Customer-first. Put yourself in the shoes of someone trying to buy our solution. We need a person who can empathize with our customers and help create strategies to continually improve the customer experience.
  • Adaptability. We're still an early-stage start-up, and things change quickly. If you are energized by learning and discovering on-the-go, this will be an excellent fit for you. We are looking for open-minded candidates that adapt well to changing environments as our company grows and scales.

Why Tint?

Tint isn’t just focused on transforming the entire insurance industry - we have ambitious goals, value merit and open communication, celebrating diversity and unique ideas. At Tint, we support your personal and professional growth by offering the below benefits:

  • Flexible Working. With team members working across time zones, we are outcome-focused and give our people the flexibility they need to do their best work. To support flexible working, we’ll give you a stipend to get your home office dialed in and we’ll also reimburse you for co-working space memberships.
  • Flexible Time Off. It's pretty simple: we don't control the days and hours that each of us works, so we're free to manage our time however we want to achieve the goals and deliverables we committed to. We have unlimited vacation time. Use it whenever you need to recharge!
  • Competitive Compensation. In addition to a competitive salary, you’ll receive equity as part of your offer. We’re all owners - when Tint succeeds, we all succeed! We also help you maximize your money by offering an FSA and a 401(k).
  • Comprehensive Healthcare. Tint covers 100% of employee (and dependent!) premiums for medical, vision and dental.
  • Company Retreats to Exciting Locations. We meet in person as a company twice a year to make sure we have time to connect in real life and get to have those conversations that are better done in person. These retreats are a mix of business and fun and we always choose a cool, central-ish location - think Barcelona, Playa del Carmen, Mallorca… Add on a few days of your flexible time off and you’ve *almost* got a free vacation somewhere cool!

About the Role

We're hiring an OTC Trader to manage day-to-day trading activities across String's OTC desk, covering fiat currencies and stablecoins.

This is a hands-on trading role for someone comfortable sourcing competitive prices from liquidity providers, distributing daily rates, quoting counterparties, and executing trades.

You'll work closely with our treasury and commercial teams to ensure trades are competitively priced, efficiently executed, and commercially profitable.

The role is focused on managing trading activity and growing transaction volumes from existing counterparties rather than originating new customers. You'll also help expand our network of liquidity providers to improve pricing and execution capabilities.


What you'll do

FX Pricing & Liquidity Sourcing

  • Source and compare live FX and stablecoin rates across banks, OTC desks, and liquidity providers.

  • Identify the best executable prices based on spreads, available liquidity, transaction size, and settlement requirements.

  • Maintain relationships with existing liquidity providers and identify new pricing and liquidity opportunities.

  • Monitor market movements, liquidity conditions, and pricing trends across supported currencies.

  • Negotiate competitive rates while maintaining String's target trading margins.

Trading & Execution

  • Provide indicative and firm quotes to counterparties across USD, USDT, USDC, GHS, NGN, and other supported currencies.

  • Manage trade execution from pricing and negotiation through booking and confirmation.

  • Maintain accurate trade records, including transaction amounts, exchange rates, spreads, and counterparty details.

  • Coordinate with treasury to confirm funding availability and settlement arrangements before committing to trades.

  • Monitor outstanding trades and resolve pricing or execution-related issues.

Counterparty Management & Trading Activity

  • Distribute daily FX and stablecoin rates to existing counterparties through approved communication channels.

  • Respond promptly to pricing enquiries and requests for quotes.

  • Maintain active relationships with counterparties to encourage recurring trading activity.

  • Follow up on outstanding quotes and identify opportunities to increase trading volumes.

  • Reactivate dormant counterparties and strengthen engagement with existing trading relationships.

Liquidity Provider & Counterparty Onboarding

  • Identify and establish relationships with new OTC desks, market makers, and liquidity providers.

  • Evaluate potential liquidity partners based on pricing competitiveness, execution reliability, settlement capabilities, and available liquidity.

  • Coordinate onboarding of new liquidity providers with compliance and treasury teams.

  • Maintain an active network of trading counterparties to support competitive pricing and execution.

Trading Operations & Risk Management

  • Monitor trading spreads, execution costs, and net desk revenue.

  • Ensure trades are executed within approved pricing, exposure, and risk limits.

  • Maintain accurate trading records and support daily trade reconciliation with treasury.

  • Escalate unusual market conditions, pricing discrepancies, and execution risks.

  • Prepare daily trading activity reports covering volumes, margins, executed trades, and outstanding transactions.


What we're looking for

  • Approximately 2–6 years of experience in FX trading, OTC trading, treasury dealing, brokerage, or institutional digital asset trading.

  • Practical experience sourcing FX or stablecoin liquidity and executing transactions.

  • Strong understanding of foreign exchange markets, bid/offer spreads, pricing, and trade execution.

  • Familiarity with stablecoins, particularly USDT and USDC.

  • Experience working with OTC desks, liquidity providers, brokers, or institutional counterparties.

  • Ability to negotiate competitive pricing and manage multiple live transactions.

  • Strong numerical and analytical skills with excellent attention to detail.

  • Good communication skills and the ability to maintain active counterparty relationships.

  • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced trading environment.


Nice to have

  • Experience at an OTC desk, FX brokerage, remittance company, payment service provider, or institutional crypto trading firm.

  • Existing relationships with OTC desks, market makers, or liquidity providers.

  • Familiarity with African FX markets, particularly Ghana and Nigeria.

  • Experience trading USD/GHS, USD/NGN, USDT/GHS, or USDT/NGN.

  • Understanding of cross-border payment settlement, banking rails, and stablecoin networks.


Performance measures

  • Daily and monthly trading volume.

  • Net desk revenue and trading margins.

  • Quote-to-trade conversion rate.

  • Quote response time and execution efficiency.

  • Trading frequency and activity across existing counterparties.

  • Competitiveness of sourced liquidity and execution pricing.

  • Trade booking accuracy and adherence to risk limits.

A Culture of Excellence

Ready to modernize medicine with us?

ModMed is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Enterprise RCM Client Manager (internally referred to as an "Enterprise RCM Client Advisor") to join our team. In this client-facing role, you will be responsible for managing and reporting on the RCM operations for our enterprise-sized medical practice clients.
