jobs.excerpt: Who is Prescryptive? Prescryptive is the healthcare technology company enabling the direct access marketplace for prescription drugs.
jobs.description:
Who is Prescryptive?

Prescryptive is the healthcare technology company enabling the direct access marketplace for prescription drugs. Our platform aligns incentives so affordability, choice, and patient access become the natural outcome of a functioning system. Learn more about us by following us on LinkedIn or visiting Prescryptive.com.

About this role

As a Director, Software Engineering, you will lead a domain within our engineering organization. You are accountable for the health of the systems your domain owns, the quality and durability of the team's technical decisions, and the growth and effectiveness of the engineers you lead. You will set direction for your domain, create clarity for engineers and partners, and ensure the team is focused on the problems that matter most.

We are hiring three Directors of Software Engineering to lead distinct product and platform domains: Consumer Experience, B2B Products & Portals, and Backend Platforms & Services. Each role shares the same leadership expectations, but the technical emphasis will vary by domain. We are looking for leaders with deep experience in at least one of these areas, not all three.

You will work directly with engineering leadership, product leaders, technical product managers, and other domain leads to connect technical strategy to business outcomes. The role requires someone who can bring structure to ambiguity, make pragmatic technical decisions, and lead people through complex work with clarity, judgment, and ownership.

The domains we are hiring for

Consumer Experience

  • Lead the engineering team responsible for consumer-facing digital experiences, with a focus on usability, performance, accessibility, and reliable delivery across web and mobile-responsive experiences.

B2B Products and Portals

  • Lead the engineering team responsible for customer, partner, and operational portals, with a focus on complex workflows, enterprise usability, permissions and data access, integrations, and scalable product capabilities.

Backend Platforms and Services

  • Lead the engineering team responsible for core backend services, APIs, data flows, and platform capabilities, with a focus on scalability, reliability, security, performance, and system integration.

What you will do

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of software engineers, including performance management, feedback, career development, hiring, and team health.
  • Assess and evolve your team's structure, capabilities, and capacity; identify talent gaps and make sound calls on hiring and allocation
  • Own the technical direction, delivery discipline, and operating rhythm for an engineering domain in partnership with product and engineering leadership.
  • Translate business needs into technical priorities, sequencing decisions, and executable plans.
  • Elevate the technical judgment of engineers around you through design reviews, architectural guidance, and mentorship
  • Stay close enough to the code and architecture to guide hard technical tradeoffs, review critical designs, and step into complex problem solving when needed.
  • Ensure the team builds and operates high-quality software from design through production operations, including on-call readiness and incident response
  • Engage directly with product, technical product managers, and executive stakeholders to assess feasibility, cost, risk, and delivery implications of strategic initiatives.
  • Identify overlapping work, cross-team dependencies, architectural risks, and technical debt before they become constraints.
  • Hold the team accountable for commitments, surface delivery risks early, and work with product and engineering partners to adjust scope, sequencing or resources when necessary.

What you will bring

  • 10+ years of software development experience, including accountability for the performance, delivery, and technical outcomes of an engineering team.
  • 3+ years of formal people management leading software engineers, with a genuine passion for coaching and for building teams where engineers do their best work
  • Strong technical depth in at least one relevant engineering domain, with the judgment to go deep when needed and the humility to rely on specialists when appropriate.
  • Experience leading delivery for complex systems that span multiple services, teams, or domains.
  • Strong proficiency in the languages, frameworks, and technologies relevant to the domain you would lead, with the ability to ramp quickly in unfamiliar areas. Our stack includes C#, Go, TypeScript, and React.
  • Proven ability to own the full software development lifecycle, from requirements and design through construction, testing, deployment, and production operations.
  • Strong understanding of the architecture, data flows, APIs, cloud environment, and operational dependencies relevant to the systems your domain owns.
  • You optimize for the right solution given real constraints, not the theoretically perfect one.
  • You create technical alignment across teams with competing priorities and make tradeoffs visible to stakeholders.
  • You hold a high bar without creating unnecessary process.
  • You translate fluently between business language and technical language, in both directions.
  • Enthusiasm for leveraging AI-assisted development tools and emerging technologies.
  • Must have permission to work in the US on a permanent basis.

Ideally you will also have

  • Experience working in healthcare, another regulated industry, or an environment with complex data, security, and compliance requirements.
  • Experience leading through organizational change, scaling engineering practices, or helping a growing engineering team mature its operating model.
  • Depending on domain, relevant experience may include:
    • Healthcare data and integration standards such as HL7, FHIR, EHR, PMS, or PBM integrations;
    • Experience with GraphQL, event-driven systems, APIs, or data pipelines;
    • Design systems, accessibility, frontend performance, or enterprise workflow design; or
    • Infrastructure as code, containerization, observability, and platform engineering at scale.

Application Instructions

Please indicate which domain best matches your experience: Consumer Experience, B2B Products and Portals, or Backend Platforms and Services. Candidates may be considered for more than one domain.

What we have to offer

  • The opportunity to grow alongside an early-stage company shaking up a big, old-fashioned industry.
  • Flexible time off, including 12 paid holidays.
  • 401k match plus 100% employer-provided medical, dental, and vision premiums.
  • Company contribution to Health Savings Account.
  • Stock options.

Prescryptive is committed to fair pay practices. The projected annual salary for this position is $220,000 to $275,000. When preparing an offer, we consider the candidate’s experience, depth of technical skills, experience in the healthcare industry, proven leadership success, scope of the assigned domain, interview feedback, internal equity, and location.

Prescryptive is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Prescryptive does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need.

jobs.description:
Madrigal is a biopharmaceutical company focused on delivering novel therapeutics for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a serious liver disease that can progress to cirrhosis, liver failure, need for liver transplantation and premature mortality. Every member of our Madrigal team is connected by our shared purpose: leading the fight against MASH.

Madrigal’s medication, Rezdiffra (resmetirom), is a once-daily, oral, liver-directed THR-β agonist designed to target key underlying causes of MASH. Rezdiffra is the first and only medication approved by both the FDA and European Commission for the treatment of MASH with moderate to advanced fibrosis (F2 to F3). An ongoing Phase 3 outcomes trial is evaluating Rezdiffra for the treatment of compensated MASH cirrhosis (F4c).

Our success is driven by our people. We are building a dynamic, inclusive, and high-performing culture that values scientific excellence, operational rigor, and collaboration. To support our continued growth, we are strengthening our workforce strategy to ensure we have the right talent, at the right time, in the right way.

Position Summary

This position will be responsible for GCP/Clinical Quality Assurance activities. The primary responsibilities will be to ensure quality and compliance of Madrigal-sponsored clinical trials with applicable GCP regulations, ICH GCP guidelines, Madrigal SOPs, and current industry standards and best practices. This position reports into the Senior Director, GCP Quality

Key Responsibilities

Strategy, Compliance and Oversight

  • May develop, implement, and/or maintain clinical quality systems and processes to ensure compliance with ICH GCP, FDA, EMA, and other global regulatory requirements
  • Ensure R&D clinical trial activities are compliant with ICH and applicable country regulations and guidelines and industry standards and best practices
  • Align organization to ICH in implementing a quality culture from the outset of clinical trials to promote patient safety and data integrity
  • Apply a risk-based approach by working collaboratively cross-functionally to ensure compliance
  • Attend routine internal and external clinical study team and ad hoc calls in support of ongoing quality oversight
  • Inform and escalate to management in real-time and/or during routine updates, as appropriate

Vendor and External Partner Quality Management

  • Engage partnership with external clinical trial vendors via adherence to Quality Agreements and routine meetings; may review Quality Agreements
  • Onboard, coordinate and/or manage services provided by external quality auditing partners (planning to closeout)
  • Assure through Qualification audits and oversight activities that clinical trial vendors are operating in compliance with all applicable procedures, study documents, regulations/guidelines
  • Review CDAs, MSAs or contract/Work Orders
  • Conduct or manage internal/external audits (clinical trial vendor, site, TMF, document, internal process) and prepare or review audit reports

Quality Events, CAPAs, and eQMS Management

  • Lead reviews, manage documentation, track and/or follow-up on Observations/Findings, CAPAs, Quality Event investigations, deviations, etc. through to closure
  • May lead quality investigations (QEs), including potential Serious Breach, Fraud/Misconduct, etc.
  • Support use of the eQMS via data entry/document upload of quality activities (audits, Findings/Observations and responses, inspections, CAPAs, SOP Deviations and updates, QEs/Investigations)
  • Perform/manage SOP reviews or updates, contribute to the annual audit plan and provide input (including metrics) to prepare for Quality Management Reviews

Clinical Documentation and Process Improvement

  • Review key clinical program or study documents, such as IBs, Protocols/Amendments, Consents, TMF Plans
  • May coordinate or manage inspection readiness activities across R&D functions; provide support during global agency inspections
  • Conduct or lead other tasks in support of GCP/Clinical Quality activities, including departmental process improvements
  • Stay abreast of applicable global regulations, guidance’s, and industry best practices
  • May manage studies across compounds/therapeutic area programs
  • Provide mentorship to other team members, as applicable

Preferred Qualifications

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in clinical quality assurance within the biopharmaceutical or CRO industry, to include auditing of clinical trial vendors, sites and/or TMFs or internal R&D process audits
  • Minimum 3-5 years of experience in a clinical operations role at a CRO or Sponsor, to include management of a study at a cross-functional level
  • Experience in inspection preparation and/or supporting health authority/regulatory agency inspections a plus
  • Overall qualification by experience to support the responsibilities not limited to those outlined above
  • Demonstrated GCP knowledge; GVP/GLP knowledge or certifications a plus
  • BS in a scientific or other relevant discipline with equivalent work experience

Key Competencies

  • Solid understanding of the cross-functional drug development process, including experience interacting with Operations, Data Management, Pharmacovigilance/Safety, Medical, Statistics/Programming, etc.
  • Skilled in developing collaborative internal and external relationships, ideally within a global organization
  • Business and Operational acumen to include escalation to management
  • Ability to interact with all levels within a global organization
  • Experience in using eQMS systems, such as Veeva

Madrigal offers a competitive Total Rewards strategy to attract and retain top talent and is inclusive of base pay, bonus, equity, and a generous benefits package. Full-time employees are eligible for base salary, bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits suite.

Base salary is determined by several factors including the candidate’s qualifications, skills, education, experience, business needs, and market demands. As of the date of this posting, a good faith estimate of the current pay scale for this position, applicable to all candidates, is $147,000 - $180,000 per year. We comply with all applicable minimum wage laws.

All full-time employees receive equity, which reinforces our ownership culture and offers meaningful opportunity for our employees to share in the success they help create. By aligning individual and company performance, we empower employees to think like owners, giving them a stake in the organization.

Full-time employees are also eligible for comprehensive benefits, including flexible paid time off, medical, dental, vision and life/disability insurance, and 401(k) offerings (i.e., traditional, Roth, and employer match) in accordance with applicable plans. We also offer additional voluntary benefits like supplemental life insurance, legal services, and other offerings. Background

The African Climate Foundation (ACF) is the first and only African-led climate change re-granting organisation on the continent. Through a combination of grant making, fellowships, transformational research, technical assistance, coalition building and advocacy the ACF seeks to support interventions at the nexus of climate change, and development that have the greatest potential to deliver long-term socio-economic transformation and inclusive development. ACF also provides Fiscal Hosting (also called Fiscal Sponsorship) services to support emerging and mission aligned organisations and initiatives.

About the Transport Programme

The ACF Transport Programme supports an African-led transition to clean, safe, affordable and accessible transport. It works on the policy, finance and public support needed to move people and goods more sustainably, and treats electric mobility as one part of a wider shift that also covers public and popular transport such as buses and minibus taxis. Working with governments, financial institutions, civil society, research partners and the private sector, the programme combines grant-making, technical assistance, research, convening and advocacy. It also collaborates with partners and global initiatives, so that African priorities shape how transport systems are planned and financed.

Purpose

Reporting to Transport Programme Manager, the Senior Programme Officer will play a pivotal role in implementing the Transport Programme’s Africa strategy, supporting the Programme Manager to deliver a continent-wide mobility transition. The role is suited for someone with a deep understanding of Africa’s transport and energy landscape, strong project management skills, and a passion for accelerating climate and industrial transformation.

Responsibilities include but not limited to:

Strategy and Implementation

  • Support the Programme Manager in the implementation of the Transport Strategy across focus countries and expansion geographies.
  • Identify and oversee sector-relevant research and analysis to inform programmatic work and ensure evidence-based decision-making.
  • Collaborate closely with other ACF programme staff to ensure synergies, integration, and cross-programme learning.
  • Work with the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) Manager to ensure effective monitoring, reporting, and evaluation of programme delivery and outcomes.
  • Ensure alignment of in-country activities and objectives.
  • Contribute to the design and refinement of national and regional EV roadmaps, policy frameworks, and implementation plans.

Partnerships

  • Develop and maintain strong working relationships and networks with key stakeholders, including national and sub-national governments, financial institutions, civil society organizations, think tanks, research institutions, and the philanthropic community.
  • Act as a key point of contact and representative of the Transport Programme, strengthening stakeholder collaboration to enhance programme impact.
  • Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with government agencies, civil society partners, multilateral institutions, and technical collaborators.
  • Represent ACF in strategic meetings, workshops, and regional convenings.
  • Monitor and advise on key developments in EV and sustainable transport policy, investment, and regulation in priority countries.

Grant-Making

  • Under the guidance of the Programme Manager, update, maintain and implement the programme’s grant-making portfolio.
  • Collaborate with ACF’s grant-making team to manage the grant cycle, including soliciting, reviewing, and recommending grants to the ACF Grants Committee and Board, and supporting grant contracting and monitoring.
  • Monitor grantee progress, ensuring timely delivery against grant agreements and providing technical and management support where needed.
  • Under the guidance of the Programme Manager, work closely with the MEL Manager to ensure grants are being monitored, information captured, and learnings are being used to inform programming.
  • Assist in reviewing grant proposals, developing work plans and KPIs, and supporting grantees to deliver impact.

Fundraising and Reporting

  • Support the Programme Manager, the Head of Strategic Partnerships, and the Head of Programmes in developing and implementing fundraising strategies to address programme funding gaps.
  • Support in the preparation of funding proposals and donor engagements.
  • Ensure timely and high-quality reporting on programme progress to donors, the ACF Board, and other key stakeholders.

Thought Leadership

  • Stay abreast of current developments to inform development and implementation of the Transport Strategy.
  • Contribute to ACF’s research outputs, knowledge-sharing initiatives, and online content, ensuring high visibility of the Transport Programme
  • Collaborate with the Communications Team and the Programme Manager to organize events, such as convenings, webinars, and workshops.
  • Provide technical guidance and insights to the Senior Management Team, Board, and other internal and external stakeholders on strategic programme developments.

Requirements include but are not limited to:

  • Master’s degree or equivalent in economics, environmental sciences, development studies, public policy, or a related field.
  • 6-8 years of progressive experience in programme design, management, or related roles, with a focus on climate action, sustainable development, transport, clean energy, climate policy, or similar fields.
  • Experience working with or supporting government institutions, donors, and financial entities on large-scale projects or policy initiatives.
  • Solid understanding of electric mobility trends, regulatory frameworks, and industrial policy in Africa and some basic knowledge of enabling policies for the large-scale electrification of cars, trucks, buses, and 2/3-wheelers and the global clean energy transition
  • Strong experience in managing grants.
  • Familiarity with policy advocacy and stakeholder engagement within the African context.
  • Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to design and implement complex programmes.
  • Sophisticated writing, reporting, and communication skills, with an ability to present technical information clearly.
  • Fluency in English.
  • Excellent organizational and time management abilities, with a capacity to prioritize tasks and meet deadlines.
  • High levels of professionalism, integrity, and attention to detail.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, remote, multicultural team environment.
  • Able to travel internationally to join events or engagements when required.
  • Fluency in French would be a strong advantage.

Start date: Position available immediately.

Location: South Africa. ACF’s operational hub is in Cape Town, South Africa. Remote working will be considered for candidates based on the African continent.

Contract duration: 12 months (renewable based on mutual agreement).

jobs.description:
Washington Rural Healthcare Finance and Revenue Cycle Leadership Opportunities

Rural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, and community healthcare organizations throughout Washington to identify experienced finance and revenue cycle leaders who understand the unique realities of rural healthcare.

We are currently connecting with professionals who may be interested in active and upcoming finance, accounting, reimbursement, revenue cycle, billing, coding, and patient financial services leadership opportunities across Washington.

These opportunities may include leadership within Critical Access Hospitals, rural and community hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, Federally Qualified Health Centers, public hospital districts, long-term care organizations, and integrated rural healthcare systems.

This Is More Than a Finance Role

Strong financial and revenue cycle operations help protect healthcare access for an entire rural community.

These leaders ensure organizations can accurately capture revenue, manage resources responsibly, support employees, maintain compliance, and remain financially strong enough to continue caring for the people who depend on them.

In a rural healthcare organization, finance and revenue cycle leaders often work across departments and may have broader responsibilities than they would in a larger system. The strongest leaders understand how registration, coding, billing, reimbursement, patient accounts, accounting, and operational decisions connect to one another.

They are collaborative, detail-oriented, approachable, and able to turn complex financial information into practical guidance for employees, department leaders, executives, and governing boards.

Opportunities May Include

This application may connect you with current or upcoming roles such as:

  • Controller
  • Assistant Controller
  • Finance Director or Manager
  • Accounting Director or Manager
  • Revenue Cycle Director or Manager
  • Patient Financial Services Director or Manager
  • Patient Accounts Manager
  • Business Office Director or Manager
  • Billing Director or Manager
  • Coding Director, Manager, or Supervisor
  • Health Information Management revenue cycle leadership
  • Reimbursement Director or Manager
  • Chargemaster or Charge Description Master leadership
  • Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable leadership
  • Payroll leadership
  • Senior Billing, Coding, or Patient Accounts supervisory roles

What You May Lead

Responsibilities will vary by organization and position and may include:

  • Leading accounting, finance, revenue cycle, billing, coding, or patient financial services functions
  • Supporting accurate and timely financial reporting
  • Managing month-end and year-end close processes
  • Developing budgets, forecasts, and financial performance reports
  • Strengthening billing, collections, cash flow, and reimbursement performance
  • Monitoring key revenue cycle metrics and identifying opportunities for improvement
  • Supporting accurate coding, charge capture, claims submission, and payment posting
  • Overseeing patient accounts, financial counseling, and collection processes
  • Ensuring compliance with payer, regulatory, accounting, and documentation requirements
  • Preparing for financial, coding, billing, or compliance audits
  • Developing policies, procedures, workflows, and internal controls
  • Training and supporting finance and revenue cycle employees
  • Collaborating with clinical, operational, IT, HIM, and executive leaders
  • Helping employees understand how their work affects organizational sustainability
  • Supporting system implementations, process improvements, or departmental restructuring

What You Will Bring

Qualifications will vary by opportunity, but organizations may seek:

  • Progressive experience in healthcare finance, accounting, revenue cycle, billing, coding, reimbursement, or patient financial services
  • Previous leadership experience as a director, manager, controller, supervisor, or comparable leader
  • Knowledge of healthcare reimbursement, payer requirements, billing practices, and financial operations
  • Experience with Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and patient-pay accounts
  • An understanding of hospital, clinic, or healthcare-system workflows
  • Experience analyzing financial or revenue cycle performance and communicating findings to leadership
  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, and team-development skills
  • Experience with Critical Access Hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, FQHCs, public hospital districts, or community healthcare organizations
  • Relevant education or professional credentials based on the position
  • A collaborative and relationship-focused leadership style

Some opportunities may prefer credentials such as CPA, CHFP, CRCR, CPC, CCS, RHIA, RHIT, or other finance, coding, revenue cycle, or health information certifications. Requirements will depend on the specific role.

Why Rural Washington?

Washington's rural healthcare organizations serve communities surrounded by mountains, forests, farmland, rivers, islands, and coastlines. These organizations frequently operate with lean teams, limited resources, and a tremendous responsibility to the communities they serve.

Finance and revenue cycle leadership in a rural organization provides the opportunity to see the direct impact of your work. Improving a process, supporting a team, or strengthening reimbursement can help preserve services, protect jobs, and keep care available close to home.

Join the RSS Rural Talent Network

By applying through this page, you are joining the confidential Rural Staffing Services talent network. You may be considered for current or upcoming finance and revenue cycle leadership opportunities that align with your background, goals, location preferences, and availability.

Please include your résumé and let us know:

  • Which Washington communities or regions you would consider
  • Whether you are open to relocation
  • Whether you are interested in permanent, interim, remote, fractional, or multiple types of opportunities
  • Which areas best match your experience, such as accounting, finance, billing, coding, reimbursement, patient accounts, or full revenue cycle
  • Your experience with rural hospitals, Critical Access Hospitals, public hospital districts, FQHCs, or community healthcare organizations
  • Which position or community you were viewing on RSSJobs.org

Our team personally reviews each application. When we identify an opportunity that may be a strong match, we will contact you directly to share more about the organization, community, responsibilities, and next steps.

Your information will be handled professionally and confidentially.

Revenue Systems owns the go-to-market technology stack at Greenhouse, from first outreach through renewal. As a Senior Revenue Systems Specialist, you’ll own systems work across both pre-sale and post-sale: Salesforce, our sales system of record, and the platforms our Customer Success and Customer Marketing teams work from every day, currently Gainsight and Accord. Breadth is a key aspect of this role, and you’ll have real latitude to shape where the stack goes next.

Who will love this job

  • A solutions-orientedpartner - you can hear what the business is trying to accomplish and turn it into something that works, and you stay with a problem until the desired outcome is achieved
  • A curious builder - you want to understand why a process exists before you automate it, and you’re comfortable saying when something doesn’t seem to make sense, including to the people asking for it
  • An owner - you take a project from first conversation through rollout and adoption without needing it project-managed for you
  • An AI-fluent operator - you already use tools like Claude, Glean, or ChatGPT in your day to day, and you’re interested in what they can do inside a revenue stack

What you’ll do

  • Own and build solutions in Salesforce, including data model design, declarative automation, validation, permissions, page layouts, and reporting, taking projects from scoping and intake through rollout, adoption, and documentation
  • Administer our post-sale platforms, including Gainsight and Accord, alongside our Customer Success Operations team, covering the rules engine, journey and email programs, surveys including NPS, and the workflows behind customer health scoring, CSM assignment, and account transfers
  • Own integrations between Salesforce, Gainsight, and the rest of the stack, standing up new ones independently and eliminating the recurring failures that come with the existing ones
  • Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Customer Marketing on their requests, working out whether the fix belongs in a system or somewhere else, and seeing it through to a working solution either way
  • Lead platform migration and consolidation work as our tech stack changes, from evaluation and vendor assessment through data movement, cutover, and adoption
  • Hold a point of view on where the stack should go, surfacing the opportunities and the risks in our implementation rather than waiting to be asked
  • Document what you build, and bring request volume down over time through automation and self-service
  • Additional projects and responsibilities as business needs require

You should have

  • Several years in revenue operations, customer success operations, business systems, or platform administration.
  • B2B SaaS experience.
  • Deep hands-on Salesforce administration experience: data model design, declarative automation, permissions and sharing, reporting, and the judgment to know when not to build. You should be comfortable making medium to large changes to a production org and reasoning about the performance and scale implications of your configuration choices.
  • Hands-on ownership of Gainsight or a comparable post-sale platform (e.g., Totango, ChurnZero, Planhat), with enough depth to configure independently and to hold a credible view on whether the platform is serving the business.
  • Experience standing up integrations without support, and a record of eliminating recurring failures rather than only resolving them.
  • Experience owning a platform migration or consolidation end to end, including the data movement.
  • A track record of taking a problem from the first report through to a working solution.
  • Comfort operating as the most knowledgeable person in the room on a platform, and the instinct to bring others along rather than becoming the only one who can do the work.
  • Clear writing. A real part of this job is explaining to a non-technical stakeholder what you built and how to use it, or what went wrong and what you did about it.
  • Experience across more than one post-sale platform is a plus. So is exposure to Salesforce CPQ, enrichment tooling like Clay, or building with MCP and agentic tooling against enterprise systems.
  • Your own unique talents! Your background has given you a unique perspective and set of transferable skills that aren’t always in alignment with a given role, but those are qualities we value at Greenhouse. About the Role

As a Senior or Staff DevOps Engineer at Trase, you will build, deploy, and operate the infrastructure supporting Red Cell Federal and Red Cell Partners’ incubations and portfolio companies. You will join Trase's dedicated RCF/RCP support team, with a strong focus on federal, government, and national security programs.

Red Cell Partners is an investment and incubation firm that builds and supports technology companies, including Trase. Red Cell Federal is our federal-focused partner within that ecosystem. This role helps RCF and other RCP partner companies adopt and operate Trase OS in their own environments.

This is a hands-on engineering role spanning partner onboarding, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, secure releases, observability, and production support. You will work directly with partner engineers, Trase's dedicated software engineers and TPM, Platform Engineering, and GRC to turn requirements into validated deployments and dependable operations.

The level will reflect the candidate's experience and demonstrated scope. Senior engineers will independently deliver and support complex partner deployments. Staff engineers will also lead architecture across partner environments, establish reusable standards, and mentor engineers.

Why this Role is Needed

RCF and RCP companies need secure, repeatable deployments across commercial and government cloud, private networks, and on-premises infrastructure. Their requirements span installation, integrations, hardening, upgrades, incident response, and ongoing vulnerability remediation.

This role provides dedicated engineering ownership from environment readiness through sustained operations. You will make deployments easier to install, validate, upgrade, and support, while turning recurring partner needs into reusable capabilities with Trase's platform team.

What You'll Do

  • Build and operate RCF/RCP partner environments across AWS, Azure, GCP, and customer-controlled or on-premises infrastructure, adapting to each program's access, networking, and security requirements.
  • Package and validate Trase OS services and dependencies using Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and approved registries. Maintain complete, versioned image inventories, release manifests, and image digests so partner deliveries contain the required artifacts.
  • Create reusable infrastructure-as-code modules, cluster bootstrap automation, and CI/CD or GitOps workflows using Terraform, Pulumi, Argo CD, or comparable tools.
  • Prepare and validate networking, IAM, secrets, certificates, storage, registries, and model-provider connectivity. Support restricted-network and disconnected deployment patterns where required, in partnership with application engineers.
  • Remove or abstract cloud-specific dependencies that block partner deployments. Validate representative agent workflows end to end, including service integrations, authentication, model access, and persistent state.
  • Own technical triage and troubleshooting for partner deployment and production issues across application services, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, and networks. Coordinate fixes and escalations with named owners and verify resolution with partners.
  • Deliver tested releases, patches, and upgrades with automated validation gates, version compatibility checks, smoke tests, rollback procedures, and clear release notes. Confirm the deployed artifacts match the approved release.
  • Operate metrics, logs, traces, audit logging, dashboards, alerts, and SLOs for partner environments. Support incident response, recovery, capacity planning, and reliability improvements.
  • Partner with GRC and RCF security teams on container hardening, vulnerability scanning, CVE remediation, SBOMs, and engineering evidence for applicable STIG, RMF/ATO, and impact-level requirements. Verify fixes through rescanning and deployment validation; coordinate exceptions and approvals with security owners.
  • Support sustainment of federal deployments, including Second Front where applicable, through patching, image updates, configuration changes, and ongoing security remediation within agreed Trase/partner responsibilities.
  • Maintain deployment guides, environment inventories, operational runbooks, and troubleshooting documentation. Provide partner onboarding, knowledge transfer, and operational handoffs with clear prerequisites, access boundaries, and support ownership.

Technical leadership

  • Lead infrastructure and reliability decisions across RCF/RCP engagements, keeping partner-specific requirements aligned with Trase's shared architecture.
  • Set practical standards for secure releases, production readiness, observability, and support handoffs across partner environments.
  • Work with the TPM, Product, GRC, and partner teams to clarify requirements, validate acceptance criteria, estimate work, and surface risks and dependencies before making commitments.
  • Turn recurring partner deployment and support needs into reusable automation and platform improvements.
  • Mentor engineers and partner teams, document decisions, and reduce reliance on individual experts for ongoing operations.

Required Qualifications

  • U.S. citizenship is required.
  • 10+ years of software, platform, infrastructure, SRE, or DevOps engineering experience, including hands-on ownership of production systems.
  • Deep hands-on experience with Linux, Docker, Kubernetes, and production cluster operations.
  • Strong experience with Helm and infrastructure as code, such as Terraform or Pulumi, including reusable modules, state management, testing, and change review.
  • Hands-on infrastructure experience with at least two of AWS, Azure, and GCP, including compute, networking, storage, identity, and managed services.
  • Experience deploying and operating software in customer-controlled, private-cloud, hybrid-cloud, or on-premises environments, including adapting cloud-native products for these deployment models.
  • Strong understanding of networking, DNS, ingress, load balancing, certificates, IAM, secrets management, persistent storage, and service-to-service security.
  • Experience operating CI/CD or GitOps systems for releases, upgrades, and rollbacks, plus observability and incident response for production services.
  • Strong software engineering and automation skills in Python, Go, TypeScript, or a similar language, with the ability to work across application and infrastructure layers.
  • Experience hardening production infrastructure and container images, investigating vulnerability findings, and delivering validated security fixes with security teams.
  • Strong partner-facing communication and troubleshooting skills, with ownership of technical issues from initial report through validated resolution and operational handoff.
  • Demonstrated experience using AI-assisted coding and engineering tools to accelerate development, infrastructure automation, troubleshooting, operational analysis, or incident investigation.

Strongly Preferred

  • Prior SRE, DevOps, or infrastructure engineering experience supporting national security, defense, federal agencies, or other government programs.
  • An active U.S. government security clearance.
  • Experience operating in restricted-network, disconnected, regulated, or security-sensitive environments.
  • Hands-on familiarity with STIG hardening, NIST controls, FedRAMP, RMF/ATO evidence, or DoD IL4/IL5/IL6 deployment requirements, as applicable to assigned programs.
  • Experience with government cloud infrastructure, including AWS GovCloud, and federal deployment platforms such as Second Front/Game Warden.
  • Experience with software supply-chain security, SBOMs, artifact signing, FIPS-enabled components, Harbor, or policy as code.
  • Experience supporting long-running, stateful, data-intensive, AI/ML, or GPU-enabled workloads.
  • Customer-facing, partner engineering, or forward-deployed experience supporting multiple organizations and transferring operational knowledge.

Up to 20% travel may be required.

If you want to be on the cutting edge of technology, building AI solutions for the future, and are up for a challenge, let’s talk!

For full-time roles

  • Identify root causes of performance gaps (skills, knowledge, process or tools) and recommend targeted fixes.

Develop the team

  • Run one-to-one and team call and deal reviews, role-plays (including AI-simulated buyers and objections), live call observation and product knowledge checks.
  • Build individual development plans and coach sales representatives on specific sales behaviors.
  • Coach team leads to apply shared quality criteria in daily work with their teams.

Track results

  • Track whether new behaviors and AI workflows are applied in real deals and how they affect conversion, deal outcomes and time spent.

Standards and CRM

  • Audit existing sales standards for gaps, contradictions and requirements that don’t help the sale.
  • Write and update sales standards: scripts, objection guides, follow-up rules, contact quality criteria and product instructions, as well as CRM stage rules — the goal, entry and exit criteria, required data, sales representative actions and next steps for each stage, ownership at handover, and SLAs agreed with the process owner (response time, working hours, exceptions and escalation).
  • Pilot and roll out new standards: incorporate feedback from sales representatives and team leads, agree commercial rules with sales leadership, write requirements for CRM fields, prompts, notifications, reports and automation, take part in acceptance testing, and train sales representatives after changes.
  • Monitor adherence to standards in the CRM: overdue tasks, missing next steps, unconfirmed stage moves, missing loss reasons and handover quality.

AI in sales work

  • Build reusable AI workflows for sales representatives and team leads (call and meeting preparation, meeting summaries, follow-up messages, discovery question planning and checking proposals against client and product data), train sales teams to use them, observe real usage and fix errors.
  • Work with AI agents and bots; maintain instructions, templates and knowledge-base materials.
  • Use AI to help sales representatives plan next steps in the CRM, making sure they review every AI-drafted message or data update before it goes to a client or changes key deal information.

Build enablement assets

  • Build and maintain the team skills map, call and deal scorecard, prioritized list of loss reasons and a library of examples and exercises.

Requirements

  • Experience in sales enablement, sales coaching or sales development in a comparable market, with personal responsibility for identifying gaps in sales representatives’ performance.
  • Experience with a complex physical product with a long sales cycle, ideally in architectural glass, interior systems or a related field.
  • Deep understanding of the full B2B/B2C sales cycle, including negotiation, closing and repeat sales.
  • Strong understanding of both phone sales and in-person sales in a showroom.
  • Strong call and deal review skills: specific feedback, structured practice and verification that skills transfer to real work; experience coaching team leads to apply shared quality criteria.
  • Experience writing sales standards and driving their adoption through team leads and sales representatives, without direct authority over the sales team; clear and concise writing; strong team player.
  • Confident CRM use at the level of funnel, stages, tasks, ownership, SLAs and data quality; ability to write change requirements.
  • Proven, hands-on use of AI in sales work, with at least one implemented workflow showing a clear task, data, personal contribution, users and result. Fluent with AI tools, structured instructions, files and knowledge bases, and able to train others to use them; experience with any specific AI product is not required.
  • Strong analytical skills: able to measure the impact of new tools and processes with before/after comparison, compare conversion rates on a like-for-like basis (same funnel stage, period and lead sources), recognize when there is too little data for a reliable conclusion, and be clear about what the numbers do and do not prove.
  • Fluent English (C1/C2).

Benefits

  • Competitive base salary + performance-based bonuses.
  • Full ownership of the sales enablement function in a fast-growing U.S. company, with the freedom to build it the right way.
  • Direct influence on how the sales team sells, with results visible in conversion and deal outcomes.
  • Hands-on work with AI in real sales processes, not pilots that stay on paper.
  • Joining a highly professional and dynamic team.
  • Exciting experience working with prestigious clients in the US market.

What are we actually trying to solve?

What matters most?

Curiosity over certainty.

This Opportunity

This role is an Applied AI engineer embedded with one business team, the way a site reliability engineer sits inside a product team: your line manager, your code reviewers and your career path come from Applied AI; your backlog and your day come from the team you serve. The engineering standards are Applied AI's; the tempo is Growth's.

What you will own

  • The GTM workflows in production. The outbound orchestrator and its sequences, the campaign builder, the intent-signal routine, the enrichment and signal pipelines, and the paid-media loop. You know how each one runs, what it costs, and what to do when it breaks.
  • Review steps before anything sends. Agents that check the list, confirm each signal is current, and review the copy before a sequence goes out, with sampled human sign-off.
  • The learning loop. Replies and meetings booked feed back into who we contact and what we say. You instrument the sends, run A/B tests on variants, and show the Growth team which messaging is working.
  • Signals and enrichment. The pipelines that bring third-party signals and first-party behavior into Snowflake, the fields the Growth team needs exposed through our MCP tools, and the work with our data engineers that gets them there.
  • Skills and routines for sellers. The Claude skills the Growth Associates and AEs run each morning, the campaign tooling, and the short working sessions that get a new team using them.
  • Deliverability and suppression. One set of contact rules every sender reads, warm-inbox discipline, and the suppression windows that keep us welcome in people's inboxes.
  • Engineering standards on your estate. Version control, alerting, tracing, runbooks and documented handover for every workflow you run, and a steady move of those workflows onto the Firn factory framework.
  • The weekly cadence. A standing backlog with the Director of Growth, priorities set by pipeline, and a short written account of what shipped and what it did. When a priority and an engineering standard conflict, the Director of Growth and the Senior Director of Applied AI settle it together.

We would love to hear from you if you have
  • Written software that runs in production. Python and SQL are your working languages, you use git every day, and when you meet a new API you read the docs and use it. Tools like n8n, Clay or Zapier are in your kit, and when they run out you write the code.
  • Built with LLMs for real work. Prompts, tools, structured outputs and evaluation, and the failure modes of each. You know what a model does when a prompt does not say where to get its data, and you design against it.
  • Run something that could not go down. Alerting, error handling, retries and recovery are habits, and when something does fail you fix the class of problem, not the instance.
  • Moved data into a warehouse. You have built or maintained pipelines into Snowflake or an equivalent, and you can model a table in dbt or learn to quickly.
  • Sat with sellers and marketers. You can take a growth director's ask, work out what they need, and come back with something they use the next week. When an ask is a symptom of a broken process, you say so before you build it.
  • A fast tempo. The team you serve measures in meetings booked per week. You are measured on what you build: whether it runs, what it costs, and what it changed for the team. You ship small, measure, and say plainly when something is not working.
  • An AI-native way of working you can show us. A workflow, automation or agent you built and still use. Expect to demonstrate it during the interview process.
  • Comfort being embedded. You can sit inside another team, take its priorities, and still hold the engineering standards your own team sets.
Bonus points for
  • Experience with Salesforce, Apollo, Smartlead, Lemlist or similar GTM tooling and their APIs.
  • Experience with email deliverability at volume.
  • Experience with paid-media platform APIs.

How we hire for this role

The interview process includes a short technical exercise in code and a working session where you walk us through how you work with AI on a real task, using your own setup. We work this way ourselves, and you are welcome to use AI when applying.

What you get in return for being awesome

  • Competitive Base Salary

  • 401k
  • MacBook and home office equipment allowance

jobs.excerpt: Gordian is evolving how we build and manage products, moving toward durable product teams with clearer business accountability, stronger customer orientation, faster learning cycles, and increasingly AI-enabled ways of working.
jobs.description:
Gordian is evolving how we build and manage products, moving toward durable product teams with clearer business accountability, stronger customer orientation, faster learning cycles, and increasingly AI-enabled ways of working.

The Director of Product Operations will build and run the operating system for the Product organization.

This leader will translate product strategy into repeatable mechanisms for planning, prioritization, execution, measurement and learning. The role will connect Product, Engineering, Design and our go-to-market organizations so that teams have the standards, insights, tools and operating rhythms required to deliver measurable customer and business outcomes.

This is not a traditional PMO role. Success is not measured by producing status reports or administering process. It is measured by whether product teams make better decisions, execute with greater speed and predictability, and deliver stronger outcomes.

The role anchors the Product Center of Excellence and partners closely with Product Unit leaders, Engineering Leaders and the CPO to continuously improve how Gordian builds products.

What You Will Own

1. Product Operating System & xDLC

Own and continuously improve Gordian's product development lifecycle and operating model from idea through discovery, development, launch, adoption and iteration.

  • Establish a simple, scalable xDLC spanning Product, Engineering and Design.
  • Define the minimum standards, decision points and artifacts required at each lifecycle stage.
  • Create clear mechanisms for moving ideas from strategic opportunity through validation, investment and delivery.
  • Reduce unnecessary handoffs, meetings and process overhead.
  • Drive adoption of AI-native workflows that improve product discovery, analysis, documentation and execution.

The objective is greater velocity of learning, not more process.

2. Portfolio Planning & Investment Governance

Create the mechanisms that connect company strategy to product investment.

  • Run the annual and quarterly product planning processes.
  • Establish consistent prioritization and investment frameworks across product units.
  • Provide portfolio-level visibility into strategic initiatives, investment, capacity, risks and expected outcomes.
  • Facilitate portfolio trade-off decisions with Product and Technology leadership.
  • Maintain clear decision records and accountability for major product investments.
  • Ensure teams can clearly connect roadmap investments to customer, strategic and financial outcomes.

3. Product Performance & Analytics

Create a single, trusted view of product performance.

Partner with Product Unit leaders, Finance and Technology to define and operationalize metrics such as:

  • Product adoption and engagement
  • High Value Actions
  • New Product Revenue and recurring revenue contribution
  • Customer outcomes
  • Product delivery effectiveness
  • Discovery and learning velocity
  • Roadmap investment and capacity
  • Product quality and operational health

Turn these measures into actionable insights for Product leadership rather than simply creating dashboards.

4. Product Management Excellence

Build the systems that make every Gordian Product Manager better.

  • Establish common Product Management expectations, competencies and career frameworks.
  • Standardize essential product practices while preserving autonomy within product units.
  • Create reusable methods and playbooks for discovery, VOC, segmentation, business cases, prioritization, roadmaps and product measurement.
  • Build onboarding and ongoing development programs for PMs.
  • Establish communities of practice that accelerate learning across product units.
  • Partner with Product leadership on capability assessment and organizational development.

5. Product & Engineering Operating Rhythm

Partner closely with Technology leadership to create a common Product + Engineering operating cadence.

  • Establish portfolio and product-unit reviews focused on outcomes, decisions, risks and learning.
  • Create transparency into commitments, dependencies and delivery health.
  • Identify systemic bottlenecks and continuously improve how work flows through the organization.
  • Partner on appropriate delivery and engineering effectiveness measures.
  • Ensure executive reviews focus on decisions and intervention rather than status reporting.

6. Product Tooling & AI Enablement

Own the strategy for the Product organization's operating toolchain.

  • Simplify and rationalize product-management tools, workflows and data.
  • Establish common information architecture and governance.
  • Automate repetitive product-management and reporting work wherever practical.
  • Drive adoption of AI-enabled product workflows.
  • Experiment with new methods that meaningfully increase PM leverage and organizational learning.

7. Product Operations Team Leadership

Lead and develop the Product Operations organization.

  • Set a clear charter and priorities for Product Operations.
  • Develop the capabilities of the team.
  • Clarify which activities should be centralized versus embedded within product units.
  • Eliminate low-value administrative activity.
  • Build a high-leverage team that improves the effectiveness of the broader Product organization.

What Success Looks Like

Strategy is executable.
Every major product investment has a clear customer problem, business outcome, owner and measure of success.

Leaders can see the portfolio.
The CPO, CTO and Business Unit leaders have reliable visibility into investment, progress, risks, capacity and outcomes.

Teams spend less time managing process.
Operating mechanisms remove friction rather than introduce bureaucracy.

Product decisions become evidence-driven.
Customer insights, product usage, commercial performance and delivery data inform prioritization.

Product + Engineering operate as one system.
Planning, delivery and measurement are shared rather than operating through functional handoffs.

PM capability rises.
PMs have clear expectations, modern tools, consistent methods and strong development pathways.

AI materially changes how Product works.
AI becomes embedded in discovery, synthesis, specification, analysis, documentation and operating workflows rather than existing as an isolated experiment.

What You Bring Required

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in Product Management, Product Operations, product strategy, technical program management or comparable software leadership roles.
  • Experience building or scaling Product Operations within a complex software or technology organization.
  • Demonstrated experience designing product operating models, planning processes and portfolio governance.
  • Strong understanding of modern product discovery, product development and product measurement practices.
  • Experience working closely with Product, Engineering, UX/Research, Finance, Sales and Customer Success.
  • Strong analytical capability and demonstrated ability to turn fragmented operational and product data into executive-level insight.
  • Experience influencing senior leaders and driving organizational change without relying solely on positional authority.
  • Strong executive communication skills and an ability to simplify complex organizational problems.
  • Experience leading and developing high-performing teams.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred

  • B2B SaaS experience.
  • Experience transforming a product organization from project/delivery orientation toward persistent product teams and outcome ownership.
  • Experience implementing product analytics and product performance frameworks.
  • Experience building Product Management competency and career frameworks.
  • Experience with AI-enabled product-development workflows.
  • Experience operating across a portfolio containing both mature products and new growth businesses.
  • Experience in construction technology, facilities management, capital planning, procurement or adjacent markets is helpful but not required.

Fortive Corporation Overview

Fortive's essential technology makes the world safer and more productive. We accelerate transformation in high-impact fields like workplace safety, build environments, and healthcare.

We are a global industrial technology innovator with a startup spirit. Our forward-looking companies lead the way in healthcare sterilization, industrial safety, predictive maintenance, and other mission-critical solutions. We're a force for progress, working alongside our customers and partners to solve challenges on a global scale, from workplace safety in the most demanding conditions to advanced technologies that help providers focus on exceptional patient care.

We are a diverse team 10,000 strong, united by a dynamic, inclusive culture and energized by limitless learning and growth. We use the proven Fortive Business System (FBS) to accelerate our positive impact.

At Fortive, we believe in you. We believe in your potential—your ability to learn, grow, and make a difference.

At Fortive, we believe in us. We believe in the power of people working together to solve problems no one could solve alone.

At Fortive, we believe in growth. We're honest about what's working and what isn't, and we never stop improving and innovating.

Fortive: For you, for us, for growth.

About Gordian

Gordian is the world’s leading provider of facility and construction cost data, software and services for all phases of the building lifecycle. A pioneer of Job Order Contracting (JOC), Gordian’s offerings also include our proprietary RSMeans data and Sightlines Facility Intelligence solutions. From planning to design, procurement, construction and operations, Gordian’s solutions help clients maximize efficiency, optimize cost savings and increase building quality. Gordian is a part of the international business group Fortive, with 26,000 people employed worldwide.We offer an excellent benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life and LTD insurance, HSA, and a 401(k) retirement plan. EOE/AA/M/F/Vets/Disabled.

We Are an Equal Opportunity Employer. Fortive Corporation and all Fortive Companies are proud to be equal opportunity employers. We value and encourage diversity and solicit applications from all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, age, marital status, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or other characteristics protected by law. Fortive and all Fortive Companies are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. Individuals who need a reasonable accommodation because of a disability for any part of the employment application process, please contact us at .

Pay Range
The salary range for this position (in local currency) is 133,600.00 - 248,500.00.

Base pay offered may vary depending on various factors, including, but not limited to: job-related knowledge; skills; experience; and other eligibility factors such as geographic location. The Total Rewards package includes competitive base pay and an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs, generally including health insurance, flexible spending accounts, health savings accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance programs, and several programs that provide for both paid and unpaid time away from work.

jobs.description:
The Role

Unit4 serves a global community of professional services organizations - management consultancies, engineering and architectural practices, IT services firms, audit and advisory, and legal services. These businesses run on people: utilization, engagement profitability, and project delivery define how they win or lose. As Product Director for Professional Services, you own the vertical product vision, strategy, and roadmap that makes Unit4 the ERP of choice for mid-market PSOs.

This is not a generalist PM role with an industry overlay. You will have dedicated engineering capacity to build genuine vertical depth in the platform - industry-specific capabilities that horizontal product teams cannot and will not build. You will work in close partnership with horizontal PMs across Financials, HR, Projects, and Procurement to ensure the full platform delivers for PSOs end-to-end. You own the backlog, the outcomes, the roadmap, and the commercial case for why your vertical wins.

AI is actively reshaping how professional services firms operate. The automation of billable work, the compression of traditional T&M models, and the shift toward outcome- and subscription-based pricing are rewriting the economics of the sector. The right candidate understands where these firms are in that journey and what it means for the software they need. You have built enterprise software for PSOs, you know what the best solutions in this space do well and where they fall short, and you can translate an industry in transition into a product roadmap that stays ahead of it.

What You'll Do

  • Own the Professional Services product vision, strategy, and multi-horizon roadmap; align it with Unit4's platform strategy and commercial growth targets.
  • Own feature outcomes, not just delivery — define clear adoption, usage, and customer impact goals for every capability you champion, and track performance against them after launch.
  • Serve as the internal authority on the Professional Services vertical, providing product, marketing, analyst relations, and pre-sales teams with the industry grounding they need to position, demonstrate, and sell effectively.
  • Lead a prioritized product backlog with dedicated engineering capacity - defining outcomes, success metrics, release plans, and quality criteria.
  • Translate deep PSO market knowledge into specific, investment-backed product requirements: opportunity sizing, problem statements, and build-vs-partner decisions.
  • Define industry-specific solution blueprints, reference configurations, and pre-built templates that accelerate customer time-to-value.
  • Act as the vertical voice in planning conversations with horizontal product teams, ensuring PSO requirements are reflected in platform investment.
  • Partner with the Industry Growth Director on launch readiness, pricing, packaging, and field enablement for new capabilities.
  • Engage directly with strategic customers and the PS Industry Board to validate roadmap direction, co-innovate, and generate outcome evidence.
  • Monitor the competitive landscape - know what NetSuite, Workday, Deltek, Kantata, and others are shipping and what it means for Unit4's positioning.
  • Work with partners to extend the value proposition for PSO customers.

What You'll Bring

  • Proven product management experience building enterprise software - ERP, PSA, or enterprise SaaS - for professional services organizations. You have shipped products used by PSOs, not just advised on them.
  • Deep operational knowledge of how PSOs run: pipeline-to-resource-to-revenue, utilization and leverage economics, engagement profitability, billing models, and partner/shareholder economics.
  • Strong command of the core PSO processes your product will need to support: project accounting and billing (including the evolving invoicing landscape as AI reshapes service delivery), project planning and execution, time and expense management, and resource planning across the full jobs-to-be-done of a mid-market professional services firm.
  • A clear point of view on where AI is taking the professional services business model - from the automation of billable work to the rise of outcome- and subscription-based pricing - and what that means for the ERP these firms will need.
  • Commercial orientation: you understand how product decisions drive ARR, win rate, and customer retention.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills at C-suite and practitioner level.

Key Responsibilities

Industry Strategy & Roadmap Alignment

  • Define and maintain a comprehensive industry roadmap for professional services, aligned with customer needs, market trends, and regulatory requirements.
  • Translate industry-specific workflows and pain points into actionable product requirements across ERP modules. Gather, document, and validate detailed product requirements based on customer interviews, market research, and regulatory analysis.
  • Champion the use of AI and automation technologies to deliver industry-specific differentiators that help clients innovate, drive efficiencies, and grow.
  • Identify opportunities to embed predictive analytics, intelligent workflows, and decision augmentation into professional services use cases to allow our users to focus on what matters.

Cross-Functional Collaboration  

  • Act as the industry voice in product planning conversations with horizontal product teams. 
  • Collaborate with Product Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success to support evangelism of our product strategy, to assist with go-to-market strategies, enablement, and to drive customer engagement. 

Customer & Market Insight 

  • Engage directly with customers, partners, and industry experts to gather insights and validate product direction. 
  • Monitor competitive offerings, market shifts, and compliance trends to inform product differentiation. 

 Product Execution Support 

  • Contribute to discovery, validation, and launch activities in collaboration with UX, engineering, and operations teams. 
  • Ensure industry-specific requirements are prioritized and delivered in alignment with platform capabilities. 
  • Experience in product management for enterprise SaaS platforms. 
  • Deep understanding of professional services business models, including project-based delivery, utilization, billing, scheduling and compliance. 
  • Strong ability to influence without authority and work cross-functionally in a matrixed environment. 
  • Proven ability to translate complex industry needs into scalable product solutions. 
  • Excellent communication, analytical, and stakeholder engagement skills. 

Desirable Experience 

  • Experience with ERP or PSA platforms  
  • Familiarity with mid-market services firms and their operational challenges. 
  • Familiarity with in AI-driven or data-rich product environments. 

Who we are?

We are a people-first community that nurtures all the areas that surround your working experience. With us, you’ll be surrounded by a high-performance team that supports your authentic self and celebrates your uniqueness.

We believe that ‘How work should feel’ is an evolving statement. Work goes beyond tasks and everyday responsibilities it’s about feeling valued, empowered, promoted, impactful, seen, and appreciated. We are reimagining how work makes people feel.

What we offer

  • a culture built on trust and accountability - giving you the freedom and autonomy to be successful and make an impact
  • balance - with our Flexible Leave Paid Time Off policy, remote working opportunities, Global Wellbeing Days, and other great benefits
  • growth opportunities - we provide the tools and guidance required so that you can focus on what really matters to you and so, ultimately, you can achieve your best work
  • talented colleagues, role models and mentors - work, learn and be inspired by some of the best talent in the software industry
  • a commitment to sustainability - with initiatives such as our Environmental, Social, and Governance strategy and Act4Good programme
  • a safe and inclusive working environment – supported by our Employee Resource Groups, which are open to all.

Our commitment to equity

Unit4 is committed to ensuring equal opportunity for everyone. We make our hiring decisions solely based on skills, qualifications, and our current business needs. We know that diversity brings fresh perspectives, ideas, and solutions to our company. This is the essence of our culture. We also welcome and encourage people who are pregnant and/or parents-to-be to apply. If you would like to know more about our commitment to diversity, visit our blogs:

jobs.title: Paid Search Strategist, DTC eCommerce
jobs.excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.
