About HighLevel

About us
HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.
To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.
Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our people
With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact
Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.

About the Team

The Lead Generation Team owns some of the most important products businesses use to build their digital presence and generate leads on HighLevel.

Our product portfolio includes Funnels, Websites, AI Studio, Forms, Surveys, Quizzes, Domains, Media, QR Codes, Listings, SEO, Analytics, Tracking, and other lead-generation experiences.

Millions of funnels, websites, forms, and other digital experiences are created using HighLevel. Our goal is to help agencies and businesses not only create these experiences but continuously improve their ability to attract visitors, capture leads, and drive conversions.

Data plays a critical role in how we make product decisions. We are looking for a Senior Product Analyst who can independently lead analytical work, deepen our understanding of customer behavior, identify growth opportunities, and help Product Managers make faster, better-informed decisions.

About the Role

HighLevel is looking for a highly analytical and product-minded Senior Product Analyst to join our Lead Generation Product team.

You will work closely with Product Managers, Engineering, Design, Data, and GTM teams to understand how customers discover, adopt, and use our products—and where the most meaningful opportunities exist to improve their experience.

You will own analytical projects end to end: framing the right questions, defining the approach, validating the data, conducting the analysis, and translating findings into clear recommendations. Your work will span the complete customer journey, from activation and feature adoption to engagement, conversion, retention, and monetization.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with a strong emphasis on independent ownership, product judgment, and cross-functional influence. Beyond delivering reports, you will proactively surface opportunities, challenge assumptions, and help Product Managers determine what we should build, why we should build it, and whether what we shipped actually worked.

Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end product analyses across Funnels, Websites, Forms, Surveys, Domains, SEO, Listings, and other LeadGen products, turning ambiguous questions into structured analyses and actionable recommendations.

  • Partner with Product Managers to define success metrics and measurement frameworks for product areas and initiatives, covering activation, adoption, engagement, retention, conversion, and monetization.

  • Build and maintain dashboards that give Product Managers and leadership clear visibility into product health, emerging trends, and business outcomes, while enabling teams to answer recurring questions independently.

  • Lead funnel and journey analyses to identify friction and drop-offs across onboarding, creation, publishing, lead capture, and other critical workflows.

  • Conduct cohort, segmentation, and retention analyses to understand differences across customer segments, usage patterns, and lifecycle stages—and identify where targeted improvements could have the greatest impact.

  • Partner with Product Managers to size opportunities, validate hypotheses, evaluate trade-offs, and prioritize initiatives based on potential customer and business impact.

  • Define measurement plans before feature launches, establish baselines, and evaluate adoption and outcomes after release. Communicate what the evidence supports, where uncertainty remains, and what to do next.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Data teams to define events, properties, tracking requirements, and instrumentation, ensuring critical customer journeys can be measured reliably.

  • Proactively identify data quality issues and tracking gaps, investigate their impact, and work with relevant teams to improve the consistency and reliability of product analytics.

  • Designand analyze A/B tests and product experiments, including hypotheses, success metrics, guardrail metrics, and interpretation of results, to support statistically sound decisions.

  • Contribute to requirements definition and feature validation across multiple initiatives, including success criteria and pre-launch validation.

  • Lead customer research, including interviews and surveys, and combine it with quantitative data and support-ticket signalsLead deep-dive and root-cause analyses when important metrics change unexpectedly, distinguishing meaningful shifts from data issues, seasonality, or changes in customer mix.

  • Proactively recommend opportunities to improve lead generation, conversion rates, product adoption, engagement, and retention, and partner with teams to assess the results of resulting changes.

  • Present complex findings as clear, decision-oriented narratives, explaining recommendations, trade-offs, assumptions, and limitations to Product Managers, Engineering, Design, and leadership.

  • Contribute to shared analytical practices, metric definitions, and documentation, bringing customer and LeadGen domain context to the numbers rather than reporting metrics in isolation.

  • Mentor junior analysts and facilitate discovery discussions with Product, Design and Engineering

Requirements

  • 4-7 years of experience in Product Analytics, Business Analytics, Data Analytics, or a related analytical role, with demonstrated experience informing product decisions.

  • Strong proficiency in SQL, including complex joins, window functions, and working independently with large datasets.

  • Demonstrated ability to own analytical projects end to end, from clarifying an ambiguous problem to delivering recommendations and following through on outcomes.

  • Experience leading customer research (interviews, surveys) and competitive analysis.

  • Experience with product analytics or BI tools such as Amplitude, Mixpanel, Pendo, Tableau, Looker, Power BI, or similar platforms.

  • Strong understanding of product metrics such as activation, adoption, engagement, retention, conversion, churn, and monetization, including how to select appropriate metrics for different product goals.

  • Hands-on experience with funnel analysis, cohort analysis, segmentation, retention analysis, and user journey analysis.

  • Experience designing or analyzing A/B tests or product experiments, with a practical understanding of hypothesis testing, statistical significance, and common analytical biases.

  • Working knowledge of event-based analytics, instrumentation, and tracking plans, with experience identifying data quality issues and validating analytical inputs.

  • Strong proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets, along with the ability to build clear dashboards and communicate findings through effective data visualization.

  • Experience partnering closely with Product Managers, Engineering, Design, and other cross-functional teams to influence prioritization and product improvements.

  • Ability to communicate complex findings in simple business terms, make clear recommendations, and explain assumptions and limitations.

  • Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to prioritize analytical work based on its potential impact.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Python for data analysis, including libraries such as Pandas and NumPy.

  • Familiarity with Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, pixels, attribution, or web analytics.

  • Understanding of websites, funnels, conversion rate optimization, digital marketing, or lead-generation products.

  • Experience working in B2B SaaS, MarTech, CRM, website builders, or high-growth technology companies.

  • Familiarity with APIs and an ability to understand how data flows between systems.

  • Experience improving analytics workflows, documenting reusable approaches, or helping teammates strengthen their analytical skills.

Preferred Soft Skills

  • Curiosity to go beyond what happened and understand why it happened and what we should do next.

  • Strong product and customer judgment, with the ability to connect analytical findings to real customer problems.

  • Comfort independently navigating ambiguity and balancing rigor with the need to make timely decisions.

  • Confidence to challenge assumptions constructively and influence decisions without formal authority.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to tailor the level of detail to the audience.

  • Strong ownership and collaboration skills in a fast-moving, remote environment.

What Success Looks Like

A successful Senior Product Analyst in the Lead Generation team will help us move from “we think this is happening” to “we understand what is happening, why it matters, and what we should do next.”

Product teams will have clearer success metrics, more reliable measurement, and a stronger understanding of customer behavior. Important opportunities and risks will be surfaced proactively, and launches and experiments will produce actionable learning—not just reports.

Your work will directly influence product strategy, roadmap prioritization, experimentation, and investment decisions across HighLevel’s Lead Generation portfolio.

Optain has achieved regulatory approval and commercial adoption of its product suite in global markets, including Australia, Europe, and more.

In 2025, Optain received US FDA clearance for its Resolve retinal camera. Optain also recently closed a Series A funding round led by Insight Partners with participation from seven leading U.S. health system investors, including Memorial Hermann Health System, Northwell Health, Novant Health, The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, and UPMC. These systems collectively deliver care to 28 million patients across 25 states and have begun deploying Optain's platform across their networks, rapidly accelerating the company's footprint and expanding screening access nationwide. Optain also acquired EyePACS, a teleophthalmology platform with a 15-year history and an established network of licensed optometrists and ophthalmologists who read retinal images for diabetic retinopathy screening.

About the Job

As the Clinical Operations Manager, you will own the operations of Optain's provider network -- the optometrists and ophthalmologists who read retinal images for health systems, clinics, and community health centers across the United States. The network has run for 15 years on the judgment and relationships of a small number of people. Your job is to turn that into documented policy, a measurable quality program, a capacity model that runs ahead of demand, and a governance rhythm in alignment with Optain’s Medical Director. You will report to the VP of Operations and work day to day with Optain's Medical Director. This is a non-clinical role for someone who has managed a network of contracted clinicians before, writes policy that physicians sign, and knows the difference between running a process and building one that doesn't need you.

Optain is at an inflection point. We have FDA clearance, a growing camera footprint, and a commercial pipeline that is moving fast. Behind every screening exam is a licensed grader reading the images through our EyePACS platform, and the operational infrastructure around that network is being built in real time. This role sits at the center of that work.

This is a remote, US-based position.

What You'll Do

  • Own the grading playbook, SOPs, onboarding materials, and the provider network policy library -- author, version, and maintain them, and route clinical content to the Medical Director for review and sign-off.
  • Establish documentation governance for the network -- ownership, versioning, review cadence, and sign-off -- so operating knowledge lives in documents rather than in individuals.
  • Design and run the grader quality program, including sampling, over-read and discordance review, turnaround accountability, and performance feedback -- establish error rates and trends where today review is periodic and manual.
  • Prepare quality reviews and escalations for Medical Director adjudication and carry out the resulting actions, including performance conversations and offboarding.
  • Build and maintain a capacity model by state, customer, and license coverage, and set recruitment triggers ahead of turnaround breaches.
  • Run the grader recruitment pipeline from sourcing through interview and recommendation, working with the Operations Manager on credentialing and onboarding execution.
  • Own intake, triage, and routing of customer and grader complaints, including urgent findings workflows -- route clinical questions to the Medical Director, close the loop with the customer, and trend issues over time.
  • Set the agenda, prepare decisions, and follow through so the Medical Director's time goes to clinical judgment rather than logistics.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering on platform improvements that reduce manual work, including documenting current-state workflows so feature development is accurate and fast, and contribute network measurables to the weekly grader operations rhythm and company scorecard.

What You'll Need

  • 5+ years in healthcare operations, with 2+ years managing a network of contracted or affiliated clinicians -- telehealth, teleradiology, or virtual care strongly preferred over traditional medical group or IPA settings.
  • Has written clinical or operational policy that a physician leader signed, and maintained it afterward.
  • Has run or materially contributed to a clinical quality, peer review, or provider performance program.
  • Prior experience operating a clinician network under a medical director's clinical oversight is a strong plus.
  • Exposure to credentialing, medical staff services, or multistate clinician licensing is a plus; teleophthalmology background is a plus, not a requirement.
  • Experience participating in product discovery or operationalizing new feature launches is a plus.
  • Comfortable building and reading operational dashboards and capacity models in spreadsheets or BI tools.
  • Startup experience is strongly preferred -- you have built a process where little existed and can show the result.
  • Clear, direct written communicator who is comfortable working with physicians as a non-clinician.
  • Has driven adoption of new processes across teams without direct reporting authority.
  • US-based, comfortable with remote work and occasional travel for team offsites and customer engagements.

What Success Looks Like in Year One

  • The grading playbook, onboarding materials, and network policy library are current, versioned, and signed, with a documented review cadence.
  • A grader quality program is running, with error rates and turnaround trends reported monthly and at least one full cycle of performance feedback completed.
  • A capacity model by state and customer is in use, and recruitment is triggered by the model rather than by turnaround breaches.
  • A complaint intake and escalation process is documented and running, with clinical questions routed to the Medical Director.
  • The Medical Director's time goes to clinical decisions, with decision prep and follow-through owned by this role.
  • At least two manual network processes have moved into the platform in partnership with Product and Engineering.

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation package, including a strong base salary, performance-based bonus, and the chance to earn upside.
  • Top-tier health, vision, dental, and commuter benefits.
  • Generous monthly health and wellness reimbursement.
  • Unparalleled exposure to new business building at the intersection of artificial intelligence and healthcare.
  • The opportunity to help solve difficult problems and collaborate with world-class experts from healthcare provider networks, academia, and industry.
  • A chance to work with a highly talented, close-knit team and world-leading mentors who can act as a support network and sounding board throughout your entrepreneurial journey.

Salary Range

  • $120,000 - $145,000 base salary, depending on experience and alignment with role expectations, plus bonus and equity.

Why Optain?Make a real difference: Your work will help solve difficult problems as you collaborate with world-class experts from healthcare provider networks, academia, and industry. Join Optain in transforming healthcare with AI!

jobs.description:
Infobase exists to power informed decisions. For decades, schools, libraries, and institutions have turned to our resources to build information literacy and help learners develop the skills they need to succeed long after the classroom. We build the platforms and content that make that possible, and right now we're growing the team behind them.

Job Summary

    The Product Manager, Careers sets product direction for Infobase’s careers and career and technical education (CTE) offerings, with the goal of significantly expanding sales in middle school, high school, community college, and public library markets. The role focuses on four areas: a careers strategy built around Advance CTE pathways and career development (guidance and assessment) at the middle school, high school, and university levels; an expanded CTE emphasis within that strategy; an assessment partnership that enables quick expansion; and modern product workflows that help the product grow across these markets. This senior individual-contributor role combines product management with content management for the careers and CTE portfolio, working in close partnership with the Vault leadership team, content teams, platform leadership, and Infobase’s enterprise-level engineering team, and building alignment through collaboration and influence rather than formal authority. The Product Manager, Careers owns the vision and roadmap for this area on an ongoing basis and may be assigned other product initiatives based on organizational needs and the publishing and release cycle of the careers product line.

Essential Functions

    Product Strategy & Roadmap Ownership

    • Define product vision and strategy for careers and CTE offerings across middle school, high school, community college, and public library markets, grounded in customer-centric design, market analysis, competitive dynamics, revenue analysis, and customer research.
    • Own and prioritize the roadmap, including technology and content, making the tradeoffs needed to balance customer value, business priorities, and delivery capacity.
    • Shape an expanded CTE emphasis within the careers strategy, aligned to Advance CTE pathways and to workforce-relevant outcomes at the high school and community college levels.
    • Build the business case for significant product investments and partnerships, including tradeoffs, revenue impact, and expected results, and present recommendations to product and executive leadership.

      • Partnerships & Assessment Integration

      • Identify assessment and video partnership opportunities, outline deal points, and serve as the frontline contact for those partners.
      • Own a potential assessment partnership, including integration requirements, delivery sequencing for quick expansion, and tracking of partnership outcomes.
      • Define how assessment results connect to careers content and learning assets, including careers videos and career guides, so users move from assessment to exploration to planning.
      • Shape career development experiences (guidance and assessment) for middle school, high school, and university learners.

        • Content Management

        • Manage the careers and CTE content portfolio, including careers videos and career guides, setting priorities for what is created, updated, acquired, or retired.
        • Identify content gaps against Advance CTE pathways, workforce-relevant outcomes at the high school and community college levels, and the needs of a partner assessment.
        • Work with editors and external content partners to plan, commission, and review content, holding it to standards for accuracy, quality, and alignment to pathways.
        • Manage content creation through external vendors, as advised by Franchise Owners and supported by limited staff time where available.
        • Maintain a content plan and update cycle so careers and CTE content stays current as pathways, labor-market information, and customer needs change.
        • Ensure content is structured and tagged so assessment results can connect users to the right videos and guides.

          • Voice of Customer & Market Insight

          • Lead voice-of-customer practices, including direct research, usage data analysis, customer feedback loops, and pilots, to keep decisions grounded in evidence.
          • Distinguish between buyers and users across school, community college, and library settings (for example, librarians, counselors, CTE educators, and students) when designing products that win sales and increase classroom usage.
          • Track competitive and market developments in careers, CTE, and related assessments, and translate them into roadmap implications.

            • Product Workflows & Go-to-Market

            • Design modern, customer-centric product workflows that help the product significantly expand sales in middle school, high school, community college, and public library markets within the constraints of an enterprise-level platform.
            • Coordinate go-to-market readiness with Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, and track results after launch.
            • Define and report on KPIs and business outcomes on a regular cadence to product and executive stakeholders.

              • Cross-Functional Leadership: Vault, Platform & Engineering

              • Serve as the liaison with platform, engineering, Vault, and customer-facing teams, aligning future product direction with content strategy and platform capabilities and consulting with content teams at key points in development.
              • Partner with platform leadership on the definition and requirements of new products and significant revisions to existing products.
              • Work with Infobase’s enterprise-level engineering team to sequence delivery and keep the roadmap realistic against shared engineering capacity.
              • Write clear product requirements and maintain a prioritized backlog for engineering, resolving tradeoffs as delivery progresses.
              • Influence cross-functional teams and stakeholders without formal authority, including when priorities conflict.
              • Share domain expertise and product practice with other Product Managers and with Franchise Owners.
              • Perform other duties as assigned.

Core Compentancies

    • Technical Knowledge: Advanced product management expertise combined with content management and working knowledge of CTE, career pathways, and assessment integration; owns product and content direction for the careers and CTE portfolio and shares product practice with other Product Managers and Franchise Owners.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewThe Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.
jobs.description:
Overview

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

Program Overview

CHAI’s Analytics and Implementation Research (AIR) Team is a results-driven team of public health experts strategically positioned at the centre of CHAI’s geographic and disease priorities, maximizing health systems, and bringing innovations to scale. AIR has years of experience tackling problems within real-world health systems in resource-limited settings and a long history of well-regarded collaboration with partner governments and CHAI country and global teams.

Position Overview

CHAI is seeking a highly motivated individual with public health experience and analytical skills to work with CHAI’s program and country teams and government counterparts to conduct epidemiological analysis, model program impact and cost-effectiveness, monitor and evaluate the success of ongoing efforts, and translate results for decision-makers. The Technical Advisor will work across CHAI's program portfolio, building, pressure-testing, and communicating analytical evidence to support strategic decisions. They will be responsible for developing and refining cost-effectiveness analyses for candidate programs across CHAI's portfolio; conducting rigorous pressure-tests of program theories of change by critically reviewing literature; and applying quantitative methods to help CHAI country teams identify priority programs, efficiencies, and geographic targeting opportunities. The Technical Advisor will also prepare clear, concise analytical outputs and presentations for CHAI senior leadership and major philanthropic funders, translating complex modelling work into strategic insights that can shape funding conversations.

This role is a unique opportunity to apply advanced epidemiological and quantitative analytics to high-impact health interventions in some of the world's most challenging contexts. You will have the chance to work across CHAI's diverse health programs, own technically complex analytical work end-to-end, interact with policymakers and donors, and directly influence how resources are allocated to save lives at scale.

This role is open to candidates based in any CHAI program country, pending leadership approval and appropriate work authorization, and requires up to 15% travel. Candidates should be able to accommodate overlapping working hours with US Eastern Time (ET) to facilitate team collaboration.

Responsibilities

Analytics and modelling

  • Apply quantitative and geospatial methods to support CHAI country teams in identifying high-priority programs, geographic targeting opportunities, and health system efficiencies
  • Build cost-effectiveness models to enable evidence-based program decision-making to achieve maximal impact
  • Manage analytical workstreams end-to-end, exercising independent judgment on methodological approach and appropriate level of analytical depth given the question and available data
  • Appropriately utilize large-scale datasets (e.g., GBD, DHS, national surveys, IHME datasets, implementation cost data) to inform program design and prioritization decisions
  • Collaborate across CHAI's disease and geographic programs to gather inputs, validate analytical assumptions, and ensure models reflect on-the-ground program realities

Evidence-based program development and technical leadership

  • Leading a portfolio of work, including setting the long-term strategy, identifying medium-term priorities and defining a workplan
  • Support the design and implementation of new pilot programs, leveraging existing evidence and data to ensure interventions are both impactful and cost-effective
  • Conduct rigorous pressure-tests of program theories of change, including critical review of evidence, interrogation of key assumptions, and assessment of causal pathways and counterfactual scenarios

Stakeholder engagement and donor deliverables

  • Translate complex modelling and analytical work into clear, concise outputs — including presentations, memos, and briefing materials — for CHAI senior leadership and major philanthropic funders
  • Support CHAI's engagement with major funders by preparing evidence-based materials that inform prioritization decisions and funding conversations
  • Collaborate with CHAI country teams and government partners to ensure feasibility and alignment of interventions within national health systems

Qualifications

Education and experience

  • Postgraduate degree in epidemiology, economics, or related quantitative discipline
  • 7+ years of experience applying quantitative methods to global health or development challenges, including cost-effectiveness analysis, impact evaluations, and mathematical modeling

Technical

  • Exceptional analytical and critical thinking skills, with proven capacity to pressure test complex theories of change
  • Excellent skills in data management and statistical analysis, including use of software such as Stata, R, or SAS
  • Experience in cost-effectiveness modeling and evaluation design (including causal inference using observational data), tailoring methodologies to diverse contexts to generate actionable insights
  • Experience assessing and reconciling data quality issues across large survey and administrative datasets, particularly in multi-country settings
  • Strong understanding of the LMIC health systems context, including data limitations, operational constraints, and the role of government and partner ecosystems

Operational

  • Strong communication skills, including the proven ability to translate research into policy recommendations, and to present complex quantitative findings to donors, government stakeholders, and other diverse audiences
  • Demonstrated fluency in using AI tools to synthesize information and produce high-quality analytical outputs, paired with the judgment to critically evaluate AI-generated work, identifying where it falls short or gets things wrong, and applying sound human reasoning to correct, refine, and strengthen the final product
  • Proven ability to work independently on an ambiguous, early-stage concept, shaping it into a clear vision, aligning a team around that direction, and driving the work through to a donor-ready and senior-leadership-ready final product
  • Commitment to collaborative work with a remote, geographically dispersed team across multiple time zones
  • Fluency in English

Preferred

  • Direct experience collaborating with donors in the global health and development space, including drafting concept notes or proposals
  • Experience reviewing or quality-checking the analytical work of others, and/or mentoring or informally leading junior analytical staff
  • Experience using geospatial methods to support budget optimization, program targeting, or subnational prioritization analyses is an advantage
  • Proficiency in one or more languages spoken in CHAI countries

jobs.excerpt: At Thorne, we work to deliver high-quality, science-backed solutions to empower individuals to take a proactive approach to their well-being.
jobs.description:
At Thorne, we work to deliver high-quality, science-backed solutions to empower individuals to take a proactive approach to their well-being. Each day begins with a mission to help others discover and achieve their best health. We count on our team members to challenge and push the boundaries to make that happen. At Thorne, you’ll be joining a team of more than 750 passionate individuals committed to our cause of providing superior health solutions at every age and life stage.The Senior Manager of Influencer Marketing will develop and manage Thorne’s paid influencer initiatives and ambassador program, translating brand and business priorities into integrated channel plans that build brand awareness, credibility, consumer engagement, and new customer acquisition. This is responsible for end-to-end planning, execution and optimization, including content volume and pacing, creator selection, budget management, campaign delivery, measurement, and adherence to established business processes. The Senior Manager will manage one direct report and Thorne’s influencer agency, coordinate cross functional execution, and build relationships with creators and ambassadors who align with Thorne’s mission and values. Success requires sound judgment, proactive communication, disciplined prioritization, and accountability for delivering results within approved strategies, budgets and timelines.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Channel Planning & Program Management
  • Develop and execute influencer and ambassador channel plans aligned with Thorne’s brand marketing objectives, business priorities, and target audiences.
  • Translate brand marketing plans, new product launches, seasonal campaigns, and always-on content needs into a comprehensive channel plan with clear objectives, investment recommendations, deliverables, timelines, and success measures.
  • Collaborate with Performance Team to recommend the creator mix, content volume, formats, production cadence, and distribution approach needed to support planned initiatives and cross-functional content requirements.
  • Apply agreed objectives across awareness, consideration, and acquisition, aligning investment and measurement with its intended contribution.
  • Use audience insights, performance data, platform behavior, and cultural trends to inform strategic recommendations and identify opportunities for growth.
  • Independently manage prioritization, sequencing, and delegation across assigned programs within approved budgets and resources. Recommend tradeoffs and escalate priorities or capacity constraints when leadership decisions are needed.
  • Communicate plans, recommendations, and results clearly and concisely, tailoring the level of detail to the audience.
Paid Influencer Planning & Execution
  • Identify, evaluate, recruit, and negotiate with influencers and content creators whose audiences, credibility, content capabilities, and brand alignment support Thorne’s objectives and reflect Thorne’s brand standards.
  • Negotiate influencers’ scopes, rates, deliverables, and usage rights within approved budgets and contracting guidelines.
  • Manage campaign development and delivery from initial brief through contracting, onboarding, content development, approvals, publication, reporting, and optimization.
  • Develop clear creative briefs that connect audience needs, product benefits, brand messaging, substantiated claims, and intended platform use.
  • Partner with Performance Marketing to define paid content requirements before production, including creative structure, deliverable specifications, usage rights, and partnership advertising permissions.
  • Secure appropriate rights for content distribution across relevant brand and paid media channels, with a focus on Meta, TikTok, and YouTube.
  • Plan and execute influencer and ambassador experiential activations, product experiences, content capture, and community initiatives within approved objectives and budgets. Define influencer roles, content requirements, distribution plans, timelines, and measurement approaches.
  • Build and maintain a reliable pipeline of creator content that supports agreed campaign needs, content volume, and delivery schedules.
  • Manage content review and approval process to ensure influencer content is authentic, accurate, consistent with Thorne’s brand standards, and appropriate for its intended use.
Ambassador Program Management & Execution
  • Audit and evaluate Thorne’s ambassador program, recommending improvements to its participant value proposition, eligibility criteria, operating model, and measurement approach in alignment with program objectives.
  • Develop recommendations for changes to program structure, scale, investment, or participation requirements for leadership review and approval.
  • Manage recruitment, onboarding, education, engagement, and support of Ambassadors that reflect the Thorne brand ethos and target audiences.
  • Develop and maintain training materials and support resources covering approved messaging, product information, disclosure requirements, content expectations, and program policies.
  • Plan and execute ambassador initiatives that drive user-generated content (UGC) in support of evergreen education, product launches, seasonal campaigns, and authentic product experiences.
  • Implement and maintain processes to monitor participant activity, content, traffic sources, and adherence to program requirements, working with relevant cross-functional teams to address gaps.
  • Regularly assess participant contribution, revenue concentration, attribution quality, and resource requirements. Use findings to recommend program improvements and investment decisions.
  • Manage and report on the Thorne brand ambassador private Facebook group, encouraging participation, facilitating relevant discussions and building an engaged Ambassador community.
Performance Analysis & Optimization
  • Partner with Performance Marketing to establish program and campaign KPIs and success metrics aligned with approved objectives.
  • Maintain consistent reporting that distinguishes organic creator performance, paid amplification results, ambassador activity, and attributable commercial outcomes.
  • Deliver timely, detailed monthly performance recaps and quarterly strategic assessments with concise insights, investment implications and recommended actions for optimization and continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate with the Performance Marketing team to develop testing plans and apply learnings to creator selection, creative development, content distribution, and program execution.
  • Monitor content performance, social trends, and relevant platform algorithm changes, recommending plan adjustments to improve results.
  • Proactively identify underperformance, delivery gaps, attribution concerns, and emerging risks, recommending corrective actions and escalating issues that require broader decisions.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Process Management
  • Coordinate planning and execution with Brand Marketing, Creative, Performance Marketing, Organic Social, New Product Development, PR, Legal, Medical Affairs, Regulatory, Finance, and other relevant teams in relation to paid influencer marketing and brand ambassadors.
  • Gather and incorporate cross-functional inputs into actionable channel plans, maintaining responsibility for assigned deliverables and respecting cross-functional teams’ capacity.
  • Develop and maintain clear roles, decision points, timelines, and workback schedules that account for negotiating, contracting, product availability, content production, review, and launch requirements.
  • Incorporate required review periods and approval milestones into project plans and ensure agreements are approved and fully executed before services or activations begin.
  • Work with Legal, Medical Affairs, and Regulatory to implement and maintain content review processes that support applicable FTC, FDA, and DSHEA content disclosure requirements and are consistent with Thorne’s internal policies.
  • Proactively identify dependencies, communicate risks, and resolve execution barriers. Escalate issues with recommended solutions and clearly identify decisions needed.
  • Maintain accurate plans and trackers that provide visibility into priorities, ownership, deliverables, budgets, and progress.
  • Operate independently, exercise sound judgment, and raise material issues early with practical recommendations.
People Management
  • Manage one (1) direct report, setting clear objectives, responsibilities, deliverables, and performance expectations.
  • Delegate work appropriately while retaining accountability for program execution, quality, timelines, and results.
  • Provide regular coaching, actionable feedback, and performance management to build capabilities and support professional development.
  • Monitor workload and capacity, adjusting assignments within available resources and recommending additional support when needed.
Budget, Agency & Partner Management
  • Manage paid influencer and ambassador program spending within approved budget, maintaining accurate forecasts, commitments, invoice tracking, and monthly reconciliation.
  • Recommend investment allocations across creator fees, usage rights, and program activations based on aligned priorities and performance.
  • Manage the day-to-day relationship with Thorne’s influencer agency, translating channel priorities into clear briefs, directing campaign execution, and holding the agency accountable for creator recommendations, deliverable quality, timelines, budgets, and performance.
  • Build productive partner relationships while holding external teams accountable for delivery, quality, and compliance with agreed requirements.

WHAT YOU NEED

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field required.
  • 5+ years of experience in influencer marketing, with at least 2 years in a managerial role, preferably within the wellness or consumer goods industry.
  • Demonstrated execution of influencer planning, budgets, campaign activation and performance optimization.
  • Deep understanding of the creator landscape, audience behavior, and content practices across Meta, TikTok, and YouTube; established influencer and creator relationships within the wellness space preferred.
  • Experience developing creator content for both organic distribution and paid amplification, including negotiating rights usage and partnership advertising permissions.
  • Experience managing ambassador or affiliate programs, including participant engagement, activity, monitoring, attribution, and program governance.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to turn performance data into clear recommendations and investment decisions.
  • Working knowledge of influencer disclosure, advertising claims, and content review practices; experience working in a regulated consumer category preferred.
  • Proven ability to manage complex work streams, prioritize competing demands, and deliver through cross-functional teams.
  • Strong negotiation, relationship management, and agency oversight skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver high-quality work within requested time frames.
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication, including executive presentations and reporting.
  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, financial discipline, and follow-through.
  • Ability to work independently, anticipate needs, make informed decisions, and deliver with minimal oversight.
  • Experience with Aspire or comparable creator marketing platforms preferred.
  • Genuine interest in health and wellness and an understanding of the importance of credible, responsible brand advocacy.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Competitive compensation
  • 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage for employees
  • Company-paid short- and long-term disability insurance
  • Company- paid life insurance
  • 401k plan with employer matching contributions up to 4%
  • Gym membership reimbursement
  • Monthly allowance of Thorne supplements
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off and holiday leave
  • Training, professional development, and career growth opportunities

At AIS, we are dedicated to providing our employees with diverse opportunities to grow their careers while supporting a variety of impactful projects. For this position, we are seeking a talented individual to join AIS as a Lead Infrastructure Engineer.

  • Core Knowledge & Skills: Aligns infrastructure strategy to business goals, leads large projects, applies compliance frameworks, designs high availability/disaster recovery and performance optimization patterns, and shapes deployment pipeline design.

  • Work & Complexity: Directs cross-team programs, performs advanced tuning, implements high availability/failover architectures, leads audits, plans growth, and manages budgets.

  • Quality & Independence: Delivers high-quality outcomes, sets team standards, introduces innovative solutions, and makes high-impact decisions.

  • Consulting & Engagement: Provides high-level consulting to leadership, builds roadmaps, negotiates vendor contracts, and sponsors innovation initiatives.

As your initial project assignment, you will support the unique needs of our client as a Cloud Migration Engineer II.

Project Summary


The Cloud Migration Engineer II is a senior hands-on engineer who owns moderate-to-high complexity and multi-tier application migrations from on-premises data centers to Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS). The role independently assesses technical readiness, selects and adapts approved migration patterns, coordinates technical execution, resolves cross-domain issues, and ensures that migration, validation, rollback, and stabilization activities are completed safely and consistently. The role remains hands-on and is not a people-manager or architect position. The role is remote.


Key Responsibilities


  • Owns moderate-to-high complexity or multi-tier application migrations from technical assessment through cutover, rollback, stabilization, and handoff.
  • Analyzes incomplete application and infrastructure information, validates complex dependencies and readiness risks, and recommends remediation before migration.
  • Selects and adapts approved Azure and AWS migration patterns and runbooks within program guardrails to address application-specific requirements.
  • Reviews target-environment configuration and resolves design or integration issues involving compute, Windows and Linux operating systems, networking, storage, virtualization, identity, security, and application services.
  • Coordinates technical migration execution, including replication, synchronization, shutdown and startup sequencing, decision points, specialist engagement, escalation, cutover, and rollback activities.
  • Leads diagnosis and resolution of cross-domain migration issues and determines when an architect or shared engineering specialist must be engaged.
  • Reviews migration readiness, runbooks, automation, validation results, technical evidence, and rollback viability before key migration decisions.
  • Develops or improves reusable PowerShell, Bash, Python, infrastructure-as-code, and migration automation assets using approved GitHub repositories and program standards.
  • Authors or approves runbooks and technical procedures for complex migration patterns and identifies systemic improvements to migration-factory methods, automation, guardrails, and controls.
  • Guides Cloud Migration Engineer I staff, reviews technical work, and serves as a technical escalation point without acting as a people manager.

Required For This Opportunity


  • US Citizen
  • Minimum five years of progressively responsible infrastructure engineering, systems administration, cloud engineering, or migration experience, including independently leading complex server or application migrations
  • Demonstrated ability to assess technical readiness, analyze incomplete dependency information, select among approved migration approaches, and adapt runbooks for application-specific requirements
  • Hands-on experience with Azure and/or AWS cloud environments, including target configuration, migration tooling, validation, troubleshooting, and operational handoff
  • Advanced troubleshooting experience across Windows Server, Linux, networking, storage, virtualization, identity and access management, security controls, and application dependencies
  • Experience installing, upgrading, configuring, and troubleshooting Windows Server and Linux environments, including Red Hat, Oracle Linux, CentOS, or similar distributions
  • Experience managing Windows and Linux file systems, including PowerShell-based Windows administration and Linux Logical Volume Manager (LVM) and ZFS
  • Experience supporting migrations with Azure File Sync, AWS DataSync, rsync, robocopy, Azure Files, NFS, and/or Amazon Elastic File System (EFS)
  • Experience establishing performance baselines, diagnosing performance issues, and recommending cloud target sizing based on existing-system data
  • Ability to develop or improve PowerShell, Bash, Python, infrastructure-as-code, or similar automation supporting deployment, configuration, migration, rollback, and validation
  • Experience reviewing another engineer’s runbooks, automation, validation evidence, or migration artifacts and providing technical guidance
  • Experience applying or validating STIG controls and/or DoD security requirements within secure and compliant engineering procedures

Nice to Have Skills


  • Experience with Azure Government or AWS GovCloud environments
  • Current associate-level cloud certification strongly preferred, such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate, AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate, or AWS Certified SysOps Administrator – Associate
  • Advanced or complementary certification such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert, Microsoft Certified: DevOps Engineer Expert, AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional, AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional, HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate, or a relevant security credential
  • Experience leading technical cutover and rollback decisions within defined program authority
  • Experience migrating multi-tier applications and resolving cross-domain migration issues
  • Experience developing reusable Terraform, Bicep, CloudFormation, or other infrastructure-as-code modules
  • Experience using GitHub and GitHub Copilot for source control, peer review, collaboration, and AI-assisted engineering
  • Federal program delivery experience and familiarity with ServiceNow-based change management

jobs.excerpt: EdOpsSchool Finance ManagerEdOps’s School Finance Manager position is ideal for school finance leaders ready to bring their expertise to a portfolio of schools and shape our nationwide finance offering alongside committed and experienced finance peers.
jobs.description:
EdOpsSchool Finance Manager

EdOps’s School Finance Manager position is ideal for school finance leaders ready to bring their expertise to a portfolio of schools and shape our nationwide finance offering alongside committed and experienced finance peers.

The School Finance Manager serves a portfolio of 5-8 schools, acting as those schools’ outsourced CFOs. Like on-staff CFOs, they leverage team members to analyze backwards-looking financial data and deliver strategic financial advice aligned with their schools’ mission and goals, build relationships with school leaders and boards, proactively notice and solve client problems, and generally act as key members of clients’ leadership teams. Internally, School Finance Managers drive innovations to our products, and the development and refinement of best practices when it comes to school finance.

Reports to Finance Director or above. Location flexible (this is a remote position). Part time arrangements possible for exceptional candidates.

Who we are:

EdOps is a B-Corp which partners with schools to provide expert support in finance, accounting, and student data management, helping education leaders make informed decisions while minimizing the financial, operational, and compliance burdens of running a school. Simply put, we make it easier for school leaders to increase student achievement. Our experience working with a wide range of schools – from newly authorized charter schools to independent schools with century-long histories, and from microschools to multi-campus networks – allows us to provide high-quality finance, accounting, and student data support across diverse educational environments.

Our team of over 100 professionals currently serves over 100 independent and public charter schools and networks across D.C., Louisiana, Maryland, Missouri, Michigan, New Jersey, and New York. We are serious about being the best possible partners to schools, and it shows in our 93% annual client retention rate. We work hard at being a rewarding, enjoyable workplace where staff can grow professionally and make an impact. We are looking for education focused, accounting and finance loving, collaborative people to join our team.

What you will do:

  • Act as an outsourced CFO for a portfolio of 5-8 schools, advising these schools’ leaders and Boards on matters pertaining to financial and operational policies, strategic decisions, and long-term financial planning.
  • Produce forward-looking financial forecasts, set budgets, and lead finance strategy development in a way that aligns with school goals and reflects EdOps’s commitment to equity and anti-racism.
  • Attend finance committee or board meetings to present and explain finance strategy.
  • Analyze, model, and solve problems on a wide range of business issues.
  • Engage in client listening and endeavor to proactively identify and solve clients’ financial challenges - either directly, or through engaging other teams at EdOps.
  • Provide development and informal oversight to School Finance Specialists and School Finance Analysts on school-specific processes. (For clarity, Finance Specialists and Finance Analysts report to dedicated People Managers; this position’s oversight of their work is relatively informal.)
  • Actively contribute to EdOps’s internal research, development and innovation of our finance product.

What you will accomplish:

  • By Year 1 you will have:
    • Solve small, real problems for schools on a daily basis.
    • Advise school leaders on nuanced, long term strategic financial decisions (i.e., facilities projects, staffing models, school expansion).
    • Develop close, trusting partnership with C-Level school leadership which will allow you to provide the best advice and support.
    • Present important financial information to a school’s Board of Directors.
    • Sharpen you expertise in strategic school finance, from multi-year budget development to internal process refinement
    • Work with 5-8 schools in different stages of growth and with different academic models.
  • By Year 3 you will have:
    • Contribute to the development and refinement of EdOps’s standard finance product, as well as our suite of best practices.
    • Lead project-based or market development work beyond your school portfolio..
    • Continue to solve real problems, small and large, for schools every day.

Who you are:

  • Care about education and outcomes for students as much as you care about budgets, forecasts and efficient financial processes.
  • Find joy in solving financial problems for individual schools. The little things make schools actually work.
  • Able to zoom in and out between high level strategic perspective and detailed, daily financial work.
  • Desire to be involved in the financial processes from input to analysis. We are outsourced CFOs but sometimes we are also controllers, accountants, and everything in between.
  • Strong in independent problem solving. We are a very collaborative community that supports each other, but our School Finance Managers are independent and solve new problems every day.
  • Energized by being in a customer service role. We are here first and foremost to serve our school clients.
  • Committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. Open to learning and growing in these areas together so that each of us can contribute to building a culture of equity and support our schools in advancing these values. Please see more on EdOps' commitment here.

What you need:

  • Experience excelling in a School Finance Management role (i.e., led finance function for a school, led part of a finance function in larger school organization)
  • Experience as part of a School Leadership Team or working very closely with a School Leadership Team.
  • Comfort with accounting. A CPA or extensive expertise is not required, but experience navigating accounting software and reading and analyzing financial reports is a must.
  • Intermediate Excel knowledge, such as formulas like vlookups and sumifs, because Excel will be your best friend at times.
  • Strong quantitative analysis, strategic thinking, and problem-solving skills, as every school is different, and approaches and solutions often have to be customized.
  • Excellent client communication and interpersonal skills. Comfort presenting and explaining information (both verbally and in writing) to people with varying financial literacy.
  • Comfort interacting with, advising, and challenging C-Level leaders in schools.
  • Strong organization and time management skills. There is a lot going on here.
  • General comfort with technology systems (e.g., Google suite) because we are not big fans of paper around here at EdOps.
  • Typically, School Finance Managers have 10-15 years of work or post-secondary educational experience.
  • Experience leading audits.

What you get:

  • Purpose driven work focusing on student achievement through operational excellence. That is what it is all about.
  • Chance to work every day with colleagues who are committed to kids and supportive of each other’s efforts.
  • EdOps salaries are commensurate with relative experience and geographic location. The range for the School Finance Manager position is $93,642-125,246/year.
  • Check out other perks of working at EdOps here. And some details on benefits here.

We know that a team from a wide range of backgrounds with different life experiences, identities, opinions, and talents makes us better able to innovate and deliver on our mission of supporting schools to improve student outcomes. Every day we work to build an inclusive company culture where everyone can be themselves at work and do their best work.

Apply:

If you are skilled in your field, excited by our mission, ready to learn, and looking for a place where you can be yourself, we want to hear from you!

What you can expect from the hiring process:

- Application Review

- First Interview

- Performance Task

- Final Interview

- Reference Check

- Offer

Salary: $96,217 – $128,690 / year

This is a hands-on role for someone who has lived in contact center operations, ideally in a regulated legal environment, and knows how to get results through a team they don't directly employ. You'll start each day knowing exactly what is in every queue, where the backlog is building, and which agents need to move. You'll spend it in shared Slack channels with the vendor, in Salesforce and Zendesk, and in the reporting you build. And you'll end it with a clear read on volume, productivity, and quality for our leadership team. As we grow, the role expands to lead our internal Tier 1 contact center operations as well.
We're moving fast and plan to fill this role within the next two weeks. Apply today: we review applications daily and move quickly with strong candidates.

What You'll Do

  • Own the day-to-day relationship with our contact center vendor: run the daily and weekly operating cadence, set priorities, resolve escalations, and hold the vendor accountable to service levels, productivity targets, and quality standards.
  • Run workforce management across every queue the vendor operates for us (inbound reception, claimant screening and qualification, outbound follow-up with accepted claimants, application prep and document review, and claim submission): forecast volume from our pipeline, set agent allocation by workstream, plan hiring classes and ramp timelines, and keep coverage aligned to Eastern Time business hours.
  • Monitor queues and backlogs throughout the day in Salesforce and the vendor's daily reports; spot bottlenecks early and move agents, adjust priorities, or escalate before service slips.
  • Be the vendor's primary point of contact in our shared Slack channels: answer questions, clarify process and policy, unblock agents, and make sure guidance is consistent and documented.
  • Build and maintain custom reporting: daily queue and backlog views, productivity and conversion metrics (contact rate, accepted-to-submitted, submissions per agent per day), quality scores, and a weekly readout for leadership.
  • Own quality: define call and casework standards, run QA and calibration sessions with vendor team leads, review calls and records in Salesforce, and drive coaching and corrective action plans.
  • Keep the status and flag workflows between the vendor and our internal teams clean (queue handoffs, contact gates, and record status in Salesforce and Zendesk), and partner with our tech and operations teams when a process or automation needs to change.
  • Manage the operational side of the vendor contract: roster and hours reconciliation, invoice review, seat and headcount changes, and cost-per-outcome tracking with Finance.
  • Serve as the escalation point for claimant-impacting issues and make sure every interaction is professional, compassionate, and compliant with our scripts and regulatory requirements.
  • Over time, take on leadership of our internal Tier 1 contact center operations and build one consistent playbook across vendor and in-house teams.

What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years in contact center operations, including experience managing a team, a site, or a vendor/BPO relationship. Prior vendor or BPO management experience is ideal; extensive hands-on contact center leadership also works.
  • Experience in a regulated legal environment. Social Security Disability (SSI/SSDI) experience is strongly preferred; personal injury, mass tort, workers' compensation, insurance claims, or other legal intake and claims operations are also a great fit.
  • Proven workforce management skills: forecasting, capacity planning, scheduling, and intraday management across multiple queues.
  • Strong custom reporting and analytics skills. You build your own reports and dashboards (Salesforce reports, Google Sheets or Excel, and ideally a BI tool) and use them to make decisions.
  • A track record of managing remote teams effectively: structured cadences, clear written communication, and accountability without being in the room.
  • Salesforce and Zendesk experience is required: you are comfortable working lists, queues, and reports in Salesforce and managing tickets in Zendesk. Experience with contact center tooling (telephony/ACD, QA, WFM) is a plus.
  • Direct, organized communicator who can run a vendor huddle in the morning and brief executives in the afternoon.
  • Available Monday through Friday during Eastern Time business hours; authorized to work in the United States.
  • Nice to have: experience as an EDPNA or with SSA representative work; experience launching or scaling a BPO engagement; experience using AI tools in a contact center setting.
Why this role: You get real ownership from day one. You'll run the operation that drives our core business metric, see the results of your changes in the numbers within days rather than quarters, and report directly to leadership. The schedule is predictable (Monday through Friday, Eastern Time), the work is fully remote, and it matters: the people we serve are navigating a difficult process, and the quality of our contact center directly shapes their outcomes.
How to apply: We plan to fill this role within the next two weeks. Submit your resume along with a few sentences about the contact center or vendor operation you've managed (team size, queues or workstreams, and the results you drove). We review applications daily and will reach out to qualified candidates within a few business days.

jobs.description:
This is a full-time, remote position from Latin America.

About the Role

Our client is looking for a hands-on Accountant to own their accounting function end to end, leveraging AI and automation to make processes faster, more accurate, and more efficient than traditional accounting workflows.
In this role, you will manage day-to-day bookkeeping, lead the monthly close, prepare financial statements, and serve as the primary point of contact for external auditors. You will also take ownership of controller-level responsibilities, including cash flow management, vendor payments, and supporting accounts receivable collections.
You will work primarily through their internally developed accounting application, Book It, and Claude. Using Claude's existing skills and developing new ones, you will continuously improve accounting workflows, eliminate manual tasks, and strengthen internal controls.
You don't need to be a software engineer. They have already built an internal month-end close application that automates recurring journal entries, posts transactions directly to QuickBooks Online with supporting documentation, generates auditable balance sheet schedules, and verifies that balances reconcile to the ledger.
Your role is to operate and oversee these systems, validate their outputs, and identify opportunities to automate the next manual step.
If you've ever thought, "I could write a skill for this" halfway through a reconciliation, this role is for you.

Key Responsibilities

1. Accounting & Month-End Close

  • Own and execute the monthly close process from start to finish using their internally developed application.
  • Manage day-to-day bookkeeping in QuickBooks Online, including bank and credit card reconciliations, chart of accounts maintenance, and applying deposits to invoices.
  • Upload and review monthly source files, including Carta reports, benefits carrier invoices, and payroll allocations.
  • Review and approve proposed journal entries, ensuring accuracy before posting them to QuickBooks Online.
  • Maintain supporting documentation and ensure all balance sheet accounts are reconciled and supported by accurate schedules.

2. Financial Reporting & Audit

  • Prepare and issue monthly financial statements, including the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement.
  • Provide concise monthly variance and flux analysis commentary.
  • Support the preparation of quarterly investor reporting.
  • Lead the external audit process, serving as the primary contact for auditors.
  • Prepare audit PBC (Prepared by Client) schedules, supporting documentation, and respond to auditor inquiries.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage AI and automation to streamline audit preparation and reduce adjustments.

3. Controller & Financial Operations

  • Monitor daily cash balances and maintain a rolling cash flow forecast.
  • Proactively communicate potential cash shortfalls and liquidity concerns to the COO.
  • Manage the vendor payment cycle, including bill approvals, payment scheduling through Bill.com, and ensuring timely payments within cash constraints.
  • Complete vendor onboarding requirements, including W-9s, banking information, insurance certificates, and supplier questionnaires.
  • Support accounts receivable collections through aging reviews, payment reminders, and coordination with account management teams.

4. Specialized Accounting Operations

  • Manage invoice factoring activities, including submissions, payment and reserve reports, fee accruals, and clearing entries.
  • Use our internal accounting application to process and reconcile factoring-related transactions.
  • Maintain accurate supporting schedules for prepaids, prepaid commissions, accruals, notes payable (including SBA EIDL and shareholder loans), stock-based compensation, and other balance sheet accounts.

5. AI & Process Automation

  • Use Claude as a primary working environment to improve and automate accounting workflows.
  • Own, maintain, and continuously improve existing Claude skills covering close procedures, balance sheet schedules, and factoring processes.
  • Develop new reusable Claude skills and workflows whenever repetitive manual tasks can be automated.
  • Maintain a prioritized list of manual processes, evaluating automation opportunities based on time savings, risk reduction, and operational impact.
  • Partner with internal developers by translating accounting requirements into clear specifications, defining expected outcomes, and validating implemented solutions.
  • Keep accounting procedures and documentation up to date as processes evolve.

How You'll Work

AI is central to this role, not just an additional productivity tool. You will use Claude to execute accounting workflows, develop reusable skills, organize financial information, and continuously improve how the accounting function operates.

Our approach is built around a few principles:

  • Review, don't retype: Our internal application proposes journal entries and supporting schedules. You review, validate, and approve them rather than manually entering everything.
  • Strong internal controls: Nothing gets posted without human approval. If a control cannot be verified, it blocks the close. You are responsible for confirming what actually landed in QuickBooks Online.
  • Continuous improvement: When a task becomes repetitive, you look for opportunities to turn it into a reusable skill or automated workflow.
  • Clear documentation: You maintain accurate, practical procedures that allow others, including non-accountants, to understand and follow the process.
  • Collaboration with developers: You define what needs to be fixed or built, explain what the expected result should look like, and validate the outcome.
Tools & Technologies: Claude (Skills, Projects, and Connectors), QuickBooks Online, Google Sheets, Bill.com, Carta, BigQuery (read-only), Slack, and Asana.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 Days

  • Complete one full month-end close alongside the team.
  • Review existing accounting procedures and Claude skills.
  • Identify and document all remaining manual steps in the accounting workflow.
  • Begin taking ownership of bookkeeping and shadowing controller-level responsibilities.

First 60 Days

  • Independently execute the monthly close.
  • Improve or develop at least two Claude skills.
  • Issue a complete set of monthly financial statements using the existing workflows.
  • Take over day-to-day controller responsibilities.

First 90 Days

  • Fully own the month-end close calendar and financial reporting process.
  • Deliver the first automation improvement from the identified manual-process backlog.
  • Develop and implement an audit PBC preparation plan.

First 12 Months

  • Reduce the monthly close timeline from 20 business days to 5.
  • Deliver a clean external audit with no material adjustments.
  • Reduce post-close corrections quarter over quarter.
  • Build and maintain a documented library of Claude skills that can be used to onboard future accounting team members.

Requirements
Must-Haves

  • 4+ years of hands-on accounting experience, including ownership of the full monthly close process.
  • Strong knowledge of US GAAP, including accruals, prepaids, revenue recognition, stock-based compensation, and notes payable.
  • Experience preparing monthly financial statements and supporting external audits.
  • Daily, practical experience using Claude or a comparable AI tool for accounting or financial workflows, with examples of how you've applied it.
  • Experience creating at least one reusable Claude skill, project instruction set, or structured prompt workflow that others can follow.
  • Advanced proficiency in QuickBooks Online and spreadsheets.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a highly detail-oriented and skeptical approach to validating AI-generated outputs.
  • Ability to explain and substantiate financial figures and identify discrepancies before they become reporting issues.
  • Strong written communication skills and the ability to document accounting procedures clearly.
    •

Nice-to-Haves

  • CPA certification or currently pursuing CPA licensure.
  • Experience with invoice factoring or other receivables financing arrangements.
  • Experience in ad-tech, media, or marketplace revenue accounting.
  • Basic SQL knowledge and experience querying financial data in BigQuery.
  • Familiarity with Claude Code, MCP connectors, or no-code automation platforms such as Make or Zapier.
  • Previous experience as the first or sole accountant at a startup.
    •

What This Role Is Not

  • Not a software engineering position: You won't be expected to build or deploy applications. You will define accounting requirements and explain precisely how systems should work.
  • Not accounting by prompting: AI helps you work faster, but you remain responsible for reviewing, validating, and approving every financial figure.
  • Not a people-management role (yet): This is a hands-on individual contributor position. As the accounting function grows, the processes and skills you develop will help scale the team.
    •

About RYZ Labs:

RYZ Labs is a startup studio built in 2021 by two lifelong entrepreneurs. The founders of RYZ have worked at some of the world's largest tech companies and some of the most iconic consumer brands. They have lived and worked in Argentina for many years and have decades of experience in Latam. What brought them together is the passion for the early phases of company creation and the idea of attracting the brightest talents in order to build industry-defining companies in a post-pandemic world.
Our teams are remote and distributed throughout the US and Latam. They use the latest cutting-edge technologies in cloud computing to create applications that are scalable and resilient. We aim to provide diverse product solutions for different industries, planning to build a large number of startups in the upcoming years.
At RYZ, you will find yourself working with autonomy and efficiency, owning every step of your development. We provide an environment of opportunities, learning, growth, expansion and challenging projects. You will deepen your experience while sharing and learning from a team of great professionals and specialists.

Our values and what to expect:

Why Finch

The Senior DevOps / SRE engineer designs, builds and operates secure, resilient Azure platforms and production services. The role combines cloud platform engineering, site reliability engineering, infrastructure as code, CI/CD and software automation. The engineer works primarily with Terraform and
Bicep, develops automation and platform capabilities using .NET/C#, Python and PowerShell, and uses AI-assisted engineering tools such as Claude to accelerate delivery and troubleshooting while critically validating generated output.

Responsibilities

  • Design, provision and maintain Azure landing zones, management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and shared platform services using Terraform and Bicep.
    • Engineer Azure networking including hub-and-spoke VNets, NSGs, route tables, Azure Firewall, Front Door, Application Gateway/WAF, Private Link, Private DNS, VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute.
    • Build reusable Terraform and Bicep modules, manage remote state, perform plan/what-if validation, detect configuration drift and promote infrastructure changes through pull-request review and approvals.
    • Build and maintain CI/CD and release automation using Azure DevOps Pipelines and/or GitHub Actions; integrate Octopus Deploy where required.
    • Develop production-quality cloud and DevOps tooling using .NET/C#, Python and PowerShell, including APIs, Azure Functions, CLI utilities, integrations, compliance checks, reporting and operational automation.
    • Build and operate containerized workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Azure Container Apps, including container registries, scaling, health probes, deployment strategies and rollback.
    • Define service level indicators and objectives (SLIs/SLOs), monitoring, dashboards and actionable alerting; participate in on call, incident response, root-cause analysis and blameless postmortems.
    • Improve reliability, availability, performance, capacity and recoverability while reducing operational toil through automation and self-service platform capabilities.

    • Enforce security and governance using Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities, least-privilege Azure RBAC, workload identity federation, Azure Policy and Key Vault.
    • Design secretless deployment patterns where possible and enforce private connectivity, certificate lifecycle management, secure logging and restricted data-plane access.
    • Support governance and compliance requirements for regulated workloads, including PCI-DSS and

Requirements

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in DevOps, SRE, cloud infrastructure or platform engineering, with strong production support experience.
