    • Advanced Terraform and hands-on Bicep experience, including reusable module design, state management, imports, plan/what-if review and drift detection.
    • Strong hands-on development and automation skills in .NET/C#, Python and PowerShell; ability to build maintainable tooling rather than relying only on administrative scripts.
    • Experience building REST/API integrations and working with JSON, YAML, Git and common software engineering practices such as code review, testing, logging and error handling.
    • Hands-on experience with Azure DevOps and/or GitHub Actions, including YAML pipelines, approvals/checks, branch policies, reusable templates and secure authentication.
    • Experience with AKS, Azure Container Apps, Docker and Azure Container Registry, or equivalent Kubernetes/container platforms.
    • Solid SRE practices including SLIs/SLOs, observability, incident management, root-cause analysis, postmortems, capacity planning and operational automation.
    • Strong understanding of Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities, Azure RBAC, Key Vault, workload identity federation and least-privilege security.
    • Experience with Azure Monitor, Application Insights, Log Analytics and KQL for production troubleshooting and observability.
    • Ability to troubleshoot across application code, CI/CD, containers, Azure services, networking, identity

and observability layers.

  • Daily, effective use of AI-assisted engineering tools such as Claude, with critical review of AI-generated
    code, IaC and recommendations before production use.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Genomics
jobs.excerpt: About Feanix BioFeanix is rebuilding animal breeding from the genome up.
jobs.description:
About Feanix Bio

Feanix is rebuilding animal breeding from the genome up.

We’re a YC-backed startup using whole-genome sequencing and custom ML models to help dairy farmers make better breeding and herd management decisions. Our technology is genuinely novel: we can sequence a full genome from a single hair at a fraction of traditional industry costs, our models achieve ~90% prediction accuracy on traits where existing approaches sit closer to ~30%, and we’re pioneering farm-specific genomic predictions that turn genetics into practical, actionable decisions.

That technology is translating into real adoption. In a short time, we’ve grown to serve roughly 1% of the U.S. dairy industry, with many customers in the pipeline. We started with dairy because our founders grew up on dairy farms and understand firsthand the problems we’re solving. But genetics is foundational to every agricultural industry, and dairy is only the beginning.

We’re building Feanix with a small, high-caliber team where people have meaningful ownership and work end to end. There are no unnecessary layers and very little room for busywork — just difficult problems at the intersection of biology, data, and software that haven’t been solved before.

If you’re exceptional at what you do and want your work to have a measurable impact on an entire industry, we’d love to build it with you.

About The Role

Feanix’s main product Autopilot is a farm decision system. It tells dairy farmers what to do with every animal in the herd: which cows to breed and with what semen, which to cull, which to sell, and which heifers are worth raising. Those decisions are driven by herd records, lactation models, farm economics, and genomics, with one aim: making each farm as efficient and profitable as possible.

Genomics at Feanix runs from sample to result. We collect hair samples from animals, run our own sequencing process, and impute full genotypes against a reference panel. Those genotypes tell us what each animal is really worth, confirm who its parents are, and help farms avoid inbreeding as they choose which bulls to breed to which cows.

This is a production role, not a research one. Our genomics work supports research, but above all it feeds the decisions that run working dairies. Genotypes don’t make those calls alone: combined with each herd’s phenotypic data (milk, reproduction, health, and lifetime records), they decide which animals to breed, keep, and sell, every week.

The base methods behind these pipelines are strong, and so is the pipeline we’ve built to run it. What comes next is expanding it for much higher volume, tighter accuracy, and lower cost per sample as we grow from 20+ farms to hundreds. And dairy is where we started, not where we stop: the pipeline you build should be ready to carry other species and genomics uses beyond the herd decisions we deliver today.

We're building out genomics as a core capability of engineering, and this is our second genomics hire. You'd partner with our founding genomics engineer, who brings deep knowledge of the genetics and the methods behind them. You bring the production engineering. You’d lead how our genomics pipelines are built and run, taking them from manually orchestrated to fully automated under code, CI, and monitoring, and set the engineering standards for genomics as the team grows. Their domain depth plus your production experience is what makes the science run unattended, observably, and repeatably, every week, at hundreds of farms.

What You'll Own

The genomics team owns everything below together; you’re the one who leads on making it production-grade. The work is continuous: keep making the genomics processing pipeline more automated, more reliable, faster, and cheaper per sample, so that adding a farm adds samples, not engineering work.

  • The genomics pipeline as a production system. Sample → sequence → align → impute → genotype → parentage/trait, scheduled or triggered by new data, with retries, version pinning, and alerting.
  • A sample-state ledger. One authoritative record per sample of where it is (received, sequenced, passed coverage, imputed, called) and, if it stopped, why.
  • Parentage, end to end. Our parentage results already reach farms, built on the same genotypes, sample identities, and compute as the rest of genomics, so the team owns it end to end, from sample to result. You’d move fleet runs onto a schedule with completion and lateness alerts, and finish the readiness work that makes our already-built successor runner the system of record.
  • CI and deploys, in partnership with infrastructure. Our infrastructure engineer designs the CI and deploy path across engineering. You’d work with them to bring the genomics repositories onto it, so every change is tested and every pipeline and workflow version is managed in code and reviewed.
  • Cost and storage. A cost-per-sample view for sequencing compute and storage, and a lifecycle policy for data measured in hundreds of terabytes.
  • Lab and vendor intake. The handoff from our in-house sequencer, outside sequencing labs, and genotyping-chip providers into the pipeline.
  • Reproducible model training. Making breeding-value model training runnable and repeatable, so time goes to methods, not reruns.

You’ll work closely with others who own the pieces on either side. Our founding genomics engineer owns methods and confidence thresholds. You should understand them well enough to debug and push back, not redesign them. Model selection and promotion into breeding decisions, delivery of results into farmers’ herd software, and the platform-wide animal identity key each sit with other engineers. The genomics team owns sample identity and how samples attach to that key.

How We Work

Python end to end, with uv and pytest, on AWS. Genomics runs on a mix of compute chosen per workload: Modal for serverless Python, Nextflow workflows on AWS HealthOmics, AWS Batch, and GPU-accelerated alignment. Data lives in S3. The genomics toolchain includes Parabricks, samtools, bcftools, PLINK, GLIMPSE2, Beagle, KING, and JWAS. Terraform/OpenTofu and GitHub Actions provision and ship it. This is what you’ll work with, not a checklist to match.

Like everyone else, we're working out how humans and agents build software together. Our engineers direct agents against real work and build the harnesses that check that work. Quality comes from what happens around the code: specs, tests, verification. Nobody has this fully figured out, and that includes us.

What You Bring

  • Several years running scientific or bioinformatics pipelines in production (Nextflow, AWS HealthOmics or Batch, or similar), scheduled, monitored, and depended on by people other than you
  • Enough fluency in genomic data to debug it: FASTQ/BAM/VCF, PLINK, imputation (GLIMPSE, Beagle, or similar), and coverage and QC metrics
  • Experience building sample tracking, LIMS-like state, or another “where is every item, and why” system
  • Strong Python, and comfort with S3-scale data, idempotent pipelines, retries, and alerting
  • Cost awareness with large data: storage lifecycle and compute spend per unit
  • A track record of working alongside scientists, translating methods into reliable systems and asking good questions about them
  • Daily, load-bearing use of coding agents, and a real position on where they break down

Preferred Qualifications

You've likely held a title like bioinformatics engineer, data engineer, or software engineer on a genomics or research-platform team. That title matters less to us than two other things: that you think creatively about how agents are changing this job, and that you're motivated by taking a working pipeline and making it run at 10x the volume, cheaper and more reliably.

  • Livestock, plant, or human population genomics
  • Parentage or pedigree work: SNP-based parentage verification, kinship, or reconciling recorded pedigrees with genotypes
  • Production experience with genotype imputation or sequencing pipelines (alignment, variant calling)
  • Genomic prediction (GBLUP and relatives); useful, not expected
  • LIMS or sample-tracking integration with a wet lab
  • Having supported a small team through a period of rapid growth
  • Time at a sequencing lab or genomics service company
  • Terraform/OpenTofu
  • Agriculture experience isn't required, but an interest doesn't hurt

Ultimately, we care far more about demonstrated ability, curiosity, and problem-solving than pedigree or conventional career paths.

Logistics

  • Reports to the Platform Engineering Manager
  • Remote (US), with 10am–2pm Pacific core hours regardless of where you're based
  • Travel 15–20%, including visits to commercial dairies and time with the team at our headquarters in Scotts Valley, CA
  • Engineers share an on-call and triage rotation: weekly, with a written handbook, and weekend work requires explicit sign-off rather than being assumed. Building the alerting that keeps genomics on-call quiet is part of this job.

Why You'll Enjoy Working With Us

  • The People: we have an amazing group of talented, smart and fun people on our team!
  • The Company: we are building something novel that has not been done before which is making a huge impact on the dairy industry!
  • The Experience: you get to come in and be a part of ground breaking work that will have a huge impact on generations to come!

Compensation and Benefits

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship or transfers at this time.

Actual starting pay for this role is determined by a variety of factors including but not limited to qualifications, experience, relevant skills, education, and geographic location. Employees are offered a variety of benefits to empower them with the resources and flexibility they need to enjoy success on the job and to live a healthy life.

We offer a flexible, remote-friendly work environment for most roles, along with a growing benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401k, pet insurance, flexible paid time off; and paid parental leave, including up to twelve weeks of paid leave and/or supplemental pay coordination with applicable state benefits.

Job Description

A bit about this role

Are you looking to build your career in cybersecurity while making a real difference for the members who depend on us? Our Cybersecurity Governance, Risk Management, and Compliance (GRC) team is looking for a Third-Party Security Risk Analyst to help run the day-to-day work of our Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program. You'll work alongside senior team members to assess our vendors, document risk, and keep our partnerships secure. It's hands-on work that directly shapes how safely we operate.

Your Responsibilities and Impact will include:

Support the onboarding and reassessment of third-party vendors under the Security purview. You'll gather information, document risks, facilitate stakeholder discussions, evaluate inherent and residual risk, and track follow-up actions and remediation activities.

  • Impact Assessments & Tiering: Perform initial impact assessments on new and existing vendors and assign risk tiers using established criteria, such as data classification, system access, criticality to operations, and regulatory exposure. The tier sets the level and cadence of due diligence each vendor requires.
  • Risk Assessments: Carry out standardized third-party risk assessments under the direction of senior team members, including reviewing security questionnaires, SOC reports, and supporting evidence.
  • Assessment Tracking: Track assessment status and follow up with risk domain owners so submissions arrive on time.
  • Risk Documentation: Document risk findings and ratings, including inherent and residual risk scores, clearly and consistently.
  • Remediation Follow-Up: Monitor open findings and remediation commitments, and escalate overdue items.
  • Contract Support: Help verify that vendor contracts include the required Infosec addendum clauses.
  • Program Documentation: Help maintain procedures, templates, and guidelines so the program stays organized and repeatable.
  • Audit Support: Support internal and external audits of the vendor risk program by preparing evidence and responding to requests.
  • Innovation: Support efforts to improve AI-enabled automation into the vendor risk program.
  • Emerging AI Risk: Help evaluate AI usage in vendors’ products and services, including how they protect data, manage model and platform risk, and meet contractual and regulatory expectations.

At the Heart of It

You'll execute the full TPRM lifecycle, from initial vendor assessments through ongoing monitoring and offboarding. Along the way you'll help third-party services join our ecosystem without compromising our security or our values.


Why Step Into This Role

This role is a strong foundation for a career in cybersecurity GRC. You'll get direct mentorship from experienced TPRM and security professionals and exposure to Legal, Procurement, Compliance, and ERM. You'll also get the chance to grow your skills while contributing to Devoted's resilience against cybersecurity threats.


Required skills and experience:

  • Practical experience in third-party risk management, vendor management, procurement, information security, compliance, or audit (relevant internships count)
  • Basic understanding of third-party risk concepts, governance policies, and common security frameworks (e.g., HITRUST, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, SOC 2)
  • Exposure to vendor lifecycle procedures, including onboarding, ongoing monitoring, and offboarding
  • Exposure to contract clause review for security, privacy, and business resilience controls
  • Familiarity with findings or vulnerability remediation tracking
  • Awareness of software and hardware supply chain risk
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and spot gaps or inconsistencies in vendor responses
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple assessments at once
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort working cross-functionally with Legal, Finance, Risk, Procurement, and business stakeholders

Desired skills and experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in risk management, information security, privacy, compliance, business, or a related discipline
  • 3-5 years of experience in a third-party risk management role, including vendor management
  • Familiarity with cloud security controls and shared responsibility models across major providers (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), including how to evaluate a vendor's cloud environment during an assessment
  • Awareness of AI-related risks and controls, such as data usage and retention, model transparency, and responsible AI practices, and of emerging frameworks like the NIST AI Risk Management Framework or ISO/IEC 42001
  • Knowledge of healthcare regulations such as HIPAA and HITRUST
  • Relevant certifications, or progress toward them (e.g., CISA, CIA)

jobs.description:
We are seeking a Senior Accountant to join our Revenue Accounting team, focused primarily on deferred revenue and contract asset reconciliation and technical revenue recognition (ASC 606) deal reviews within a healthcare information technology environment. The Revenue Accounting team this role would join owns some of the company's most significant and complex revenue arrangements and has direct visibility to Finance and business leadership. This role is well-suited for a detail-oriented accounting professional with strong technical accounting fundamentals and solid knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles. Candidates should be comfortable partnering with sales, legal, billing, and finance teams on complex revenue matters.


The ideal candidate combines a strong revenue accounting foundation with prior SaaS or technology industry experience — comfortable applying ASC 606 across both hosted and on-premise deployments, under both subscription and license revenue models, and skilled at evaluating multi-element contracts, contract modifications, and other non-standard deal structures. This is a strong opportunity for a technical accountant to deepen their revenue accounting expertise in a complex, fast-growing segment of the healthcare technology industry.


What You'll Contribute:


  • Owns the end-to-end reconciliation of deferred revenue and contract asset balances, ensuring accuracy and completeness across all customer accounts and product lines, spanning both hosted and on-premise deployments and both subscription and license revenue models.
  • Prepares and maintains detailed deferred revenue and contract asset roll-forward schedules on a monthly and quarterly basis, analyzing activity drivers such as billings, revenue recognition, contract modifications, and terminations.
  • Determines the appropriate contract balance sheet classification — contract asset versus deferred revenue (contract liability) — for each customer arrangement based on the relationship between cumulative revenue recognized and cumulative amounts billed or collected.
  • Records and reviews revenue transactions in compliance with ASC 606 and company revenue recognition policies.
  • Ensure revenue, deferred revenue, and contract asset balances are accurately recognized, recorded, and reported in accordance with US GAAP (ASC 606).
  • Performs monthly close activities including journal entries, account reconciliations, and variance analysis related to revenue, deferred revenue, and contract asset accounts.
  • Ensures proper cut-off and completeness of revenue recorded across customer accounts and service lines.
  • Investigates and resolves reconciling items between the billing system, revenue subledger, and general ledger in a timely manner.
  • Partners with billing, collections, and systems teams to ensure deferred revenue and contract asset data integrity across source systems.
  • Performs technical accounting reviews of new and modified customer contracts to assess revenue recognition treatment under ASC 606, including identification of performance obligations, determination of transaction price, and allocation of SSP.
  • Evaluates complex arrangements such as multi-element deals, contract modifications, variable consideration, and bundled offerings to determine appropriate accounting treatment.
  • Prepares technical accounting memos documenting revenue recognition conclusions for significant or non-standard arrangements.
  • Serves as a subject matter resource for internal stakeholders — including sales, legal, and deal desk teams — on revenue recognition implications during the deal structuring process.
  • Coordinates with external auditors on technical revenue matters, providing supporting documentation and responding to inquiries.
  • Supports SOX control requirements related to deferred revenue and contract assets, including preparation of reconciliations and supporting evidence for preparer/reviewer sign-off.
  • Identifies trends or anomalies in deferred revenue and contract asset balances and escalates findings with supporting analysis.
  • Assists in the preparation of revenue-related schedules for financial reporting and audit support, and supports internal and external audit requests related to revenue recognition and deferred balances.
  • Timely delivery of financial information and analysis to stakeholders.
  • Assists in the development and documentation of accounting policies related to revenue recognition.
  • Completes special projects as assigned on an ad hoc basis.

Required Qualifications:


Education:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance or related field – or equivalent (Required)

Work Experience:

  • 3+ years relevant work experience (Required)

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:


  • Excellent analytical skills to assist in financial analysis required
  • Knowledge of SEC regulatory agency reporting requirements and standards
  • Knowledge of internal controls and SOX requirements
  • Ability to translate large, raw datasets into audit-ready, GAAP-compliant financial information
  • Strong working knowledge of ASC 606 and its application to SaaS/technology revenue arrangements, including both hosted and on-premise deployments and both subscription and license revenue models
  • Ability to distinguish and properly account for contract assets versus deferred revenue (contract liabilities) based on the timing relationship between performance and billing/cash collection under ASC 606
  • Ability to evaluate complex, multi-element contracts and apply sound revenue recognition judgment to non-standard deal structures
  • Familiarity with healthcare IT industry dynamics — electronic health records (EHR), revenue cycle management (RCM), and payer interface/connectivity solutions — and how they influence contract and revenue recognition complexity
  • Comfortable managing high contract and customer volume characteristic of a customer base composed of small-to-medium, independent physician practices across varied specialties

Preferred Qualifications:


  • 4-7 years relevant work experience
  • 2+ years SaaS industry work experience
  • Public accounting experience
  • Revenue accounting experience
  • SaaS / Technology Industry experience
  • Contract accounting experience under ASC 606, including multi-element arrangements and variable consideration
  • Healthcare IT or healthcare technology industry experience
  • Certified Public Accountant
  • SaaS/technology industry revenue accounting experience, spanning hosted and on-premise deployments as well as subscription and license revenue models
  • Contract accounting experience, including multi-element arrangements, variable consideration, and SSP allocation under ASC 606
  • Experience with a customer base of small-to-medium, independent physician practices, where high contract/customer volume and varied deal terms increase reconciliation complexity
  • Revenue and billing systems experience (e.g., Zuora, Oracle, Salesforce, or comparable revenue automation platforms)
  • General ledger and ERP systems experience (e.g., Workday, Oracle, or comparable platforms)
  • Advanced Excel and data tools (Power Query, SQL) to reconcile high-volume subscription and usage-based billing data
  • Close automation platforms (BlackLine, FloQast, Trintech)

Working Arrangements:

  • Standard work week or as defined by assignment requirements
  • Primarily works in standard office environment or remotely

  • On-call and after hours work during peak times including end of month/quarter/year; during this time PTO is limited to meet business needs

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The dynamic professional we seek is a leader with these qualifications.

Technical platform narrative

Product demonstration strategy

About the work

You'll work on the macOS sensor for CrowdStrike Falcon, an on-device security agent. It monitors file, process, network and identity activity, blocks malicious behavior, and streams telemetry to the cloud. The sensor runs entirely in user space as a System Extension. Much of the code is shared with Windows and Linux. The work requires high concurrency, high reliability, careful attention to memory & CPU usage and performance.

Required

  • Languages: modern C++ (C++17/20) and Swift 6 (async/await, actors, strict concurrency checking). Also Objective-C++ to bridge Swift, C++ and C APIs.

o XCTest, sanitizers, fuzzing, and xcodebuild-based CI.

o Apple Silicon and Intel.

through the engineering lifecycle.

  • Develop and maintain cross-process, cross-thread, performance-critical code paths where correctness, latency, reliability, and stability are important.

Technical Ownership

  • Own well-scoped features across the engineering lifecycle, including design, implementation, testing, deployment, telemetry, and live-site debugging.
  • Contribute to design and code reviews, and apply engineering practices for testability, performance, reliability, and long-term maintainability.
  • Contribute to iterative improvements to Windows client technologies in an agile engineering environment with frequent releases.
  • Investigate customer and production issues, determine root causes, and implement engineering improvements that reduce recurrence.
  • Share systems-level knowledge through design discussions and code reviews, and contribute to raising engineering quality across the team.

Technologies

  • C++ for native Windows and systems-level development.

You'll own everything behind that moment: the real-time connection layer, the API, the job pipeline and the cloud infrastructure every device talks to. Ready to be a Titan?
ServiceTitan is building the Developer Platform for enterprise-scale SaaS: a shared engineering ecosystem that powers seamless, high-velocity software delivery across our entire product footprint.

This is not a collection of script-runners. Our DevX platform is the runtime, framework, build, deployment, guardrail, and telemetry layer that lets hundreds of engineers ship code safely, observably, and at enterprise scale.

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to be the deepest technical voice on our DevX platform team. This is an individual-contributor role with outsized scope: you'll set technical direction, make architecture calls that other engineers build against, and personally ship the hardest, highest-leverage parts of the platform. You won't manage people, but you'll be expected to lead through influence — raising the technical bar for engineers and managers alike.

We need someone with deep production scars, strong systems intuition, and the judgment to know when to go deep on a gnarly problem versus when to unblock the team and move on. You should be comfortable being the technical backstop for a small, senior-heavy team and the person other engineers (and their managers) come to when something is architecturally ambiguous or on fire.

What You'll Build

You will be a primary technical owner across foundational DevX platform capabilities, including:

  • Environments: Cloud development environments (CDEs), on-demand provisioning, high-fidelity mocking, data seeding, and configuration management.

  • A track record of raising the technical bar for teams they're not formally managing — through review, mentorship, and design leadership.

  • Hands-on experience building with or on top of coding agent runtimes (e.g., Codex, Copilot, Cursor, or similar) — not just using them as an end user, but integrating or extending them as platform infrastructure.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience designing or operating internal developer platforms, custom build networks, or internal control planes at multi-hundred-engineer scale.

Being human isn’t about checking every box on a list. It’s about the experiences we have, people we meet, and the perspectives we share. jobs.excerpt: About AvaazAvaaz is an international campaigning and advocacy organisation that provides its global membership of almost 70 million people with opportunities to make our world a better place.
jobs.description:
About Avaaz

Avaaz is an international campaigning and advocacy organisation that provides its global membership of almost 70 million people with opportunities to make our world a better place.

We’re one of the world’s largest online global campaigning movements, with people from every corner in the world taking action to close the gap between the world we have and the world most people everywhere want. This includes protecting human rights worldwide, supporting indigenous struggles, saving our planet from climate change and other threats, and fighting to stop disinformation and other cyber threats from undermining our democracies.

Our model enables people to channel their voices into a powerful collective force at tipping point moments to impact the pressing global challenges of our time, from climate and ecological collapse to human rights abuses and the dismantling of democracy.

Avaaz is funded through small donations from individual Avaaz members, no big money from governments or corporations. This keeps us independent and allows us to keep a laser focus on doing what the world needs.

Language Associate (Dutch) - Part-Time Position (Approx. 20 hours/week)

This is an exciting consultant position that offers a unique opportunity to support large-scale social change efforts. Language Associates bring Avaaz to millions of people each week by translating Avaaz campaigns from English into key languages and rewriting them to be fitting to local contexts. This role requires strong written communication skills and cultural awareness that allow you to capture the heart of Avaaz’ campaigns and powerfully translate them into Dutch language.

The successful candidate for this part-time position (20 hours/week) will work closely with the Dutch language lead and with the Member Engagement and Community Petitions teams, and they will report to an Avaaz staffer. Please note that this position is on a freelance/independent contractor basis.

Responsibilities

  • Translate Avaaz campaigns from English to Dutch to turn them into strong, emotive, and compelling campaigns to send out in The Netherlands and Belgium, and to Dutch-speaking members around the world.
  • Hands-on technical support for campaign development, including setting up email blasts and landing pages in the Avaaz website backend interface, and supporting the drafting and testing of campaigns.
  • Looking for sources for campaigns -- finding relevant, issue-specific, supporting materials from the press, NGOs, etc.
  • Monitor and enhance the Dutch Avaaz website and other tools for functionality and language errors, supporting clear and effective communication with members.
  • Support the Dutch campaign team to write and edit excellent campaign materials such as briefings, advocacy letters, and press releases. Translate and/or edit other materials as necessary: Media material, content for social media etc.
  • Reviewing, managing, and supporting the petitions published by Dutch members on the Avaaz Community Petitions website.

Qualifications

  • Excellent written and oral communication, and translation skills in Dutch, combined with creative thinking to craft engaging texts.
  • Excellent communication skills in English, the Avaaz team’s working language.
  • Professionalism, efficiency, and results-oriented delivery on short timelines.
  • Flexibility and ability to adapt to (somewhat) varying weekly workloads.
  • Passion and commitment to global justice, citizen empowerment, and social change.
  • Strong teamwork skills, comfortable in a highly collaborative culture, and a hierarchical team structure.
  • Proficient in Google Suite and online communication systems (Slack, Zoom, etc).
  • Ideally: cultural and linguistic understanding of regional differences (e.g. the Netherlands and Belgium), to guarantee Avaaz content can be understood across Dutch-speaking regions.

Compensation

This is an independent contractor role, paid at an hourly rate of €25,- depending on experience and location. Contractors are responsible for their own taxes and statutory contributions in their country of residence.

Location

Avaaz is a virtual organization, with most of our work done online. Our staff and contractors are based in locations all over the world. For this position, the candidate would ideally be based in the European/Middle East/African time zones.

Application Timeline

We are reviewing applications on a rolling basis, and encourage all candidates to submit applications as soon as possible.

Our Recruitment Process

Avaaz undertakes a comprehensive recruitment procedure designed to select the most talented candidate for any given position. The recruitment process is comprised of the following steps:

  1. Application Review
  2. Screening Call
  3. Written exercise
  4. Final Interview
  5. Offer Call

Avaaz’s Commitment to Equity and Inclusion

As a global organization with millions of members around the world, it’s important to us that our team reflects the diversity needed to lead a movement of people from across the planet, rising to meet some of the most complex challenges humanity has ever faced. We believe we can only succeed by building a diverse team full of fresh perspectives and original ideas, and we are committed to creating a working environment in which everyone has an equal opportunity to fulfill their potential.

Our team includes English as a first language, as well as second language speakers, the self-taught and university-educated, people with all sorts of professional backgrounds. If doing the job you just read about would make you excited to come to work every day, if you’re talented, hard-working, and committed to making a difference, we want you to apply.

Avaaz does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, colour, ancestry, language and accent, national origin, citizenship, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, family/parental or marital status, political affiliation, religion, socioeconomic class, caste, disability or any other characteristic protected by law.

We’ll provide reasonable accommodations for qualified applicants with disabilities or special needs to participate in the application process, so please let us know if you have such a request when you apply.

Please do not send your application via email or LinkedIn. Only applications received via the form online on our website will be considered. Thank you!

jobs.excerpt: We’re hunting for a talented direct response video editor and static designer who can craft paid media ads (video and static) that stop the scroll and sell.
jobs.description:
We’re hunting for a talented direct response video editor and static designer who can craft paid media ads (video and static) that stop the scroll and sell. O’Connell Digital Media Group is an Inc. 5000 direct-response agency that has managed hundreds of millions in profitable ad spend for some of the top direct-response advertisers in the world. You’ll join a veteran team of account directors, media buyers, creative strategists and video editors who share a common goal: generate clicks that convert into high ROAS sales and scale ad spend.

So, if you’re obsessed with performance ads that convert, have edited at high volume in an agency or fast-scaling in-house team, and…

  • You LOVE taking a script and seeing the finished ad in your head before you open Premiere…
  • You LOVE building the first three seconds that stop the thumb…
  • You LOVE sweating the B-roll, the text, the music and the sound until the story lands…
  • You LOVE using AI tools to make ads that were impossible a year ago…
  • You LOVE seeing the numbers on your ads and finding out why one won…

… then please keep reading as you may be the perfect fit.

Especially if you’re tired of assembly-line edits with no feedback on what worked… tired of the freelance hustle chasing your next project… or stuck inside a single brand, cutting the same content over and over.

Note: Please do not apply if your editing experience is limited to weddings, corporate video, organic social or YouTube content, or to stitching UGC clips into a template.

What Are the Key Points?

  • Core Compensation: $1,500 - $1,750 USD per month
  • Location: 100% remote
  • Hours: 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. ET, Monday to Friday (adjustable for those outside the US)
  • Position: Full-time contractor
  • Culture: Accountable, transparent and obsessed with performance
  • #1 Objective: Deliver ads that convert, on time, on spec and on quality

Note: For those applying outside the US, hours may be adjusted to a heavily overlapping schedule we agree on together.

Who Will You Report To?

Hello, my name is Tom Clayson, Head of Creative at O'Connell Media, and I need your help.

I joined O'Connell Media just under a year ago to transform the creative team into one that can scale to meet the projected client growth demands. Our video editors work in small pods, each led by an Editing Team Lead, and with most of the heavy lifting done, I’m now expanding the editing team for the next leg of growth. That’s where you come in.

The volume of ads we need to ship based on our forecast exceeds our current capacity. It’s a good problem to have… but it’s still a problem. I’m hiring editors who can take a strategist’s script and brief and deliver a finished ad that needs no rescue from anyone downstream. You’ll join a pod, work day to day with strategists, and get coaching from me and your team lead along the way.

What’s the Ideal Candidate’s Background?

You’ve been editing direct-response video ads for paid social (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok) or YouTube for at least two years, in a high-volume agency or a fast-scaling in-house team. Cutting multiple new ads a week is your normal week. You’ve edited for supplement, health or wellness offers that drive traffic to long-form funnels like VSLs and advertorials and/or performance-based e-comm funnels.

You’re an expert in Premiere Pro. After Effects is a strong plus and Photoshop. Plus you’re deeply comfortable with AI in the edit: digital twins, voice cloning, video cloning, AI-generated B-roll and images, and AI captioning. We don’t force a single tool (Higgsfield is our main AI platform today), but we want to know exactly which tools you’re proficient in and what you’ve made with them.

Most importantly… you edit for marketing, not for content. You know the first three seconds decide whether anyone sees the rest. You understand the structure of a persuasive ad, from hook to problem to mechanism to proof to offer to call to action, and you cut so the viewer never has a reason to leave. You study why ads win on your own time because, quite frankly, you simply can’t get enough of this stuff.

What Will You Be Responsible For?

Put simply, you’ll deliver the creative strategist’s brief on time, on spec and on quality. Here’s what that looks like:

  • The Brief: Take the script and brief from the creative strategist in ClickUp, ask the questions that matter before you start, and lock the turnaround date.
  • The Hook: Build thumb-stopping openers. We test the first three seconds, so you’ll often deliver several wildly different openers for the same script.
  • The Story: Choose the B-roll, on-screen text, graphics, music and sound design that make the viewer see themselves in the ad. Not the first clip you find, the right one.
  • The AI Build: Produce digital twins, cloned voices, generated B-roll and other AI assets when the brief calls for them.
  • The Finish: Deliver a fully dialed-in cut with captions, graphics and sound design, checked against our editing checklist, ready for strategist and client approval.
  • The Revisions: Take revision notes from the strategist and your Editing Team Lead, turn them fast, and learn from every round.

How Will Your Time Be Spent?

While any given week varies with client demands, here’s a rough estimate:

  • 65% Editing: Building ads from brief to finished cut
  • 20% Revisions and Polish: Working with your Editing Team Lead and strategists to perfect each ad
  • 15% Learning: Studying winning ads, new formats and new AI tools

What Does Initial Success Look Like?

We hold every ad to a clear standard. Here’s what success looks like as you ramp up:

  • Great-Enough First Cuts: Your first cut matches the brief and the strategist’s vision, so revisions make the ad better instead of fixing it.
  • On Time, On Spec: You hit your weekly ad quota and turnaround dates without letting quality slip.
  • Hooks That Hold: Your openers earn the view and your edits keep attention all the way to the call to action.
  • AI in Real Ads: Within your first month, AI assets you built are running in live ads.

What’s It Like Working at O'Connell Media?

We’ve built the editing team around what the best editors want most: clear direction, fast feedback and the chance to see their work win.

  • A Pod That Has Your Back: You’ll work in a small pod with an Editing Team Lead who reviews your work and coaches you daily.
  • Clear Briefs: Strategists hand you scripts with visual direction, so you’re never guessing what the ad should be.
  • Access to Data: You’ll see how your ads perform, spot the patterns and build on what’s winning.
  • Clear Feedback: Direct feedback from your Editing Team Lead and routine coaching from me.
  • Subject Variety: A range of clients and offers, with fresh subject matter all the time.
  • A Rhythm That Works: A short daily stand-up keeps every ad moving.
  • Room to Grow: Our Editing Team Leads come from inside the team. Your results decide how fast you move up.

Requirements

  • 2+ Years of DR Video Editing: You’ve edited video ads for paid social or YouTube that ran with real spend, ideally for supplement, health or wellness offers.
  • High-Volume Experience: You’ve worked in an agency or fast-scaling in-house team where cutting multiple new ads a week was the norm.
  • Premiere Pro Expert: Premiere Pro is your home. After Effects is a strong plus.
  • AI-Fluent: You’ve used AI tools in real ads for digital twins, voice cloning, video cloning, generated B-roll and captions, and you keep up as the tools change.
  • Visual Storyteller: You turn a script into a sequence of images, text and sound that persuades, and you can explain why each choice is there.
  • Marketing Mindset: You understand what moves hook rate, hold rate, CTR and conversion rate, and you edit to move them.
  • Detail Obsessed: Your cuts arrive double-checked, captioned and compliant. Nobody downstream has to fix your work.
  • Organized Under Pressure: You keep multiple ads moving at once, keep ClickUp current and hit your deadlines.
  • Fluent English: You work effortlessly in an English-speaking team, in writing and on calls.
  • Constant Upskilling: You relentlessly improve by studying winning ads, deconstructing edits and seeking feedback.

Customer Experience Manager – Client Relations & After-Sales Operations

Location: Quezon City

Department: Customer Experience / Accounts & After-Sales Management

Employment Type: Full-Time, Monday-Friday (CWW)

Position Overview

Are you a high-performing Real Estate Customer Service Officer, Senior Specialist, or Team Lead ready to elevate your career into full managerial leadership?

We are seeking a dynamic, client-facing Customer Experience Manager to oversee our buyer journey, after-sales operations, customer care, and client accounts management. In this role, you will bridge the gap between frontline customer care, loan processing, and executive operations. You will lead a dedicated team of associates to deliver exceptional service, resolve complex account disputes, streamline property turnovers, and drive collection efficiency.

This position is ideal for an experienced supervisor or rising officer with deep developer-side experience who thrives in direct client interactions and is eager to own and optimize end-to-end customer service operations.

Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities

1. Client-Facing Excellence & Escalation Management

Serve as the senior point of contact for high-value clients, buyers, and brokers, ensuring an exceptional client journey from project reservation through unit turnover.

Direct customer service resolution efforts, personally handling escalated client complaints, account disputes, and sensitive payment or turnover concerns.

Conduct face-to-face buyer meetings, property orientations, and virtual consultations to negotiate payment restructures, resolve billing disputes, and minimize sales cancellations.

2. Operational Leadership & Team Empowerment

Lead, mentor, and supervise a team of Customer Care, Billing, and Documentation Associates to achieve high service standards and operational targets.

Establish clear team KPIs, monitor daily performance, and foster a professional, solution-oriented service culture.

Design and implement Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for customer handling, query resolution, and account servicing.

3. Accounts Management & After-Sales Coordination

Oversee the end-to-end after-sales process, including Statement of Account (SOA) issuances, account reconciliations, aging analysis, and overdue account interventions.

Collaborate closely with Sales Administration and Finance teams to facilitate smooth unit turnovers, title conveyances, and loan take-outs (Bank, Pag-IBIG/HDMF).

Coordinate with Legal and Collections teams regarding demand letters, defaulted account restructuring, and account reopenings.

4. Process Optimization & System Management

Leverage real estate CRM and ERP platforms (e.g., SAP, NetSuite, Salesforce) to track customer interaction metrics, collection turnaround times, and resolution rates.

Present monthly customer satisfaction (CSAT) reports, delinquency updates, and operational bottlenecks directly to executive leadership (COO/Management Committee).

Qualifications & Candidate Requirements

Industry Experience: Minimum 5+ years of continuous experience in Real Estate Development or Property Management handling customer care, after-sales, billing, or accounts management. (No BPO-only backgrounds).

Leadership Background: At least 2+ years in a supervisory, team lead, or senior officer capacity with proven experience mentoring direct reports or leading project workflows.

Core Skills:

Proven client-facing negotiation and dispute resolution skills.

Solid understanding of real estate documentation (CTS, DOAS, Reservation Agreements), property turnover clearance, and buyer financing (Pag-IBIG / Bank / In-House).

Familiarity with enterprise software (SAP, NetSuite, Salesforce, or similar CRM tools) and advanced MS Excel.

Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Real Estate Management, Finance, or any related field (Master’s/MBA or Civil Service eligibility is a plus).

Attributes: High emotional intelligence, strong command of written and verbal communication, excellent problem-solving ability under pressure, and a drive for career growth into senior leadership.

jobs.description:
Job Description

PTG is seeking a Vice President, ServiceNow Practice to lead the strategy, growth, commercial performance, and overall direction of our ServiceNow business.


PTG has established a growing ServiceNow practice with strong public sector experience, an expanding customer base, established sales and delivery capabilities, and significant opportunity for continued growth. As the practice enters its next stage, we are looking for an experienced ServiceNow leader who has successfully helped build and scale a consulting and services business and understands how to turn market opportunity into a focused, repeatable growth strategy. This is not simply a sales leadership position.


The Vice President will serve as the senior leader of the ServiceNow practice, bringing together Sales, Solution Consulting, and Operations & Delivery under a clear strategy and operating model. This leader will be responsible for determining where and how PTG competes, strengthening PTG's position within the ServiceNow ecosystem, building a scalable growth roadmap, developing the team and organizational structure as the practice grows, and ensuring commercial decisions translate into successful and profitable customer outcomes.


The right candidate will bring deep ServiceNow ecosystem experience, strong consulting and services business acumen, and the judgment that comes from having helped scale a ServiceNow business before. This individual should be equally comfortable setting long-term direction, coaching a team through a complex pursuit, challenging an investment decision, engaging ServiceNow leadership, and making the day-to-day decisions necessary to move a growing practice forward.

What You'll Own

Practice Strategy & Direction

  • Own and develop the strategic roadmap for PTG's ServiceNow practice, establishing clear priorities for near-term execution and long-term growth.
  • Determine where PTG should compete, how the practice should differentiate, and where the company should invest to drive sustainable growth.
  • Evaluate opportunities across net-new business, install-base expansion, managed services, packaged offerings, new capabilities, partnerships, and other potential growth channels.
  • Translate strategy into clear priorities so investment, hiring, sales activity, capability development, and go-to-market decisions support a common direction.
  • Build the structure and operating discipline necessary to scale the practice without creating unnecessary complexity or bureaucracy.
  • Continuously assess the practice's strengths, gaps, market position, and growth opportunities and adjust the roadmap accordingly.
  • Develop business cases and recommendations for significant new offerings, investments, partnerships, and strategic initiatives.

Commercial & Growth Leadership

  • Own the overall commercial performance of the ServiceNow practice, including revenue growth, pipeline, bookings, pricing strategy, deal economics, and profitable growth.
  • Establish and lead the sales strategy for the practice.
  • Own pipeline management, forecasting discipline, account strategy, territory and account alignment, and overall sales performance.
  • Establish expectations, processes, and accountability across the sales organization while maintaining PTG's collaborative, discovery-led approach.
  • Provide experienced guidance on deal structure, pricing, commercial models, and pursuit strategy.
  • Serve as an executive leader on PTG's largest, most complex, or strategically important pursuits.
  • Identify opportunities to turn successful customer engagements, capabilities, and solutions into repeatable growth motions.
  • Open doors and leverage industry relationships where appropriate while enabling Account Executives to maintain day-to-day ownership of their accounts and opportunities.
  • Assess the sales organization as the practice grows and recommend additional talent, roles, territories, or capabilities as needed.

ServiceNow Ecosystem & Market Leadership

  • Strengthen PTG's position, visibility, and credibility within the ServiceNow ecosystem.
  • Build and maintain senior relationships across relevant ServiceNow sales, public sector, partner, and regional leadership organizations.
  • Develop a deliberate strategy for increasing ServiceNow awareness of PTG's capabilities and creating stronger co-sell and partner-led opportunities.
  • Position PTG as a partner ServiceNow leaders and sellers trust and actively want to bring into customer opportunities.
  • Ensure PTG is taking full advantage of applicable ServiceNow partner programs, competencies, designations, enablement opportunities, and market investments.
  • Represent PTG credibly with ServiceNow executives, customers, partners, and other industry stakeholders.
  • Maintain a strong understanding of changes within ServiceNow's market strategy, product direction, partner ecosystem, and competitive environment and translate those changes into action for PTG.

Practice Leadership & Operating Model

  • Serve as the senior leader across the ServiceNow practice, aligning Sales, Solution Consulting, and Operations & Delivery around common priorities and outcomes.
  • Establish clear roles, decision rights, accountability, and operating expectations across the practice.
  • Provide decisive leadership and experienced guidance when teams need direction, particularly in complex pursuits, customer situations, investment decisions, and cross-functional issues.
  • Create repeatable operating models for how the practice approaches sales pursuits, proposals, customer engagement, new offerings, strategic initiatives, and internal decision-making.
  • Ensure the practice remains focused on agreed priorities rather than pursuing disconnected initiatives that do not support the broader strategy.
  • Build an organizational structure that evolves appropriately as the business grows rather than adding layers ahead of demonstrated need.
  • Develop leaders and team members while creating clear expectations for performance and accountability.

Sales, Solution Consulting & Delivery Alignment

  • Lead the Account Executive, Solution Consulting, and Operations & Delivery leadership functions as an integrated practice.
  • Preserve and strengthen collaboration between Sales and Solution Consulting while establishing clear accountability for each function.
  • Ensure Delivery is engaged appropriately throughout the sales lifecycle so commitments are feasible, appropriately scoped, and aligned with execution capabilities.
  • Partner closely with the Director of Operations & Delivery on capacity, capability, delivery risk, customer health, and execution readiness.
  • Own final practice-level business decisions while ensuring material delivery risks and feasibility concerns are surfaced, understood, and appropriately addressed.
  • Ensure commercial decisions consider scope, delivery requirements, staffing, margin, customer outcomes, and long-term account value—not simply revenue.
  • Intervene when cross-functional issues require senior leadership, clear direction, or accountability.

Leadership & Decision Authority

The Vice President is expected to operate with significant autonomy and make day-to-day strategic, commercial, organizational, and operational decisions for the ServiceNow practice.


The role will partner with the COO / Executive Sponsor on significant matters including major changes to practice strategy, material investments outside established budgets, significant organizational expansion, executive-level hiring or termination decisions, acquisitions, and other decisions with broader PTG implications.


As the leader establishes a strong understanding of PTG's business, culture, customers, and financial model, the expectation is increased autonomy—not continued executive dependence for routine practice decisions.


Required Experience

  • Significant leadership experience within the ServiceNow ecosystem, with a strong understanding of how ServiceNow's sales, partner, and services ecosystem operates.
  • Demonstrated experience helping build, lead, or scale a ServiceNow consulting and professional services business.
  • Proven experience leading sales teams and developing high-performing commercial organizations.
  • Strong understanding of consulting and professional services economics, including pricing, margin, utilization implications, staffing considerations, and deal structure.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing growth strategies rather than solely carrying an individual sales quota.
  • Proven ability to lead complex enterprise pursuits and provide experienced guidance on deal strategy and commercial models.
  • Established relationships and credibility within the ServiceNow ecosystem, with evidence of successfully converting ecosystem relationships into business opportunity and strategic alignment.
  • Experience selling consulting and technology services to public sector customers or significant experience supporting organizations focused on public sector markets.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams that include Sales, Solution Consulting, and Delivery.
  • Experience making organizational, investment, and go-to-market decisions in a growing business environment.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience scaling a ServiceNow consulting/services practice through a comparable stage of growth.
  • Experience working for a ServiceNow implementation partner, consulting organization, or within ServiceNow in a role with significant partner/services exposure.
  • Experience developing managed services or other recurring services offerings.
  • Experience building repeatable or packaged ServiceNow offerings.
  • Experience with ServiceNow subscription/resale models.
  • Experience working with public sector procurement vehicles and complex government buying processes.

Leadership Profile

We are looking for a leader who:

  • Is decisive and comfortable making informed decisions with incomplete information.
  • Has the confidence and experience to provide clear direction rather than escalating routine decisions upward.
  • Can challenge Sales, Delivery, executives, and customers constructively when necessary.
  • Is commercially minded without sacrificing delivery quality or customer outcomes.
  • Thinks strategically but remains close enough to the business to understand what is actually happening.
  • Brings structure and discipline without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.
  • Communicates clearly, directly, and consistently.
  • Coaches people to make better decisions rather than becoming the permanent decision-maker for every issue.
  • Is comfortable operating in a candid, collaborative, fast-moving environment where healthy debate is expected.
  • Knows when to move quickly, when to gather additional information, and when an opportunity does not align with the practice's strategy.
  • Builds organizations intentionally as growth requires rather than assuming headcount is the answer to every problem.

What This Role Is Not

This is not an individual Account Executive role with an executive title.

It is not a role focused solely on carrying a personal quota, maintaining a book of business, or personally managing every customer opportunity.

It is also not a purely strategic position removed from day-to-day execution.

jobs.excerpt: About MegaportWe’re not your typical tech company – and we don’t want to be.
jobs.description:
About Megaport

We’re not your typical tech company – and we don’t want to be. Megaport is the global leader in Network as a Service (NaaS), and has transformed the way businesses connect to the cloud, data centers, and each other. We’re publicly listed on the Australian Stock Exchange and partnered with the biggest names in tech like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Oracle, IBM, and more. Headquartered in Brisbane with a crew of over 600 people spread across Asia-Pacific, Europe, and the Americas, our employees enjoy an environment that is collaborative, supportive, and (actually) fun.

Our Team Culture

We’re a team of problem solvers, pixel pushers, code slingers, and cloud fanatics. Culture is more than a poster on the wall here – collaboration beats hierarchy, curiosity fuels our growth, and everyone’s voice matters. We take our work seriously, but not ourselves. We work across time zones to execute on our global vision, trust each other to get things done, and never compromise our values for commercial gain. Most importantly, we place our customers at the center of everything we do.
We’re committed to increasing representation in the tech industry and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. Don’t meet every requirement? That’s okay. If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role

You’ve got a few years of building backend services under your belt, and you’re ready to own real features on systems that customers depend on every day.

We’re looking for a mid-level Backend Engineer to join our Engineering team and help us ship high-quality software, faster. Reporting to the Engineering Manager, you’ll work on the core systems behind the Megaport platform — the APIs and services that turn a click in the Portal into provisioned connectivity between data centers on opposite sides of the world.

Our main codebase is a mixture of Java and Kotlin using the Spring Boot framework, and we are migrating fully to Kotlin over time. You don’t need Kotlin on day one, but you’ll be writing it before long.

You'll work alongside a skilled, driven team, and have genuine room to shape how we solve problems. Our backend engineers also run a dedicated mentoring program, so you'll have someone in your corner as you grow.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Design, build and ship backend services and APIs, from an ambiguous problem through to tested, maintainable code in production.
  • Work in a modern JVM stack including Java, Kotlin, Spring Boot, Postgres, RabbitMQ and Redis, and help shape how we use it.
  • Ship to a Kubernetes and AWS platform where GitHub Actions handle the heavy lifting, so you spend your time on the product rather than on infrastructure.
  • Turn business requirements into technical solutions, and speak up when a requirement doesn't quite add up. We'd rather you asked why before how.
  • Collaborate with engineers, product, and stakeholders across the business to build systems that stay reliable, secure and fast as we grow.
  • Write JUnit and Kotest tests that let us ship with confidence, and take part in code review as both author and reviewer.
  • Help improve our architecture, patterns and processes, and keep our technical debt in check to ensure the codebase remains flexible and well-maintained.

What We Are Looking For

    We care as much about how you think and work as what you already know. The technical bar matters, but so does curiosity, clear communication, and the drive to own your work.

    You'll thrive here if you:

  • Have a few years building backend services in Java or Kotlin.
  • Are comfortable working with Spring, and have a sense of what it's doing for you.
  • Know your way around relational databases and can model data with an eye on how it'll be queried.
  • Communicate clearly — you can explain a technical trade-off to an engineer and to a non-engineer, and you listen as well as you talk.
  • Like solving problems, and can think critically about them. You dig into the why, weigh options, and aren't satisfied with "it works" when it could be right.
  • Take ownership — you're keen to pick up a problem, run with it, and see it through.

    • Nice to have (or happy to help you learn):

  • Kotlin, or an appetite for picking it up.
  • Experience with Go or Terraform. We maintain our own Terraform Provider, and we’re upskilling the team to build on it.
  • Experience with ORMs like Hibernate, and a sense of when not to reach for one.
  • Knowledge of the major cloud providers’ products or APIs. We integrate directly with AWS, Azure and GCP to provision customer connectivity.
  • An interest in networking — IP routing, MPLS, or just how the internet actually fits together.

What We Offer

  • Flexible working environment — Brisbane-based with one or two days a week in the office, or fully remote anywhere in Australia with good overlap with east-coast hours
  • Generous leave plans — including parental leave, birthday leave, and a purchased annual leave program
  • Health and wellness support — through a wellness allowance and employee wellbeing initiatives
  • Comprehensive learning support — generous study and training allowance plus paid study leave
  • Creative, modern workspaces — designed to inspire when you're not working remotely, plus access to coworking spaces via our global WeWork membership if you work remotely, but like to get out of the house sometimes
  • Motivated, inclusive team — work alongside industry experts and fresh talent
  • Recognition programs — celebrate achievements with our Legend and Kudos awards
If you have any questions, please reach out to Megaport's Talent Acquisition Team at
NOTE: All Megaport business correspondence is conducted via our business email accounts (@megaport.com). If you have any concerns, please reach out to Megaport's careers team directly and we will verify the legitimacy of any communication. Megaport will not ask you to create an account via Microsoft teams, and does not associate with any email accounts under "@megaportau.com".
All applications will be treated in confidence.
Please see Part 2 of our Privacy Policy to see what information Megaport collects from job applicants, why, and how we store and use it. Note that you’re entitled to know what personal data of yours Megaport holds, to request updates, rectification, and in some circumstances restriction or deletion thereof if you object (you being entitled to withdraw your consent to our holding your information at any time). Please see Part 5 of our Privacy Policy for more details on this and how to contact Megaport's data protection officer if you have any further privacy-related questions. Candidates who meet the selection criteria will be invited to attend an interview. Strictly no Recruitment Agencies.

What Do We Do?

Triple Whale is the AI operating system built for modern commmerce. We help you see what's actually working in your business, what's not, and what to do next. Then we take action for you — pausing the underperforming ad, generating the next batch of creative, flagging the inventory risk before it hurts your bottom line.

We pull every signal in your business into one place, and put it on the most trusted measurement foundation in the industry. And on top of that, we give you the only AI harness in commerce — Moby — letting you tap any LLM you want, grounded in the full context of your business. Moby doesn't just surface insights, it executes decisions for you, with automations that make the rest of your stack smarter.

The result: more than 65,000 brands like Kitsch, OUAI, and True Classic turn mountains of complex data into actions that actually grow profit, at a speed and scale that is not humanly possible.

Why Triple Whale Needs You

This is not a passive relationship management role. It's a hands-on, technically demanding position where you'll be the first person a brand trusts with their data stack — and the last thing standing between them and churn.

As a CSM on the Growth team, you'll guide a high-volume book of eCommerce brands through the full onboarding lifecycle — owning every technical configuration, every kickoff call, and every moment where the platform either clicks or doesn't. Once a brand is live, you stay in their corner as a scaled, data-driven consultant across a shared inbox, live chat, and office hours model.

The people who thrive here move fast, think in systems, love solving technical puzzles for non-technical users, and genuinely care about whether a brand succeeds.

What You'll Do

  • Own an active book of onboardings end-to-end — from kickoff call through nurture — operating with speed, ownership, and clear communication at every step.
  • Run structured kickoff calls that map each customer's tech stack, stakeholders, and goals before diving into configuration.
  • Guide customers through Triple Pixel installation: enabling Theme App Embed and Checkout Web Pixel in Shopify, validating with live URL tests, and advising on third-party/landing page installs via GTM.
  • Configure and validate UTM and tracking parameters (tw_source, tw_campaign, tw_ad_id) with platform-specific dynamic tokens, ensuring Triple Whale attribution is capturing data accurately across all paid channels.
  • Connect and troubleshoot coreintegrations — Meta, Google Ads, TikTok, Klaviyo, Google Sheets, Slack — preventing feature-blockers before they happen.
  • Walk customers through the Summary and Attribution dashboards — validating clean data, configuring Custom Metrics (CM1/CM2, blended ROAS), and explaining attribution model selection (Triple Attribution, Last Click, First Click, Linear) based on their business use case.
  • Manage your onboarding and success pipelines in HubSpot, tracking health and milestone progress from kickoff through renewal.
  • Collaborate with Sales on unresponsive customers and with Support on technical escalations, keeping onboarding velocity high across your entire book.
  • Manage a high-volume, scaled customer portfolio through shared inbox, live chat, and office hours — driving retention and satisfaction in a fast-paced, largely automated environment.
  • Proactively identify churn risk early: monitor usage patterns, flag cost-based objections, and develop resolution strategies before the renewal conversation.
  • Drive expansion by identifying upsell opportunities within the Growth segment and collaborating cross-functionally to move them forward.
  • Contribute to the continued development of the Triple Whale customer experience — improving playbooks, surfacing common friction points, and helping the team get better every quarter.

What You'll Bring

  • Experience supporting customers in the eCommerce or marketing technology space — ideally within a SaaS environment.
  • Demonstrated comfort with technical setup and configuration: you don't need to be an engineer, but you need to be the kind of person who learns a new platform thoroughly and can confidently walk someone else through it.
  • Familiarity with the eCommerce marketing stack — Meta Ads, Google Ads, TikTok, Klaviyo, Shopify, UTM tracking — is a strong advantage.
  • Prior high-volume customer success, customer support, or SDR experience; you know how to manage a large book of accounts without letting things fall through the cracks.
  • Superb written and verbal communication skills — you can translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable guidance for operators who are experts in their business, not in analytics.
  • Strong organizational skills and comfort managing multiple onboardings simultaneously in a fast-moving, process-driven environment.
  • A natural sense of ownership: you're the kind of person who tracks things down, follows up proactively, and doesn't wait to be asked.
  • Positive, high-energy, service-oriented mindset — customers feel your investment in their success.
  • Comfort driving negotiation and renewal conversations to positive outcomes.
  • Thrives in collaborative team environments and embraces change as the product and processes continue to evolve.

Join Us in Making Waves

If you’re looking for more than just a job and want to be part of a movement reshaping the future of Ecommerce, Triple Whale is the place for you. We’re on the lookout for driven, curious, and creative individuals ready to thrive in a fast-paced environment.

The Constellation Kidney Group (CKG), part of the Miram Solutions Portfolio of the Perseus Group within Constellation Software Inc. Group of companies, is a global leader in dialysis technology serving kidney care providers across seven countries. CKG’s integrated KidneyOne platform brings together modern EHR, analytics, and interoperability capabilities built on over 50 years of innovation, helping providers optimize care, operations, and compliance.

CKG’s US solution portfolio spans Clinical Vision (CV), FOCUS Billing, CKG Intelligence, Renal AI, DrFirst/e-Prescribe, and related platform services supporting dialysis providers across clinical documentation, billing, analytics, and regulatory compliance.

Role Summary

The Head, Client Training & Adoption is accountable for the end-to-end design, delivery, and continuous improvement of client-facing training programs and revenue cycle management (RCM) education across CKG’s US operations. Reporting to the Director of Professional Services, this role serves as the single point of expertise bridging product training, clinical workflow enablement, and medical billing knowledge ensuring clients achieve measurable adoption, operational proficiency, and financial performance outcomes across the KidneyOne platform.

Day to day, the Head, Client Training & Adoption designs scalable curricula spanning clinical and billing workflows, leads training engagements tied to implementation milestones and go-live readiness, and acts as the primary RCM subject-matter expert for client-facing billing questions, denial resolution guidance, and revenue cycle optimization. This role partners closely with implementation project teams, the Engagement organization (Clinical & Billing Services), and the RCM team to drive feature adoption, support retention and expansion, and translate complex payer and regulatory requirements into actionable education for both clients and internal teams.

In this role, ‘clients’ encompasses both external customers dialysis providers using the KidneyOne platform and internal teams who rely on product and billing proficiency to serve those customers effectively. External-facing work centers on client training and adoption; internal-facing work centers on product enablement, ensuring every team that touches the client experience has the knowledge and confidence to deliver.

Key Responsibilities

1. Training Strategy & Program Ownership

  • Own the overall client and internal product training strategy and annual roadmap across client-facing and internal education, aligning training priorities to CKG’s business objectives, product roadmap, and client success goals.
  • Help set the standard for how product / client training is designed, delivered, and measured across CKG establishing consistent quality, methodology, and governance for all education programs.
  • Define product / client training program priorities in partnership with Professional Services, Engagement, and Product Management leadership, ensuring resources are allocated to highest-impact initiatives.
  • Maintain a rolling training roadmap that accounts for product releases, implementation schedules, client adoption goals, and internal enablement needs.

2. Client Training Program Design & Delivery

The work lives at the boundary of applied research and production engineering!

What you will be doing:

  • Architecting and implementing high-performance communication and memory management libraries for distributed AI

  • Driving hardware-software co-optimization with GPU, DPU, NIC, and switch teams through GPUDirect RDMA, NVLink, and next-generation interconnects

  • Profiling and optimizing data movement across GPU memory, system DRAM, NVMe, and network fabrics

  • Integrating networking capabilities into AI serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM

  • Contributing to and maintaining open-source projects, mentoring engineers, conducting design reviews, and prototyping experimental technologies to evaluate their viability

What we need to see:

  • 12+ years in systems software and/or networking with demonstrated ownership of complex projects.

  • MS, PhD or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

  • Solid understanding of high-performance networking: InfiniBand, RoCE, RDMA, NVLink, GPUDirect.

  • Strong C/C++/Rust systems programming with comfort in performance profiling and low-level debugging.

  • Understanding of ML systems concepts—transformer architectures, KV cache mechanics, model parallelism, or distributed training and inference patterns.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Knowledge of ML inference frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) and their communication requirements.

  • Knowledge of storage networking (NVMe-oF, GPUDirect Storage, S3).
