jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Applied AI
jobs.excerpt: About Snowplow Snowplow is the real-time customer context layer that collects, validates, enriches, and delivers behavioral data for advanced analytics, ML, and AI agent decisioning.
jobs.description:
About Snowplow

Snowplow is the real-time customer context layer that collects, validates, enriches, and delivers behavioral data for advanced analytics, ML, and AI agent decisioning. Snowplow's event tracking is leveraged across 2M+ websites and applications globally, processing over one trillion events per month.

More than 250 companies, including Experian, AutoTrader, Strava, Condé Nast, and HelloFresh, rely on Snowplow to build a well-governed, first-party data foundation that powers their customer-facing AI agents, in-session personalization and recommendations, and real-time analytics.

This Opportunity

Snowplow is rebuilding how the company runs its own work. AI-native transformation is the operating priority for the business, and the Applied AI team owns it: the platform every team's AI work runs on, the pattern for how a function's critical workflows move onto agents, and the measurement of whether it worked. Individual AI adoption is already high across the company. The next stage is redesigning functions so that agents run the recurring work and people set the goals and judge the output.

You are the first Forward Deployed Engineer on the team, reporting to the Senior Director of Applied AI. The team is also hiring a principal engineer to own the platform and an Applied AI engineer to embed with our Growth team. The Senior Director you report to still ships code. You are the one who moves between functions. You embed with one function at a time alongside its leader and the people who do the work by hand today, map how the work actually runs, build the agentic workflow that takes it on, tune it with the experts until they trust it, and hand it back to the function to own. Then you move to the next one.

You sit with our major business functions, one at a time. The Senior Director of Applied AI and the function's leader choose each engagement, and your workflow maps are the evidence they choose from. Priorities will shift as the transformation moves, and the role is designed for that.

This is the forward deployed model applied inside our own company. You write the code, and you also do the discovery a consultant would. The function's leader owns the decision to change how their team works. You own the engineering and the pattern. You'll spend as much time listening to someone walk through a task they do by hand every week as you will writing the agents that run it, and the deliverable is a function that works differently, understands why, and can run what you built.

What you will own

  • The workflow map. You sit with the people who do the work and leave with how it actually runs today: where work enters, what moves between steps, who says yes, and what "good" means. It is the first thing you do in every engagement.
  • The case for whether to build. Before anything gets built, you bring the evidence from the map and make the case for whether the workflow is worth moving onto agents, including when the answer is that it does not need AI. The decision sits with the function's leader and the Senior Director; the evidence is yours.
  • The build. You design and build agentic workflows on Snowplow's shared factory framework, which Applied AI runs: declared queues and gates, focused agents, and a central ledger that records every agent run. Every factory you build is compatible with every other one, in any function.
  • Approval gates. You decide where the agent acts on its own, where it proposes and a person approves, and what gets recorded so anyone can see what the agent did and why. The people in the function keep the judgment. The agents take the rest.
  • Agent readiness. You make the function's knowledge, systems of record, and quality bar explicit enough for agents to work from. Often this is the real work, and the agents are the easy part.
  • The last twenty percent. Most of the work comes after the prototype: reliability, edge cases, evaluation, and a team choosing it over the way they worked before. You tune the output alongside the domain experts and encode their judgment into checks that hold after they step back.
  • The handoff. You train the function to run and evolve what you built, then leave. Where an Applied AI engineer is embedded in the function, you hand it to them. Success is a workflow still running months after you have moved on, owned by people who are not you. After the handoff you stay available: when the function sees a problem or a way to improve the workflow, you coordinate it with the embedded and platform engineers rather than taking it back, and you help build the platform those workflows run on.
  • The pattern itself. You own how a workflow moves from map to agents to handoff, written down so the next engagement starts from it. What you build also goes back into the shared framework as reference implementations. The second factory in any function should be cheaper than the first.

We would love to hear from you if you have

  • Shipped real software in someone else's stack. You are comfortable being dropped into an unfamiliar codebase, dataset, or business system and productive in it fast. You are fluent in at least one of Python, TypeScript, or Go, and you pick up the others as the work needs them.
  • Built with LLMs in production. You have designed agents or agentic workflows that run real work, with prompts, tools, evaluation, and the failure modes that come with them. You know the difference between a demo and something a team relies on every day, and you have done the unglamorous work of closing that gap.
  • An AI-native way of working you can show us. A workflow, automation, or agent you built and still use. Expect to demonstrate it during the interview process.
  • Sat with non-engineers and understood their work. You can spend a day with a sales, marketing, or customer team and come back with the actual process, including the parts nobody wrote down. Active listening matters here as much as the stack.
  • Self-direction and comfort with ambiguity. Engagements are time-boxed, functions differ, and the next one is decided by the business. You plan your own work inside an engagement and stay steady when the business changes what comes next.
  • The instinct to hand off. You would rather install a capability that keeps producing without you than become the person a team depends on.
  • Low ego. You retire your own work when a better approach shows up, including one a teammate built. Models and tools change fast, and last quarter's build may need replacing.
  • Clear communication with senior stakeholders. You can explain to a function leader what changes for their team, in their language, and hold your ground on the pattern when it matters.
  • A track record you can talk through. You have worked in a forward deployed, solutions engineering, internal tools, or consulting engineering role, or you have transformed a process end to end inside a company you worked for.

How we hire for this role

The interview process includes a working session where you walk us through how you work with AI on a real task, using your own setup. We work this way ourselves, and you are welcome to use AI when applying.

What you get in return for being awesome

  • Meaningful equity stake
  • Competitive Base Salary
  • Flexible working
  • Generous PTO
  • Private Medical Insurance
  • Company Pension
  • MacBook and home office equipment allowance
  • Enhanced Family leave

jobs.excerpt: Position:SALESFORCE ARCHITECTLocation:ELIZABETHTOWN, KY or REMOTE (US ONLY)Salary:$130-150k We are hiring a Salesforce Architect to lead the technical design of the Salesforce solutions we deliver to Department of Defense (DoD) customers.
jobs.description:
Position:SALESFORCE ARCHITECTLocation:ELIZABETHTOWN, KY or REMOTE (US ONLY)Salary:$130-150k
We are hiring a Salesforce Architect to lead the technical design of the Salesforce solutions we deliver to Department of Defense (DoD) customers. You will own the overall architecture, which covers the data model, security model, automation, and integrations, in a secure DoD cloud environment. You will guide the development team and advise government stakeholders on technical trade-offs.

Candidates must be a US Citizen to meet contractual and job requirements.

This role is 100% remote.

DUTIES AND RESONSIBILITIES

  • Own the end-to-end solution architecture for the program's Salesforce environment
  • Translate mission and business requirements into scalable designs for the data model, security model, automation, and user experience
  • Design the security and sharing model to protect Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) using profiles, permission sets, sharing rules, Shield Platform Encryption, and Event Monitoring
  • Define the integration strategy with the MuleSoft Integration Architect, including APIs, events, and data synchronization
  • Set development standards, the sandbox and environment strategy, and the release management and CI/CD process
  • Lead design reviews and code reviews, and mentor senior and junior developers
  • Produce architecture documentation, including system diagrams and data flows, to support Authority to Operate (ATO) and Risk Management Framework (RMF) packages
  • Assess each Salesforce release for impact, risk, and new capabilities
  • Advise program leadership and government stakeholders on platform limits, licensing, and technical options

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Infrastructure & Release
jobs.excerpt: About Feanix BioFeanix is rebuilding animal breeding from the genome up.
jobs.description:
About Feanix Bio

Feanix is rebuilding animal breeding from the genome up.

We’re a YC-backed startup using whole-genome sequencing and custom ML models to help dairy farmers make better breeding and herd management decisions. Our technology is genuinely novel: we can sequence a full genome from a single hair at a fraction of traditional industry costs, our models achieve ~90% prediction accuracy on traits where existing approaches sit closer to ~30%, and we’re pioneering farm-specific genomic predictions that turn genetics into practical, actionable decisions.

That technology is translating into real adoption. In a short time, we’ve grown to serve roughly 1% of the U.S. dairy industry, with many customers in the pipeline. We started with dairy because our founders grew up on dairy farms and understand firsthand the problems we’re solving. But genetics is foundational to every agricultural industry, and dairy is only the beginning.

We’re building Feanix with a small, high-caliber team where people have meaningful ownership and work end to end. There are no unnecessary layers and very little room for busywork — just difficult problems at the intersection of biology, data, and software that haven’t been solved before.

If you’re exceptional at what you do and want your work to have a measurable impact on an entire industry, we’d love to build it with you.

About The Role

Feanix’s main product Autopilot is a farm decision system. We ingest farm data, configure our models around each operation's economics and goals, and generate farm-specific decisions for every animal in the herd — which to breed, which to cull, which to sell. Autopilot produces those decisions overnight and delivers them into the herd-management software the farm already runs.

Today we work with 30 of the roughly 150 largest dairies in the country, ~250,000+ cows. Over the next 5 months we need to grow to 50 farms, and within 12 months to half of that market, while launching new offerings beyond what we ship today.Most of the software behind that system currently is supported by a small team of engineers. This role exists to increase the stability, efficiency and speed of that team and system.

You would lead infrastructure at Feanix — you'd own the foundation the other engineers build on and your success would be measured in their throughput: how fast they learn whether a change is safe, and how fast they find out something didn't run. We've added the basics — observability, testing and release tooling as we've grown. What's missing is someone owning it end to end.

The job is the whole delivery ecosystem — everything between an engineer's commit and decisions landing on a farm: the environments a change is proven in, the gates it passes, how it rolls out, and how we know it arrived. Today a change can't be exercised end to end against realistic farm data before it reaches production, which shapes how cautiously (or indeed how riskily) everyone works. The reliability half isn't the usual one, we don't run a low-latency service, we run pipelines overnight, so what matters is whether a run started, finished, finished in time, and landed on the farm.

What You'll Own

Roughly half this role is CI, test and release engineering; a quarter is observability; a quarter is access control, cost, and consolidating our infrastructure as code. Work on a Windows fleet is a small slice.

  • Alerting and service-level objectives for the farm pipeline. What “decisions on the farm by time T” means per herd, instrumented and alerted. A run that never started, never finished, or finished late should reach a person before anyone on the farm notices.
  • The release path. Building out a path where staging runs on every commit and software engineers get quick feedback if the change was right.
  • Infrastructure as code, end to end. Agentic coding has not eliminated infrastructure as code, it has enhanced the speed it can be developed and changed.
  • Cost. There's a rough baseline today. You'd turn it into a real one, own the cost curve per herd, act on obvious waste, and help engineers estimate what something will cost before it ships rather than after.
  • Test infrastructure other engineers depend on, including for the third-party herd software and the machines that move files to and from farms. You'd make that boundary testable. You wouldn't own the automation itself.

How We Work

Python end to end, on AWS. A FastAPI service and Celery workers on ECS Fargate, PostgreSQL and S3 behind them, OpenTofu and GitHub Actions for everything that provisions and ships it. Bursty and GPU work runs on managed compute rather than a cluster we operate — the split is chosen per workload and it's deliberate.

Like everyone else, we're working out how humans and agents build software together. Our engineers direct agents against real work and build the harnesses that check that work. About half our recent commits are co-authored with agents. Quality comes from what happens around the code: specs, tests, verification. Nobody has this fully figured out, and that includes us.

Infrastructure as code is still the rule: changes are reviewed, versioned, and applied through CI, not typed into a console. So the question isn't whether agents write infrastructure, it's how agent-written infrastructure clears that bar. What does review mean when the author produced three hundred lines in a minute? Which checks have to be machine-enforced because a human reading a plan will miss the one line that matters? We care more that you verify agent output than that you use it. Bring yours and argue them out with us.

What You Bring

  • Strong OpenTofu or Terraform, and real AWS depth — ECS/Fargate, IAM, S3, networking
  • Test and release engineering: CI design, test environments with real databases, staged rollouts, and regression testing of pipeline outputs, not only unit tests
  • Operational judgment — alerting that pages on the right thing, service objectives that reflect what a customer actually experiences
  • Comfort with heterogeneous compute, without needing to unify it
  • Strong Python; GitHub Actions and OIDC
  • Security fundamentals and the judgment to apply them proportionately at this stage
  • Daily, load-bearing use of coding agents, and a real position on where they break down

You might be a fit if you've built the release path for a team that was shipping without one, and you measure yourself by whether other engineers got faster. If overnight pipelines with hard delivery windows interest you more than another request-latency problem. If you have opinions about how agent-written infrastructure should be reviewed — and you've changed your mind about some of them.

You might not be if your first quarter would involve introducing Kubernetes or a new orchestration platform, or if the part of the estate that reaches machines on farms reads as beneath the role rather than as the interesting constraint.

Preferred Qualifications

You've likely held a title like infrastructure engineer, release engineer, SRE, or ops. That title matters less to us than two other things: that you think creatively about how agents are changing this job, and that you're motivated by supporting other people through your own technical work.

  • Having supported a small team through a period of rapid growth
  • Fleet management for software running on machines you don't control
  • Compliance readiness (SOC 2 or similar) — useful, not expected
  • Agriculture or biology experience isn't required, but an interest doesn't hurt

Ultimately, we care far more about demonstrated ability, curiosity, and problem-solving than pedigree or conventional career paths.

Logistics

  • Remote, with 10am–2pm Pacific core hours regardless of where you're based
  • West-coast based candidates preferred!
  • Travel 15–20%, including visits to commercial dairies and time with the team at our headquarters in Scotts Valley, CA
  • Engineers share an on-call and triage rotation — weekly, with a written handbook, and weekend work requires explicit sign-off rather than being assumed. Building the alerting that makes on-call survivable is part of this job.

Why You'll Enjoy Working With Us

  • The People — we have an amazing group of talented, smart and fun people on our team!
  • The Company — we are building something novel that has not been done before which is making a huge impact on the dairy industry!
  • The Experience — you get to come in and be a part of ground breaking work that will have a huge impact on generations to come!

Compensation and Benefits

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship or transfers at this time.

Actual starting pay for this role is determined by a variety of factors including but not limited to qualifications, experience, relevant skills, education, and geographic location. Employees are offered a variety of benefits to empower them with the resources and flexibility they need to enjoy success on the job and to live a healthy life.

We offer a flexible, remote-friendly work environment for most roles, along with a growing benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; 401k, pet insurance, flexible paid time off; and paid parental leave, including up to twelve weeks of paid leave and/or supplemental pay coordination with applicable state benefits.

We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

  • 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

  • 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.

About Lantern

Lantern is the specialty care platform connecting people with the best care when they need it most. By curating a Network of Excellence comprised of the nation's top specialists for surgery, cancer care, infusions and more, Lantern delivers excellent care with significant cost savings to employers and their workforces. With convenient access to specialists nationwide, Lantern means quality care is within driving distance for most. Lantern is trusted by the nation's largest employers to deliver care to more than 6 million members across the country. Learn more about us at lanterncare.com.

Lantern is the specialty care platform, connecting people with high-quality, affordable specialty care close to home. We operate in a regulated healthcare environment (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2), we handle protected health information at scale, and we are becoming an AI healthcare company, with AI adoption a top company priority.

This Principal IAM Engineer is a senior level, individual-contributor role and the technical authority for identity at Lantern. In an organization where the security perimeter is effectively identity, you will own the identity control plane end to end, and you will determine who can reach PHI and under what conditions. You will set the identity standard, build the automation behind it, and hold the verification bar that other teams operate against.

You will report to the CISO and partner closely with our IAM engineer and with the platform, cloud, and service delivery teams that execute alongside you. This is a hands-on principal seat, not a people-management role today, with a clear path to expand into a leadership role as the identity function grows.

Our security philosophy is open by default, secure by design. Security exists to help the business move fast, safely, and the default answer is “yes, safely,” because guardrails are built into the platform, pipelines, and tooling rather than enforced by someone saying no. Gates exist only where risk genuinely warrants them, and even then they are automated, fast, and transparent.

Location: Remote

Responsibilities:

  • Own the identity lifecycle: joiner, mover, and leaver provisioning and deprovisioning, automated from role- and attribute-based models (RBAC/ABAC), with deprovisioning verified against an entitlement inventory rather than assumed.
  • Own access management, including Conditional Access, phishing-resistant MFA, and privileged access on a Zero Trust model, with least-privilege by default, just-in-time (JIT) elevation, and enforcement confirmed on every access path rather than only saved.
  • Own directory and federation across Entra ID, single sign-on, SAML, OIDC, and OAuth2.
  • Own secrets and non-human identity, including API keys, service accounts, and workload identity, and maintain an owner registry for them.
  • Own key access governance and separation of duties in a model where another team operates the key management system.
  • Own identity automation and identity-as-code, building lifecycle and access controls as reviewable, version-controlled infrastructure (Terraform and policy-as-code) rather than manual configuration.
  • Own the identity-verification standard the service desk follows for password resets, MFA resets, and device enrollment. This is a hands-on control point, because helpdesk-initiated resets are a leading account-takeover vector.

Key Deliverables in Your First Year:

  • Conditional Access enforced by default on PHI-facing applications, with enforcement verified.
  • Automated joiner, mover, and leaver provisioning and deprovisioning that meets its SLA every time.
  • A secrets golden path, with vaulted secrets, none in code, and a populated key-to-owner registry.
  • Strong, phishing-resistant MFA coverage on privileged accounts.
  • Documented runbooks and depth across the control plane, so no critical control depends on a single person.

How You Will Work:You will set standards that partner teams execute. Service Delivery performs provisioning tasks and resets against the verification bar you own. Cloud Engineering carries cloud access, workload identity, and key-management operations, with key access governed by you. HR events are the sole trigger for lifecycle changes. The Governance, Risk & Compliance team independently attests to the entitlements you produce, and access certification deliberately sits outside this role so that the team reviewing access is not the team granting it. Holding those boundaries cleanly is central to the job.

Requirements:

  • Eight or more years in identity and access management, including principal- or staff-level ownership of an identity control plane.
  • Deep Microsoft Entra ID engineering, including Conditional Access policy design, phishing-resistant MFA, single sign-on, and federation across SAML, OIDC, and OAuth2, and verifying that enforcement takes effect across every access path, not only the expected one.
  • Identity lifecycle automation across cloud, SaaS, and privileged systems, with role- and attribute-based provisioning (RBAC/ABAC) and deprovisioning verified against an entitlement inventory.
  • Zero Trust identity design, including least-privilege, just-in-time (JIT) access, and risk-based or adaptive access controls.
  • Identity governance and administration (IGA) platform engineering, including privileged access management.
  • Automation and scripting (PowerShell, Python, or similar) to build lifecycle workflows and custom connectors.
  • Identity-as-code and policy-as-code practice, using Terraform with source-controlled change management (for example, GitHub).
  • Secrets and non-human identity (API keys, service accounts, workload identity), and maintaining an owner registry for them.
  • Key access governance and separation of duties in a model where another team operates the key management system.
  • The ability to act as the technical authority for a function without formal people-management authority, working directly to a CISO.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, or equivalent professional experience.

Strong Candidates Will:

  • Healthcare or another regulated environment where identity controls gate access to PHI.
  • Hands-on Saviynt with PAM, Azure PIM, and Keeper, or transferable depth in comparable platforms.
  • Experience remediating a Conditional Access enforcement gap or a deprovisioning failure, and making the structural change that prevented recurrence.
  • Passkeys and FIDO2, or phishing-resistant authenticator experience, aligned with NIST SP 800-63 Rev. 4.
  • Experience growing a technical scope into a broader leadership remit.
  • Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator certification, CIMP, or equivalent.

Who Thrives in This Role:

  • Verified enforcement. You do not consider a control done until you have seen it working on every path.
  • Automation bias. You remove the manual step rather than documenting it more carefully.
  • Structural fixes. You solve the class of failure, not the instance.
  • Boundary clarity. You hold the standard with partner teams without taking over their execution.
  • Governance respect. You keep access certification independent rather than absorbing it.

Benefits

  • Medical Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Short & Long Term Disability
  • Life Insurance
  • 401k with company match
  • Flexible Time Off
  • Paid Parental Leave

About You:

  • You use LOGIC in your decision making and understand that progress is critical to making change. You focus on the execution of your content while balancing a fast-paced environment and you take the time to celebrate both the small & big wins.
  • INCLUSION is a core tenant of your personal beliefs. A diverse and inclusive environment is incredibly important to you. You understand and desire to be a part of a diverse team with different experiences and perspectives & you cherish the differences in each individual that you interact with.
  • You have the GRIT, drive and ambition to tackle big problems. Big problems require big ideas and a team that supports new ideas.
  • You care deeply for your customers are driven to keep HUMANITY in all decisions. Your customers aren’t just the individuals using your product. They are the driving factor in your motivation to make a change.
  • Integrity guides you in life. Focusing on the TRUTH vs. giving people the answers they want to hear.
  • You thrive in a Team Environment. Collaboration is key in innovation and creating change.

These pillars of LIGHT are a reminder to our team that we are making a difference by providing guidance and support in navigating the often complex and confusing landscape of healthcare. We hope that through this LIGHT, individuals can find their way to the best care, resources, and support they need to get back to life.

The Design Enablement Engineer develops and deploys critical PDK components that accurately represent semiconductor manufacturing processes within customer design and verification environments. The engineer will work at the intersection of process technology, design rules, device modeling, EDA, circuit design, and physical design to create differentiated physical verification and extraction solutions that enable first-time-right product designs.

The role will have particular responsibility for Design Rule Checking (DRC), Layout Versus Schematic (LVS), and Parasitic Extraction (PEX) rule development, validation, release, and continuous improvement.   • Analyze and debug complex DRC, LVS, and PEX issues, identify root causes, and work with process, modeling, design, and EDA teams to resolve discrepancies between process intent and design-flow implementation.

  • Diseñar y acompañar técnicamente la implementación y monitoreo de programas de conservación y gestión integrada de recursos hídricos.
  • Desarrollar, administrar y aplicar modelos hidrológicos, hidro-sedimentológicos, de calidad de agua y evaluación de servicios ecosistémicos.
  • Realizar análisis espaciales avanzados y gestionar bases de datos geoespaciales e hidrometeorológicas asociadas a los proyectos del programa.
  • Liderar análisis técnicos especializados relacionados con hidrología, calidad de agua, sedimentos, cambio climático y seguridad hídrica.
  • Asesorar a equipos técnicos y programáticos de NASCA en temas especializados relacionados con hidrología, hidroinformática y gestión integrada del recurso hídrico.
  • Supervisar consultores, contratistas y alianzas técnicas relacionadas con los proyectos bajo su responsabilidad.
  • Generar información técnica, indicadores y métricas para el seguimiento de metas institucionales y plataformas corporativas como la Shared Conservation Agenda (SCA).

Sostenibilidad Financiera y Desarrollo de Negocios

  • Apoyar el diseño de propuestas técnicas y proyectos para la movilización de recursos.
  • Contribuir con enfoques innovadores de hidroinformática, seguridad hídrica y gestión de recursos hídricos en iniciativas estratégicas de NASCA.
  • Participar en la identificación de oportunidades de financiamiento y asociación técnica.

Gestión del Conocimiento y Representación Técnica

  • Elaborar informes, artículos, publicaciones científicas, manuales y otros productos técnicos.
  • Participar en eventos científicos y técnicos para divulgar resultados y lecciones aprendidas.
  • Representar técnicamente a NASCA ante socios, autoridades, academia y otros actores relevantes cuando sea requerido.
  • Facilitar procesos de transferencia de conocimiento y fortalecimiento de capacidades internas y externas.
  • Brindar apoyo a los integrantes del Grupo de Gestión Integrada de cuencas y recurso hídrico para comunicaciones a nivel técnico de detalle.
  • Acompañar al equipo directivo de NASCA o a otros equipos de trabajo en eventos o reuniones que requieran asesoramiento especializado en los temas de su trabajo.
  • undefined

CUALIFICACIONES MÍNIMAS

  • Profesional en ingeniería, ciencias ambientales, ciencias de la tierra, geografía, recursos hídricos, hidrología, matemática aplicada o disciplinas afines.
  • Mínimo cinco (5) años de experiencia profesional relevante o combinación equivalente de experiencia y formación académica.
  • Conocimiento y experiencia en análisis y modelación de hidrología superficial, recursos hídricos, hidrometeorología, hidráulica fluvial y manejo integrado de cuencas.
  • Experiencia en programación científica utilizando herramientas como Python, R, MATLAB o equivalentes.
  • Experiencia en diseño y desarrollo de herramientas informáticas, aplicaciones analíticas o sistemas de apoyo a la toma de decisiones.
  • Conocimiento en administración de código y control de versiones (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket o similares).
  • Experiencia en gestión de bases de datos relacionales y espaciales (PostgreSQL, PostGIS o equivalentes).
  • Experiencia en sistemas de información geográfica y análisis espacial.
  • Experiencia en elaboración de informes técnicos y científicos.
  • Capacidad para trabajar de manera autónoma, gestionar múltiples prioridades y cumplir plazos establecidos.

CONOCIMIENTOS, HABILIDADES Y EXPERIENCIA DESEADAS

  • Especialización o maestría en Hidroinformática, Hidrología, Hidráulica, Hidrosistemas, Recursos Hídricos o disciplinas afines.
  • Conocimientos avanzados de modelación hidrológica, hidro-sedimentológica, calidad de agua, morfología fluvial y evaluación de impactos del cambio climático.
  • Experiencia en herramientas de modelación como HEC-HMS, HEC-RAS, SWAT, WEAP, InVEST, RIOS, Qual2K, WASP o equivalentes.
  • Experiencia en diseño e implementación de programas de monitoreo hidrológico y de ecosistemas de agua dulce.
  • Experiencia en desarrollo de software, automatización de procesos analíticos y construcción de tableros de visualización.
  • Conocimiento de servicios ecosistémicos relacionados con el agua, seguridad hídrica, resiliencia climática y soluciones basadas en la naturaleza.
  • Experiencia en gestión y supervisión de contratos, consultorías y proyectos multidisciplinarios.
  • Experiencia trabajando con instituciones públicas, organizaciones no gubernamentales, academia o agencias de cooperación.
  • Capacidad de trabajo en campo durante períodos prolongados y disponibilidad para viajar dentro y fuera del país.
  • Deseable nivel intermedio o avanzado de inglés técnico y científico.
  • undefined

En TNC promovemos la igualdad de oportunidades y alentamos la postulación de personas con discapacidad. Si requiere ajustes razonables durante el proceso de selección, por favor indíquelo para brindarle el apoyo necesario.

Esta posición está sujeta a la confirmación de proyectos y fuentes de financiación actualmente en proceso avanzado de estructuración y aprobación

Grade: 6

Locatión: Bogotá

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring:

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers competitive and comprehensive benefits packages tailored to the individual countries where we work. These may include health care benefits, retirement benefits, parental leave, paid time off, life insurance, and disability coverage as well as an employee assistance program and other life and well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer.Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

jobs.description:
About SNV Proximate
What if you could combine the commercial rigour of consulting, investment, or corporate strategy with the opportunity to create meaningful development impact at scale? SNV’s newly established impact capital accelerator aims to do exactly that: develop commercially viable solutions that generate both business value and development impact. Combining expertise in impact-driven finance and inclusive commercial value chains, SNV Proximate will operate with the pace, ambition, and commercial mindset of a boutique advisory firm while leveraging the reach, credibility, and market presence of a global development organisation.

Working with companies, investors, development finance institutions, foundations, and governments, this is your chance to join the team that will design, test, and grow new approaches to mobilising investment, strengthening markets, and building more inclusive and resilient value chains across emerging economies. It is a place for people who are excited by building something new, comfortable operating across both commercial and development environments, and motivated by turning ambitious ideas into scalable results.

Position overview
SNV is building a commercial markets accelerator, which runs client engagements across two streams — impact-driven finance (IDF) and inclusive commercial value chains (ICVC). Associates are the delivery backbone of both. This role sits at the intersection of substantive client work and internal knowledge building — you will contribute to billable engagements, work directly with clients in the field and in meetings, and help build the evidence base that sharpens the offer over time.

This is an early-career role designed for someone with 3–5 years of experience who has done solid analytical work and is ready to take on more client-facing responsibility. You will work across both IDF and ICVC engagements, mentored by stream leads, with the expectation that you develop a meaningful specialism in one stream over time.

The Accelerator is small and the work is varied. In any given month you might be building a financial model for an impact fund client, conducting field interviews with smallholder farmers, drafting a chapter of a market systems report, or packaging an internal case study for BD use. You will not be siloed.

Who you are
You are a motivated, curious, and analytical professional who enjoys tackling complex challenges and turning insights into action. You combine strong analytical skills with sound judgement, including knowing when to use AI and when a more human-centred approach is needed.

You thrive in fast-paced environments and enjoy working across different workstreams rather than specialising in a single sector or vertical. Adaptable and commercially minded, you are excited by opportunities to create both business value and development impact.

As an Associate, you contribute to both winning and delivering client mandates through high-quality analysis, research, stakeholder engagement, and problem-solving. You structure complex problems effectively, identify the key insights and implications, and translate mandates into practical recommendations and deliverables. Your work is accurate, well-reasoned, and thoroughly checked, requiring minimal rework and giving managers confidence in your output.

You act on feedback quickly, keep stakeholders informed, meet deadlines, and proactively flag risks or challenges. Over time, you take on increasingly complex assignments, require less guidance, and build a reputation as a trusted colleague whose expertise and collaboration make clients and peers eager to work with you again.

Key Responsibilities

Client engagement delivery

  • Contribute substantively to client engagements as a core delivery resource — research, analysis, data collection, and drafting, to a standard that requires minimal rework by the delivery lead.
  • Conduct primary research: stakeholder interviews, field visits, surveys, and focus groups. Travel to project geographies is a standard part of this role.
  • Synthesise secondary research: literature reviews, market assessments, policy analysis, and competitor landscape reviews.
  • Build and maintain financial models, data trackers, and analytical frameworks to the level required by the engagement.
  • Draft sections of client reports, slide decks, and working papers — presenting findings clearly and at a level of quality appropriate for external audiences.
  • Participate in client meetings and workshops where appropriate — presenting analysis, facilitating sessions, and taking structured notes.

Stream-specific work

  • Associates are generalists across both streams, with the expectation of developing a specialism in one. The lists below illustrates what the work looks like in each stream.
  • IDF stream tasks
    • Landscape analysis of impact investment opportunities in a specific sector or geography.
    • Financial modelling for blended finance structures — grant/concessional capital ratios, return scenarios, investor waterfall analysis.
    • Due diligence research on investees or TA recipients — financial performance, impact track record, operational capacity.
    • Impact indicator development and data collection for investor reporting (IRIS+, IMP frameworks).
    • Market sizing and pipeline development analysis for fund managers or DFIs.
    • Synthesis of portfolio-level impact data across multiple investees into consolidated investor reports.
  • ICVC stream tasks
    • Value chain mapping and diagnostic analysis — identifying bottlenecks, margin distribution, and inclusion gaps.
    • Smallholder farmer interviews and household-level data collection and analysis.
    • Market systems analysis — mapping actors, incentives, and constraints across a commodity or sector.
    • Business case development for inclusive sourcing or supply chain investment, including financial modelling.
    • Competitive landscape reviews for agribusiness clients entering new markets or commodities.
    • Supplier development programme design — segmentation, needs assessment, and service delivery modelling.
    • Policy and regulatory environment analysis for government advisory engagements.

Internal knowledge and BD support

  • Contribute to the internal knowledge base — producing case studies, evidence summaries, and sector briefs from completed engagements. This feeds directly into the sales collateral and proposal infrastructure. Work produced here has a commercial use, not just an archival one.
  • Support the Senior Manager for Impact and Intelligence with cross-portfolio data collection and analysis.
  • Contribute to BD collateral where relevant: sector evidence packs, market data, and proof points for pitch materials.
  • Support proposal development with research, data, and analysis sections — not writing the proposal, but providing the evidence infrastructure. Proposal support is a regular part of this role, not an occasional one. The unit cannot win work without strong analytical inputs to bids.

What you bring

To be considered for this role, you bring:

  • 3–5 years of experience in research, analytical, or advisory role — in consulting, development finance, agribusiness, international development, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience producing high-quality analytical outputs that were used in client-facing or decision-making contexts.
  • Experience conducting primary research — interviews, surveys, or field data collection — in emerging market or development contexts.
  • Some exposure to either IDF or ICVC subject matter: impact investing, blended finance, value chain development, agribusiness, or market systems.
  • Experience working across multiple projects or workstreams simultaneously.

Additionally, we value:

  • Strong analytical skills — quantitative and qualitative. Comfortable building financial models and analysing large datasets as well as synthesising interview findings and qualitative evidence.
  • Clear, concise written English to publication standard. You can write a crisp executive summary, a well-structured analytical section, and a compelling slide — and they do not all sound the same.
  • Proficiency with Excel and PowerPoint at a working level. Experience with data analysis tools (R, Python, Stata, or equivalent) an advantage.
  • Intellectual curiosity about the sectors we work in. You read beyond the brief.
  • English required. French or Portuguese a strong advantage.
  • Reporting line: Director
  • Location: Flexible.We welcome applications from candidates based anywhere within the time zones spanning Ghana to Singapore. As this role involves international collaboration and travel, candidates should be located within reasonable reach of a well-connected international airport.
  • Travel requirements: International travel will be required.
  • Expected start date: November/December 2026

What we offer
We offer a unique opportunity to help build and shape a new venture from the ground up, working alongside a diverse and experienced global team. You will have significant autonomy, exposure to senior leaders and clients, and the opportunity to influence how the Accelerator grows and operates.
We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, with compensation determined based on relevant experience, skills, and internal equity.

Contract arrangements
As a globally flexible role, employment arrangements will be aligned with the successful candidate's location and applicable local regulations. Further details will be discussed with shortlisted candidates during the recruitment process.

Working at SNV
At SNV we challenge and inspire and offer continuous growth. We offer meaningful opportunities to shape the future, expand your skills, and collaborate with a vibrant, global network of experts. At SNV your contribution matter, and your development is our priority.

We are home to 57 cultures working in 22 countries, with about 95% of our team members holding the nationality of the respective countries we work in. We promote international career development. Our workforce consists of a mix of both people with longstanding tenure, willing to share their institutional knowledge, as well as people with local expertise and knowledge. All with an inquisitive view and united in ‘ONE SNV’ working towards our purpose.

Together, we are committed to the effective and efficient stewardship of resources and maximising positive, lasting impacts. Our ability to deliver results rests on our robust foundation of experience, technical knowledge, evidence and learning; our commitment to strengthening capacities and catalysing partnerships; and the relationships and trust of those we work alongside.

SNV is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment and make recruitment decisions based on merit, competence, and organisational needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, nationality, marital status, or any other status protected by applicable law. Women, persons with disabilities, and candidates from under-represented backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.

How to apply
If you meet the key requirements and feel inspired by this opportunity, we warmly welcome your application. Please submit your CV and motivation letter by 15th of November 2026 via SmartRecruiters.

To ensure a focused and respectful recruitment process, we kindly ask that you apply only if you meet the essential qualifications and are available to work in the specified location.
Please note that only candidates progressing to the next stage of the selection process will be contacted. Individual feedback cannot be provided.

If this role isn’t the right fit but you’re interested in joining SNV in the future, we invite you to follow us on LinkedIn and our career page Vacancies | SNV to stay updated on new opportunities that match your profile.

Reference and vetting check
At SNV, our belief in the CARE principles — Commitment to impact, Adaptive to Context, Respecting Difference and Expertise in Practice — shapes how we work with each other and every interaction we have with our colleagues, partners, and the communities we serve. These values guide how we welcome new team members, ensuring our workplace remains a place of trust, safety, and dignity for all.

As part of our commitment to a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace, we carry out reference and background checks for all determined positions, with particular attention to safeguarding. You will be invited to provide the contact details of [two] referees, and we will only approach them once you have given your permission. We handle this process with care, empathy, and strict confidentiality, using the information solely for purposes related to your application and the role you have applied for.

SNV is committed to safeguarding and to protecting children and adults from all forms of harm, with zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, harassment, or any other form of misconduct. As part of creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive working environment, all staff, consultants, and partners are expected to uphold SNV’s safeguarding, child protection, ethical standards, and CARE principles. In line with these commitments — and as a participant in the Inter‑Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS) — SNV will request a Statement of Conduct from your previous employer(s), covering any substantiated findings of misconduct, to ensure a recruitment process that safeguards and protect the communities we serve.
